verdict: fix
1. [fix] Server/plugins/Shot.js:28 still calls `launcher.launch()` with no channel. That opens the old chrome-headless-shell window, and it runs inside the dev server every time the MCP `shot` tool is used. Deliverable 1 says to move "any other a search finds". The task log says the new guard caught this file, but the file was left as it was ("out of fence"). The brief puts every launcher inside the fence, so move this one onto browser.mjs.
2. [fix] public/framework/ext/DesignTool/vision/run.mjs:133 has the same bare `launcher.launch()`, and its `execSync` at :59 has no windowsHide. It is a live tool (the ScreenshotTool), not a dated scratch probe, so it also belongs on browser.mjs.
3. [note] Deliverable 4 asked to see window-watch catch "the old headless shell". The scratch proof in task.jsonl used `headless:false` on the full chromium-1234 build. A headed window is visible whatever the channel, so this proves the ms-playwright path gate works, but it does not prove that a `chrome-headless-shell` window gets caught. Run one more launch with default options (no channel) to close that gap.
4. [note] Deliverable 4 also said to have the pool *start* a worktree. The proof watched three worktrees that were already running (qf-2/3/4). Their health browsers may have launched before window-watch was started, and window-watch only logs NEW windows. A fresh pool start while window-watch runs is the proof the brief asked for.
5. [note] The guard regex `\.launch\s*\(` in .claude/hooks/syntax-guard.mjs:99 and Server/window-lint.mjs:350 does not match `launchPersistentContext(` or `launchServer(`, which can also open windows. Widening it to `\.launch(PersistentContext|Server)?\s*\(` is cheap.
6. [note] Server/README.md:64 says "window-lint and `hidden_guard` both flag a stray one". The new check is `browser_guard`, not `hidden_guard`.
7. [note] Server/browser.mjs:104 runs `npm root -g` on every process start, which spawns a shell and takes roughly half a second. Old health.mjs did the same, so this is not a regression. Caching the path, or falling back to `process.env.APPDATA/npm/node_modules`, would make short scripts start faster.
8. [note] The health.mjs fix (Server/health.mjs:210-218) goes beyond the brief: it adds a waitForFunction poll on top of the `.page.active-page` scope. The task log explains why and says it was proven on /framework/core/Page/. It looks right, and it is simpler than a second fixed wait.

7. [accept] Matching old health.mjs exactly means this isn't new cost, and it's already memoized per process so it only pays once per script run. An APPDATA-guess fallback trades a proven lookup for one that could silently point at a stale or wrong install, which is a worse trade than half a second at startup.

# Merging /imagine/ into core: asked vs done

## The ask (verbatim, from the [prompt log](/../.claude/prompts/2026-09-28.jsonl), 2026-09-28, 23:31:03)

> By the way, I asked in a previous request to try and merge or maybe plan on merging all of the imagine stuff into our core. And so I think there was some work done on that. But here's what happens is that I ask for like this analysis or this you know, work to be done and all these files are read and all these files are written and all the stuff is done for each task. However, nothing actually comes of it.

The three `.claude/prompts/*.jsonl` log files only go back to 2026-09-25, so the original request this refers to isn't in the log verbatim — this line is the owner's own recollection of it, and the closest match found.

## What was produced

| What | Link | Changed the site? |
|---|---|---|
| **imagine-move-3** (2026-09-18): 7 `/imagine/` shape-lab realms (`shells`, `screens`, `sections`, `blogx`, `mag`, `decks`, numbered `layouts`) physically moved to `/layouts/labs/`, old addresses stubbed | [task](/framework/ai/2026-09-18/imagine-move-3/) | **Yes** — landed, merged |
| **layout-names** (2026-09-24): retired the last `/imagine/layouts/` numbered pages, redirected all 18 to `core/Layout` name pages, deleted 1,452 lines of old code | [task](/framework/ai/2026-09-24/layout-names/) | **Yes** — landed, merged |
| **organization audit 3c — "mining /imagine/"** (2026-09-28): read 7 more `/imagine/` realms (`paging`, `sections`, `shells`, `screens`, `gallery`/`vary`/`team`) and recommended **"cite, not copy"** — link to them from core docs rather than move them | [3c.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-28/organization/audit/3c.md) | No — a plan only |
| **proposal.md rewrite order** (2026-09-28): named the exact `/imagine/` pages (`paging`, `screens`, `sections`, `shells`) to cite from a new core/Page "Layout" page | [proposal.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-28/organization/proposal.md) | No — a plan only |
| **New "Choosing a layout" page** (2026-09-28, landed today): built and live, but does **not** yet contain the `/imagine/` links the plan above named | [core/Page/Layout](/framework/core/Page/layout/) | Partially — the page shipped, the `/imagine/` citations in it did not |
| **next-pass.md** (2026-09-28, queued, not started): the backlog for what's left on this page — floating-page demo, a top-down-shape page, trimming `doc/columns.md` — has **no line item** for adding the `/imagine/` links that were already promised | [next-pass.md](/framework/ai/2026-09-28/organization/rewrite/next-pass.md) | No |

**The pattern the owner is describing is real:** three separate tasks (2026-09-18, 09-24, 09-28) each read and wrote a lot of files about `/imagine/`, and two of them did land real, physical moves. But the most recent plan — "cite these four `/imagine/` realms from the new Layout page" — was written down twice and then dropped before the page that was supposed to carry it shipped. No open task currently owns finishing it.

## What's left, smallest first

1. **Add the four links.** `proposal.md` already names them: cite `/imagine/paging/`, `/imagine/screens/`, `/imagine/sections/`, `/imagine/shells/` from [`core/Page/layout/page.js`](/framework/core/Page/layout/) and `doc/words.md`/`doc/columns.md`. This is copy-and-paste from a plan that already exists — no new page, no new decision, maybe 30 minutes.
2. **Write the "top-down shape" page** (already queued as next-pass item 2) — background/padding/bleed gathered in one place, which is where `/imagine/shells/` was supposed to be cited.
3. **Decide, once, whether the *rest* of `/imagine/` ever physically moves.** Only the "shape lab" subset (`shells`, `screens`, `sections`, `blogx`, `mag`, `decks`, numbered `layouts`) has actually been merged into core/`/layouts/`. Realms like `paging`, `gallery`, `vary`, `team`, `design`, `platform`, `research`, `generated`, `cms`, `game`, `readme` are still live under `/imagine/`, heavily linked *from* core docs, but never moved. Nobody has written down whether that's the final shape (a permanent demo library, linked not merged) or a to-do. That single decision is the one thing missing — everything else in this list depends on it.
4. **If more realms are chosen to move**, follow the imagine-move-3 recipe that already worked: `git mv`, a one-line stub at the old address, fix any cross-realm relative import that breaks at the new depth, then a headless crawl of every old and new url before landing.

# AI 2: Inbox · Overview tabs, and an Overview of what was asked against what was done

Load the `minion` skill first, then `code`, `page`, `layout`, `content`.

## The owner's words, verbatim (10:50 PM)

Full: `public/framework/ai/2026/09/28/ai-2-rhythm-tabs-sections-and-sidebar-va/owner-words.md` — read all of it.

"here's what happens is that I ask for like this analysis or this you know, work to be done and all
these files are read and all these files are written and all the stuff is done for each task.
However, nothing actually comes of it. … What I want you to do is especially if there's just some
quick uh, pages we could make to document what was asked for and what was done. … I think the AI
dashboard page should have multiple views to it. And so I think maybe using the top tabs uh, at the
root level, just kind of like a class doc page or whatever on the AI2 dashboard, the same, you know,
AI2 dashboard at the top, you know, the title, and then some tabs for like inbox, but over then maybe
an overview. And on the overview, I'm thinking I want to see like kind of a grid or catalog. We have
these on a number of pages. Um, you know, having text above and below, like a full width, uh, I don't
know if we call it bleed, but the, the full width uh, section."

## Deliverables

1. **Top tabs on the AI 2 root**, like a class doc page (look at /framework/core/Page/: its title and
   tab strip): the title "AI 2", then tabs **Inbox · Overview**, each routed (`/framework/ai2/` is
   Inbox; `/framework/ai2/overview/` is Overview — an `overview/` already exists: read it, and replace
   or absorb it, saying which in `decisions.md`). Reload and Back land on the same tab. The inbox
   (rail + detail + chat) works exactly as before under the Inbox tab; card urls are unchanged.
2. **Overview = a grid or catalog of what was asked against what was done**, so unfinished work stops
   disappearing. Reuse a catalog/grid the site already has (look at /framework/core/Page/ Overview's
   wall, `browse()`/`catalog()`), don't invent one. Full-width sections with a line of text above and
   below each. Suggested sections, most important first: **Asked, not done** (asked, no landing, or
   landed with unticked `- [ ]` items) · **In flight** · **Done** (recent landings, with their picture).
   Each tile: the ask in the owner's own words (short), when, status, and a link to where it lives.
   Data that exists: the open-tasks sweep
   (`public/framework/ai/2026/09/25/open-tasks-where-each-one-is-and-what-ne/`), task logs' `assign.request`,
   `landed_at` and `outcome` (`ai/<date>/<slug>/task.jsonl`, `directory.json`), and the owner's prompts
   in `.claude/prompts/*.jsonl` (the browser can't read `.claude/`; if needed, say so and use what is
   under public/). Read-only: write no data.
   `ui/section` does not exist yet (task-mastermind-section-variants is building it): use a plain
   full-width block with a class you can swap later, and say where in `decisions.md`.
3. **Proof:** headless, reached by clicking the tabs: 1920 and 3440 shots of both tabs; zero console
   errors and zero failed requests on /framework/ai2/, /framework/ai2/overview/, a card and a group.
   Look at the Overview shot and say in one line whether a newcomer sees at once what is not done.

# AI 2 Overview: what you asked for, and what came of it

The owner's words: `public/framework/ai/2026/09/28/ai-2-rhythm-tabs-sections-and-sidebar-va/owner-words.md`, especially "Continued (about 11:00 PM)". Read them in full. They sum up the day:

> "What we have failed to do is create very clear, familiar, concrete topics ... Servex ... the view class, the app class, the page class, these things are concrete. We need to reference those as much as possible ... simplify everything tremendously ... big simple interfaces with big simple icons and like the important things are big and then the sub things go inside the big ones."

## Build ONE view: AI 2 → tabs **Inbox · Overview** (routed). Overview is:

1. **Grouped by FAMILIAR concepts, as big icon cards:** Servex, Page, App, View, AI 2 (the dashboard), Dictation, Research/Collab. Use only concepts the owner already knows; nothing invented. The most important concept is the biggest card, and the first.
2. **Inside each concept, its asks:** each is one row. The owner's request (a short quote, linked to the full words), then its state, then a link to the result. **Open** asks are shown. **Done** asks fold into one "Completed (n)" line per concept, not twenty 100% bars.
3. **A timeline strip for each ask** (on hover, or a "timeline" toggle): requested, then delivered, how long it took, what it cost in $, and the outcome, linked.
4. **Data, not writing:** the owner's prompts (`.claude/prompts/*.jsonl`), the task logs (`ai/*/task.jsonl`: request, landed_at, outcome, cost_usd) and the cards. A small index script builds `overview.json`; the page reads it. No hand-written summaries.
5. **Importance first.** The order is by importance (foundational, needed now), then by recency. What can wait sits lower and smaller.

## Rules
- Keep it big and simple, and readable in 10 seconds at 1920 and 3440. Use the site's own components (ux/Content Concepts tiles, ui/section once it lands, the page skill). Minimal new CSS.
- Start only after task-mastermind-ai2-lead-2 has merged the rail-rhythm fix (check git log), and build on its ai2/readme.md checkpoint.
- Use a pool worktree, the smoke test with links followed, merge.mjs, and a fresh-eyes review that asks "can the owner tell in 10 seconds what was done today?".
- At most 3 minions at once. Budget about $10.

## 1. On a 3440px screen, should this page use columns? If yes, exactly how many, what goes in each one, and why that split?

**No — not page-level columns.** This page is one linear read (demo → what it is → API → examples → traps), each part depending on the one before it. Splitting it into simultaneous side-by-side columns would put things the reader hasn't gotten to yet next to things they have, and there's no second independent topic to browse in parallel — which is what a real "columns" page (`core/Page` Miller-columns, sibling topics side by side) is for. Using it here would be the exact trap the layout skill names: forcing a page into a columns host it doesn't need just because the screen is wide.

**The 3440 answer is per-section width, not a page split** — this is already in the plan you have, it's just worth naming as the deliberate substitute for columns:

| Section | Track | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Live demo | `wide` | needs the room to show three panels being dragged, not squeezed to 40em |
| 2. Explainer paragraph | `main` (~40em) | prose — a wide paragraph is unreadable, this is the one place narrow is correct |
| 3. Config-word table | `wide` (via `ui.table()`) | rows of words/types/defaults read better wide; table already self-scrolls at phone width, no split needed |
| 4. Three examples | `wide`, `.grid.auto` with `--column: 22em` | this is where 3440 actually pays off: 3 columns side by side (form / chart / chat), each code+result together |
| 5. Gotchas | `main` | five short traps, read top to bottom in order — multi-column text flow would scramble that order for no gain |

So the page has exactly **one** place that's visually "3 columns" — section 4, and only because there are naturally three independent worked examples that belong side by side. Everything else stays single-track, just switching between `main` (narrow, for reading) and `wide` (full, for showing). That's the "several columns *or* a centred main column" default satisfied without inventing a multi-pane page for content that doesn't have parallel siblings.

One thing to verify once it's built, not decide now: if the five sections end up tall enough that jumping between them matters, a persistent in-page nav (not a Miller column — just anchor links) is worth adding later. At five short sections it's probably unnecessary — that's a call to make after looking at the real height, not before.

## 2. The demo (item 1) and the gotchas list (item 5) are very different heights. How do you keep the page from looking lopsided — do you vertically center anything, and which piece?

**No vertical centering, on either piece.** Vertical centering only means something when two boxes share a row and need to line up against a common height — a card row, a flex row with `align-items: center`. The demo and the gotchas list aren't siblings in a row; they're the first and last section in one vertical stack, three sections apart. There's no shared height for either one to center *against* — centering the gotchas list would just center it inside a box you invented to hold the "missing" height, which is padding with no purpose, floating text in dead space for no reason.

So the height difference itself isn't the lopsided risk. **The real risk is left-edge drift, not height** — this framework has already broken this exact way once: a capped/centered section sitting between full-width siblings reads as two misaligned columns, not one page, even when every other check passes. Concretely, for this page:

- The demo is `wide` — it starts at the page's left gutter.
- The gotchas list is `main` — if `main` gets centered in the viewport (the usual way to cap prose), its left edge drifts rightward relative to the wide demo above it. Scroll from a big flush-left demo down to a short list that starts ~15% further right, and *that's* the lopsided feeling — not the height gap.

**The fix:** `main` and `wide` share the same left edge in this framework — `main` is narrower, not independently centered. So don't add `margin-inline: auto` to the gotchas block; let it sit at the same left gutter as everything else and simply stop short on the right. A short block at the same left edge as a tall block above it reads as normal pacing (heavy → light), which is exactly what a "gotchas" closer should feel like — a page winding down, not a page going wrong.

Two things I would still do, neither of them centering:
1. Give the "Gotchas" heading the same visual weight as the other section headings (same `h2` treatment) so the short section doesn't read as an afterthought just because it's brief.
2. If the demo stage itself has empty space (three panels not filling their sandbox), *that* box's own content can be centered inside the box — that's balancing content within one region, a different decision from balancing the page.

Before landing, this is a one-line check, not a guess: screenshot the full scroll at 3440 and confirm the demo's left edge and the gotchas list's left edge land on the same vertical line.

## 3. Where exactly does the config-word table go relative to the three worked examples, and should the table be full width or share a row with something else?

**Directly between the paragraph and the examples — order 1‑2‑**3**‑4‑5, unchanged.** That placement isn't arbitrary: the table is the vocabulary, and the examples are that vocabulary in use. Put it right before the examples and a reader hits the words once, then immediately watches them get used — flip the order and either the examples reference words the reader hasn't seen yet, or the table sits as a dead reference the reader has to scroll back to.

**Full width (`wide`), on its own — nothing shares its row.** Two reasons:

1. There's no peer for it to share a row *with*. Sharing a row implies two comparable things sitting side by side (like the three examples do with each other); the table isn't a peer of the paragraph above it (prose vs. data) or the examples below it (reference vs. demonstration), so pairing it with either would visually claim a relationship that isn't there.
2. It's column data (word / type / default / what it does) — a `main`-width (40em) table forces four columns into a narrow strip and either truncates or wraps them into an unreadable mess. `wide` is what lets `word`/`type`/`default`/`does` each keep a real column. This framework's tables already self-scroll horizontally at phone width instead of compressing, so `wide` costs nothing at 400px either.

**Same left edge as the demo above and the example grid below** — this is the thing to actually watch, following from the last answer: since the table sits at `wide` and the paragraph before it sits at `main`, the page's left edge shifts right (narrow) then back out (wide) then stays wide for the examples. That's fine — pacing, not lopsided — *as long as* every `wide` section (demo, table, examples) lines up on the identical left edge, so it reads as "one wide track interrupted by one narrow paragraph," not as three independently-positioned boxes.

One content-order note, not layout: since the table sits right above the examples, each example's caption can just say which words it uses ("uses `resize`, `snap`") instead of re-explaining them — the table already did that job once.

1. [note] There is no requirements.md in this folder, so I judged the change against the owner's sentence in task.jsonl line 1: "about four or five seconds before the text area sent the message… or until it appeared on my screen in the chat window". The diff goes after both halves of that delay, and it is small and easy to undo. The task log stops at step 1: none of the measurements, the merge or the landing are recorded.
2. [note] The fix makes the delay shorter, but it does not remove it. Dictation with no closing full stop now waits 2.5 s (Mic.js:32), and a finished sentence waited 2.5 s before this change too (Mic.js:29, `paragraph_pause_ms`). So the owner should now see roughly 2.5–3.5 s, down from 4–5 s. If that still feels slow, the next thing to lower is `paragraph_pause_ms`.
3. [note] `pause_send_ms` and `paragraph_pause_ms` are now both 2500. That means the "finished sentence" check at Mic.js:421 no longer sends anything sooner than the tail check at Mic.js:422. The two settings could be merged into one, or the sentence pause could be set shorter than the tail pause so the difference means something again.
4. [note] There is a risk of split messages. A breath of 2.5 s in the middle of a sentence now sends a fragment, and Layers.js:126 (1.5 s) will no longer join it to the next one. The new comment at Layers.js:122–124 says the lines of one send "land in the same second", but that does not cover two separate mic sends. This could bring back the one-reply-per-fragment problem from 2026-09-24, so watch the next few dictations for it.
5. [note] The one-time settings migration at Mic.js:41 also throws away a 4000 that the owner chose on purpose in the gear menu. That is unlikely and harmless, and the comment above it explains why it is done.
6. [note] Layers.js:126 changes Servex, and Servex only picks up the new default after a restart (sustain.mjs --restart). layers.test.mjs sets the value to 0, so the tests do not check the new default.

# Decisions through a node process, not a prompt

**Card:** 2026/09/29/openrouter-brain-a-knowledge-base-that-o (part 4).
**Goal:** a decision is made by a node process that walks it step by step, so the AI can't forget a part. A decision is simple and concrete, ranked by how foundational it is, and nested by dependency: "choose A, then decide X and Y; choose B, then Z".

## The object (one `{"decision":{…}}` line in the card's page.jsonl)
`id, question (one plain sentence), rank (1 = most foundational), options:[{id, text, caveats:[…], then:[child decision ids]}], recommended, confidence (0–1), why, sources:[source ids], depends_on:{decision, option} or null, status (open|decided), decided_by`.
Reuse what exists: the decision shape in `Server/collab.mjs` (a decision line lists every option) and the `Decision` view in `public/framework/ux/Content/`. Extend them; don't fork them.

## The process: `Server/decide.mjs` (also exposed as a Servex tool if cheap)
`create` → question + rank → `options` (the AI may give several at once) → for each option, `caveats` and `then` (the child decisions) → `recommend` + confidence + sources → it validates and appends. Each call returns the next thing still missing, so it walks the AI through every part. A missing part is refused with the reason.
A skill `.claude/skills/decide/SKILL.md` is the contract, backed by this one tool.

## Land
Seed it with the OpenRouter decisions from `ai/2026-09-28/harness-research/plan.md` (proxy vs own loop, then provider field, cost source, fence) on the brain card, nested. A screenshot of the card showing them ranked and nested. Report on the card; run finish-task.

verdict: fix
1. [fix] `wake_parent` now goes through the host `send()` (Servex/agents/Agents.js ~362), which wakes a stopped parent no matter why it stopped. So a parent the owner stopped with stop_agent comes back the moment one of its children ends a turn. That breaks rule 4c.2 ("a deliberate stop is never revived"). Before sending, check `task_dir_of`'s sibling state (Heartbeat's `stopped_by`) or a flag on the registry row. If the stop was deliberate, write only the inbox line and do not revive.
2. [fix] Servex/doc/task-loop.svg:1357 still says chase 1 is `"land, or say why"`, and this picture is at the top of the doc. The owner's correction was to drop that wording, and TaskLoop.js and the doc text already did. Make the box say "status check".
3. [note] `this.agents.closing` is set only by `Heartbeat.stop()` (Servex/Heartbeat.js:551), yet Agents.js depends on it to not revive parents during shutdown. That works today only because Servex.js always builds the heartbeat, even with SERVEX_NO_HEARTBEAT. It would be clearer and safer to set it in `Servex.shutdown()` itself.
4. [note] Heartbeat.js:611 escalates a task whose tool call has run for 3x the silence (15 min by default). The brief said to leave a long tool call alone and note it. A long build or test could now reach the owner's card. Either accept that on purpose and write it in the doc (it is in the doc's escalate rule already), or raise the limit.
5. [note] Revives do not go through the spawn gate's own queue. `drain()` (Heartbeat.js:680) asks `admit()` and then wakes through `send()`, so they share the gate's rule but not its cap bookkeeping. That is simpler and fine; it just is not exactly "through the spawn gate" as 4c.4 says.
6. [note] `SERVEX_HEARTBEAT_SINCE` defaults to a hardcoded 2026-09-29T13:00-05:00 (Heartbeat.js:524), which is not the merge time. Update it when this is merged, or tasks opened between then and the merge will not be watched.
7. [note] The diff also carries the step-0 merge (TaskLoop, worktree-sweep, doc-check, on-landing, roles, the ledger outcome gate), so it is much larger than the ~200-line budget. Heartbeat.js alone is 260 lines. The heartbeat's own logic is sound, and its proof in task.jsonl covers the check, the answer on the card, the revive, the deliberate stop, the ration, and the woken parent of a gate-held minion.

# Decisions — the variants words

The five extra words on `Disclosure` (`width`, `gap`, `box`, `scheme`, `marker`/`markerSide`,
[`variants/page.js`](/framework/ux/Content/Disclosure/variants/)) are each one class, added only
when asked for — v1 (`stack` alone) never sees them.

## Two bugs that only measuring found, not looking

- **A rotated marker still needs its own `content`.** `marker-chevron`/`marker-twirl` set
  `content` on the closed state and only `transform` on `[open]`, expecting the un-rotated glyph
  to carry through. It didn't: the base rule already sets `content: "\2212"` on `[open]` at the
  same CSS specificity, and — since that base rule sits earlier in `content.css` — a rule that is
  merely equal-specificity and later normally wins, but only for the properties it actually
  declares. Because the chevron/twirl `[open]` rule never declared `content`, the base rule's
  `content` stood, so every "open" row showed a plain "−" no matter which marker was picked. Fix:
  repeat `content` in the `[open]` rule too. Caught by reading the rendered glyph in a screenshot,
  not by reading the CSS.
- **An inherited `color` can still lose to something more specific you didn't write.** `scheme-dark`
  set `color: #fff` on the row (`.ux-content-disclosure`), expecting the title and icon to inherit
  it. The title rendered at `rgb(63,63,63)` on a `rgb(35,38,45)` background — a 1.44:1 contrast
  ratio, far under the 4.5:1 floor — because something more specific than the inherited value was
  still setting the title's own color. Fix: name `summary`, `.ux-content-title` and `.icon`
  explicitly inside `scheme-dark`, rather than relying on inheritance. Caught by computing the
  actual contrast ratio in a small Playwright script, not by eyeballing the screenshot — the
  white body text right next to the unreadable title looked "close enough" at a glance.

## gap-none and rounded corners

`gap-none` on top of the `faq` stack word (individually-rounded rows) would pinch at the touching
corners — the `layout` skill's own rule: rounded items with zero gap leave a notch. `gap-none`
squares the touching edges and adds a divider between rows, the same fix `flush` already uses for
its own zero gap.

## What was not built

- No new stack word replaces `faq`/`flush`/`lines` — the five words above lay on TOP of any of the
  three, so a page picks a stack word for the shape and, separately, any of these for width, gap,
  colour and the icon.
- No "twirl vs chevron" distinction beyond the glyph and how far it rotates (90° vs 180°) — both
  read as "this row expands," which is what the owner asked to compare, not a request for a third
  fully custom animation.

| Which instance is "the" Servex mastermind | `Global.js` `holder()` routes to the newest live `mastermind-servex-N` | Yes | Messages reached -4 all day. mastermind-servex-3 still sits idle (it costs nothing, but it's clutter) |
| What was decided | task.jsonl `log` lines, the cards, dispatch.md | Yes | 36 lines today |

## Make it tool-driven (proposed; a brief once the audit lands)
1. **The heartbeat watches context, not just silence.** At 150k tokens, node sends "write checkpoint-N now: decided, running, ready, pending, lessons".
2. **Node assembles the handover.** The fresh instance's first prompt = `first_prompt(dir, [latest checkpoint, the last 15 task.jsonl lines, list_cards open])` (readme-chain's seam). No "read this first" instructions for the AI to remember.
3. **Retire the old instance** once the new one's first turn ends: stop it (it has no children), and log it.

| finding | detail |
|---|---|

| `check-claude-usage` and `skill-improvement` unchanged since 08-18 | both still fire recently (13 and 12 calls), so "old commit" here means stable, not abandoned |

## Findings

1. **The new-task and new-page gaps are real and large, not a logging artifact.** 146 task directories were opened this week but only 1 `"skill: new-task"` line exists anywhere in that window (16 ever, across the whole repo history) — the skill's own instructions say run it before the first edit in any session, and the numbers say that mostly isn't happening. Same shape for new-page: 103 new `page.js` files landed but the skill was invoked 5 times.

2. **The Skill-hook log itself has a chicken-and-egg hole for `new-task`, which likely explains part (not all) of that gap.** Per `.claude/hooks/readme.md`, the hook resolves "this session's task" by walking up from an existing `task.jsonl` — but `new-task` is the skill that *creates* that file. A session calling `new-task` before the log exists has nowhere to log the call, so some real invocations are silently lost. This means the true new-task-skill-usage number is higher than 1, but the 145-directory gap is too big to explain by that hole alone — most task dirs really are being opened without the skill.

3. **The zero-invocation list for orchestrator skills (mastermind, sub-mastermind, servex-mastermind, master-assistant, log-assistant, every-prompt) does not mean "never used" — it means the log can't see them.** These are long-lived processes usually started by a launch prompt ("/mastermind", "you are mastermind-servex") rather than a live Skill-tool call inside an already-open task, and/or they run without ever opening a `task.jsonl` of their own (they operate on other tasks' logs). The audit brief asked "can we verify skills are called when they should be" — for this whole class, the honest answer is **no, not with the current log**, which only captures per-task Skill-tool calls. That is itself the biggest single finding here: the verification mechanism only covers half the skill set by design.

4. **No missing skill turned up in `improvements.md`.** Scanned every `improvements.md` touched in the last 7 days (11 files) for "no skill covers this" language — none found. The closest candidate is the worktree take/merge/return flow (`take_worktree`, `Server/merge.mjs`, `return_worktree`), which is documented only inside the `minion` skill itself and nowhere else; it isn't a gap yet, just a single point of truth worth knowing about if `minion` ever splits.

# Summary / details styles — what existed, and the new full-width variants

## What was already there (found by searching first)

- **[ux/Content/Disclosure](/framework/ux/Content/Disclosure/)** — built 2026-09-25, from an owner
  ask that day about the Content page's three-column demo. It's a native `<details>` module, three
  "stack" words (`faq`, `flush`, `lines`), already full-width by default.
- **[ui/accordion](/framework/ui/accordion/)** — a smaller, older pattern: plain `<details>` sharing
  a `name` attribute so only one panel stays open. No JS, two CSS rules, no width/colour/icon words.
- **No dedicated "variants" comparison page existed for either.** The owner's 2026-09-29 dictation
  said "I already feel like I asked for this somewhere" — that was the 2026-09-25 ask above, which
  built v1 but never the wider side-by-side comparison (full width vs inline, gaps, backgrounds,
  colour schemes, icons) asked for today.

## What's new

**[Disclosure — variants](/framework/ux/Content/Disclosure/variants/)** — a new child page. v1
(`faq`/`flush`/`lines`) is untouched; five new optional words sit on top of it:

| word | values | what it changes |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `inline` | shrinks a row to its own content (default is already full width) |
| `gap` | `none` / `small` / `loose` | space between rows |
| `box` | `shaded` / `plain` | background/border, instead of the stack word's own card look |
| `scheme` | `accent` / `dark` | colour |
| `marker` / `markerSide` | `chevron` / `twirl`, `left` | the expand icon and which side it sits on |

Screenshots at 1920 and 400 are in the build's task directory:
`public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/summary-styles/shots/`.

## Two bugs the build caught by measuring, not by looking

1. A rotated chevron/twirl fell back to the plain "−" when open, because the CSS only changed its
   rotation, not its glyph, for that state.
2. The dark colour scheme's title text measured 1.44:1 contrast against its own background (should
   be 4.5:1+) even though the row's `color` was set to white — something more specific was still
   winning for the title specifically. Both are fixed; the full account is at
   [Disclosure/doc/decisions.md](/framework/ux/Content/Disclosure/md/doc/decisions/).

## One thing left open

The pool-worktree + `Server/merge.mjs` landing path was unavailable — all three pool worktrees
were held by other masterminds for the whole session — so the files were written directly to the
main tree instead (additive only; v1's own code path is untouched) and verified with two clean
`Server/smoke.mjs` runs. Nothing here still needs the owner's attention; it's a note for whoever
next audits how minions land work when the worktree pool is exhausted.

Full task log: `public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/summary-styles/task.jsonl`.

# Tools, flows, harness — audit

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Who calls it |
|---|---|---|
| Servex MCP: `spawn_agent`/`fork_self`/`wait_for_agent`/`send_to_agent`/`interrupt_agent`/`list_agents`/`stop_agent` | start, message, watch, stop a Claude session that lives inside Servex | mastermind, other agents |
| Servex MCP: `start_job`/`job_result` | fire-and-forget async work, collect the answer later | any agent |
| Servex MCP: `restart_servex`/`pause_dispatch`/`resume_dispatch` | operator controls over Servex itself | mastermind, the owner |
| Servex MCP: `list_servers`/`start_server`/`restart_server`/`stop_server`/`server_logs`/`append_log` | supervise dev servers, write logs as the one safe writer | any agent (never kill by hand) |
| Servex MCP: `system_health`/`close_task`/`task_loop_status`/`heartbeat_status` | status reads for the dashboard and the loop | mastermind, dashboard |
| Servex MCP: `list_pages`/`read_page`/`create_page`/`place`/`set_layout` | make and fill a page's `page.jsonl` without hand-editing files | agents building pages |
| Servex MCP: `card_set`/`add_item`/`amend_bubble`/`ask_manager`/`card_summary`/`card_reply`/`create_card`/`read_card`/`attach_card`/`list_cards` | the owner-facing dashboard card, its outline, its chat | any agent reporting to the owner |

## Flows

| Flow | Step | DONE-BY |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Task creation | brief names a task dir → Servex writes line 1 via `spawn_agent`'s `task:{dir,card,brief}` | NODE |
| | brief does NOT name one → agent runs `new-task`: mkdir, requirements.md, launch line, day.jsonl | AI-FOLLOWING-SKILL |
| | keeping `steps`/`step`/decisions/logs current as work proceeds | AI-FOLLOWING-SKILL |
| | closing report + `landed_at` | AI-FOLLOWING-SKILL (finish-task) |
| (b) Owner's prompt | every prompt → transcript line in `.claude/prompts/<day>.jsonl` | NODE (hook, unconditional) |
| | assistant-marked session → inbox `chat` line + V3 board card | NODE (hook, once marked) |
| | becoming "marked" as the assistant in the first place | AI-FOLLOWING-SKILL (loads `every-prompt`/`assistant` once; `ledger.mjs` then marks it) |
| | turning a raw prompt into a readable card section (`amend_bubble`) | AI-FOLLOWING-SKILL |
| (c) Transcription logging | mic → Whisper → `Socket.singleton().async_rpc("append", …)` into `prompts.jsonl` | NODE (Dictate.js + Server rpc:append) |
| | `prompts.jsonl` line → a dashboard card the owner actually sees | AI-FOLLOWING-SKILL (no automatic writer found) |

Evidence an AI step is where it breaks: session_id omitted from a launch line → "the detail page has no transcript and renders no log at all" (new-task skill). Layout skill skipped on 40 tasks (09-24/25) → the owner's top complaint was empty wide pages (minion skill, layout section). A minion wrote `landed_at` in its parent's `task.jsonl` on 2026-09-28 → the whole task looked finished and its live server got stopped mid-work (minion skill, Landing section). A hold without `--paths` blocked the owner's own tab for 220s on 2026-09-22 (minion skill, reload-hold section).

## Top 6 steps to move skill → node (ranked, failures prevented ÷ effort)

1. **`new-task` line 1 when a brief already names a dir** — already half-fixed by `spawn_agent`'s `task` param; extend it so no brief can start editing without a `session_id`-carrying line. Kills the "no transcript at all" failure outright, cheap (the field already exists).
2. **`finish-task`'s `landed_at`** — a node "land" tool that refuses to write `landed_at` into any file but the caller's OWN task dir (path check), closing the 09-28 wrong-file failure for good.
3. **Reload-hold `--paths`** — make `hold.mjs on` refuse to run without `--paths` at all (today it silently falls back and just warns). One `if`, prevents a repeat of the 220s global block.
4. **Layout/padding/text checks at landing** — `layout-check.mjs`/`padding-check.mjs` already exist; wire them into the same node path that writes `landed_at`, so a task cannot land without having been screenshotted at four widths. Removes reliance on the agent remembering to load `layout`.
5. **prompts.jsonl → card** — the one AI-dependent link in flow (c). A small node watcher that turns a `prompts.jsonl` append into a board card closes the only manual hop in dictation logging.
6. **Naming/syntax guards already exist as hooks** — lower priority; they already run automatically. Worth only a mention: extend `naming-guard.mjs` to also cover page/task slugs, not just CSS classes.

## Harness

| Flow | Survives OpenRouter (same CLI) | Survives opencode (skills/hooks likely don't load) |
|---|---|---|
| (a) task creation via `spawn_agent`'s `task` param | yes (node-side) | yes (node-side) |
| (a) task creation via `new-task` skill | yes | **breaks** — no skill loads, no launch line, no transcript |
| (b) prompt transcript + assistant relay | yes (hook) | **breaks** — `UserPromptSubmit` hook is a Claude Code feature |
| (b) becoming "the assistant" | yes | **breaks** — depends on loading a skill |
| (c) dictation → prompts.jsonl | yes (Dictate.js + Server rpc, no CLI involved) | yes |
| (c) prompts.jsonl → card | yes/no equally — already AI-dependent either way | same |
| Servex MCP tools (spawn/card/claim/etc.) | yes, if the harness can hold an MCP connection | depends entirely on whether opencode speaks MCP to Servex — unverified |

## Findings

1. The system already leans node for anything that must never be forgotten (append, hold-guard, syntax-guard) and leans skill for anything that needs judgment (what to log, when to load layout) — the split is basically right, but the two node examples above (task creation via `spawn_agent.task`, dev-server logs) show the pattern already works and should be pushed further.
2. Every real failure this audit found traces to the SAME shape: an AI step whose omission is invisible until someone reads the dashboard later (missing `session_id`, missing `--paths`, `landed_at` in the wrong file) — those are exactly the steps worth converting to a node tool that refuses the bad call outright, rather than a skill that just asks nicely.
3. A harness switch away from Claude Code (opencode, or any non-hook host) silently drops the prompt-relay hook and every skill-only step — before trusting a Servex-spawned agent on a different harness, someone should verify MCP still reaches it, because right now that is the one thing this whole tool inventory depends on.

# Skills audit — which skills fire, which don't, can we tell

Read-only, no edits outside this file. Window: task dirs `2026-09-22` → `2026-09-29` (no dirs for 09-26/27).

## Inventory (26 skill dirs with a SKILL.md, sorted by size)

| skill | lines | last commit | description starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| mastermind, layout, fork-claude-session, ui-test, sub-mastermind, code | 484/363/320/284/220/209 | all 09-21→09-29 | the big reference/orchestrator skills; no size or freshness problem |
| research, minion, page, css, check-claude-usage | 147/121/117/112/101 | 09-29/09-29/09-29/09-29/**08-18** | mid-size, all still actively called (see next table) |
| finish-task, new-task, servex-mastermind, documentation, auditor | 90/90/75/74/71 | 09-28/09-29/09-29/09-29/**09-21** | landing + orchestration skills |
| new-page, log-assistant, new-css-class, content, every-prompt, master-assistant, clarity | 61→50 lines | 09-21→09-28 | small, focused trigger skills |
| skill-improvement, decide, naming | 38/42/13 | **08-18**/09-29/09-29 | short, mechanical |
| **openrouter** | 7 | **untracked (`??`)** | never committed — can vanish on any clean/stash elsewhere |
| **assistant** (dead dir) | no SKILL.md | 09-21 | only holds `say.mjs`; not in the skill listing at all — leftover from before `every-prompt` was named |

## Invocations, 09-22 → 09-29 (146 task dirs opened in that window)

| skill | count |
|---|---|
| finish-task | 72 |
| documentation | 25 |
| check-claude-usage | 13 |
| skill-improvement | 12 |
| layout | 11 |
| fans | 10 |
| code | 10 |
| css | 6 |
| new-page | 5 |
| new-css-class | 4 |
| minion | 4 |
| page | 3 |
| ui-test | 2 |
| new-task | 1 |
| all others (mastermind, sub-mastermind, servex-mastermind, auditor, clarity, master-assistant, log-assistant, every-prompt, naming, decide, research, content, openrouter, assistant) | **0** |

## Trigger gaps (skill that should fire vs. what actually happened)

| trigger skill | should-fire count | logged calls | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| new-task | 146 task dirs created | 1 (16 ever, any date) | 145 |
| finish-task | 150 `landed_at` writes | 72 | 78 |
| new-page | 103 `page.js` files added (git log, same window) | 5 | 98 |

## Stale / missing

Zero logged calls, 09-22→09-29: mastermind, sub-mastermind, servex-mastermind, auditor, clarity,
master-assistant, log-assistant, every-prompt, naming, decide, research, content — explained in
finding 3, not a straightforward "unused" list. No skill's text pointed at a missing file on
spot-check (`Servex/ext/openrouter/readme.md` etc. all exist). No repeated "no skill for this"
complaint found in any `improvements.md` touched in the last 7 days (11 files, checked below).

## Findings

1. **The new-task and new-page gaps are real and large, not just a logging artifact.** 146 task
   directories opened this week, but only 1 `"skill: new-task"` line anywhere in that window (16
   ever, whole repo history) — the skill says run it before the first edit, and mostly that isn't
   happening. Same shape for new-page: 103 new `page.js` files landed, the skill fired 5 times.

2. **Part of the new-task gap is the hook's own chicken-and-egg hole, but not most of it.** The
   hook resolves "this session's task" by walking up from an existing `task.jsonl` — the file
   `new-task` itself creates. A call made before that file exists has nowhere to log, so the true
   count is higher than 1. It can't be higher than ~16, though, against 146 dirs — most task dirs
   are still being opened without the skill.

3. **The zero-invocation orchestrator skills prove the log can't see that whole class, not that
   they're unused.** mastermind, sub-mastermind, servex-mastermind, master-assistant,
   log-assistant, every-prompt are long-lived processes started by a launch prompt rather than a
   live Skill-tool call inside an open task, and often never open a `task.jsonl` of their own. The
   brief asks "can we verify skills fire when they should" — for this half of the roster, the
   honest answer is **no, not with the current log**, which only captures per-task Skill-tool
   calls. That gap in the verification method is the biggest single finding here.

# Item UI and object views: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`; read them in full. Two phases, one task, because object views are built FROM items.

## Phase 1: the item (icon item)
1. **One line: an optional icon, then a name.** It fills the row by default; an inline (span) variant also exists. Padding is roughly a button's standard padding (check it against ui/button; tighten if needed).
2. **Optional parts:** a right-side icon (a ⋯ menu button, or an arrow when it's a link); expandable (built on native summary/details, so an item can be a summary that opens); nesting and indentation, so items make a TREE, the way a file tree does.
3. **A class word:** put `item` on an element and the system configures it (layout, expandability). Relation to core/Item (persistence): study it, then propose merge vs. keeping them separate, with the reasons. Don't break core/Item.
4. Reuse ux/Content/Concepts (icon tiles), Disclosure (and the summary-styles variants being built now) and the file explorer's tree. Unify where it's cheap; don't build a fourth tree.

## Phase 2: object views (every instance can be a card)
5. **Study all the modules** in framework/: which classes are object-like, and which already have a view (ux/Content/Object is the object card built 09-28). A table: class, has a view?, is worth one?
6. **A default view, automatically:** a view that walks an instance's own properties and renders a best guess as nested items. Property names show with a leading dot (`.children`, `.nav`); the instance shows as "a Page". It can be overridden with the owner's pattern `Thing.View` (`class Thing { static View = class extends View {…} }`, as `thing.view`).
7. **Instance tracking, opt-in:** `Class.track(this)` in the constructor, so a doc page can show live instances.
8. **First uses:** a live Page object on /framework/core/Page/ (name, "instance of Page", children, nav, files…), and the App (current route and settings).
9. **Write the pattern into the `code` skill** (an OOP section: `Thing.View`, `track`, the default view), briefly.

## Rules
Keep v1 of anything you restyle reachable. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test, merge.mjs, a fresh-eyes review, and screenshots at 1920 and 400. At most 3 minions; budget about $12. # Item UI and object views: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`; read them in full. Two phases, one task, because object views are built FROM items.

## Phase 1: the item (icon item)
1. **One line: an optional icon, then a name.** It fills the row by default; an inline (span) variant also exists. Padding is roughly a button's standard padding (check it against ui/button; tighten if needed).
2. **Optional parts:** a right-side icon (a ⋯ menu button, or an arrow when it's a link); expandable (built on native summary/details, so an item can be a summary that opens); nesting and indentation, so items make a TREE, the way a file tree does.
3. **A class word:** put `item` on an element and the system configures it (layout, expandability). Relation to core/Item (persistence): study it, then propose merge vs. keeping them separate, with the reasons. Don't break core/Item.
4. Reuse ux/Content/Concepts (icon tiles), Disclosure (and the summary-styles variants being built now) and the file explorer's tree. Unify where it's cheap; don't build a fourth tree.

## Phase 2: object views (every instance can be a card)
5. **Study all the modules** in framework/: which classes are object-like, and which already have a view (ux/Content/Object is the object card built 09-28). A table: class, has a view?, is worth one?
6. **A default view, automatically:** a view that walks an instance's own properties and renders a best guess as nested items. Property names show with a leading dot (`.children`, `.nav`); the instance shows as "a Page". It can be overridden with the owner's pattern `Thing.View` (`class Thing { static View = class extends View {…} }`, as `thing.view`).
7. **Instance tracking, opt-in:** `Class.track(this)` in the constructor, so a doc page can show live instances.
8. **First uses:** a live Page object on /framework/core/Page/ (name, "instance of Page", children, nav, files…), and the App (current route and settings).
9. **Write the pattern into the `code` skill** (an OOP section: `Thing.View`, `track`, the default view), briefly.

## Rules
Keep v1 of anything you restyle reachable. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test, merge.mjs, a fresh-eyes review, and screenshots at 1920 and 400. At most 3 minions; budget about $12. # Item UI and object views: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`; read them in full. Two phases, one task, because object views are built FROM items.

## Phase 1: the item (icon item)
1. **One line: an optional icon, then a name.** It fills the row by default; an inline (span) variant also exists. Padding is roughly a button's standard padding (check it against ui/button; tighten if needed).
2. **Optional parts:** a right-side icon (a ⋯ menu button, or an arrow when it's a link); expandable (built on native summary/details, so an item can be a summary that opens); nesting and indentation, so items make a TREE, the way a file tree does.
3. **A class word:** put `item` on an element and the system configures it (layout, expandability). Relation to core/Item (persistence): study it, then propose merge vs. keeping them separate, with the reasons. Don't break core/Item.
4. Reuse ux/Content/Concepts (icon tiles), Disclosure (and the summary-styles variants being built now) and the file explorer's tree. Unify where it's cheap; don't build a fourth tree.

## Phase 2: object views (every instance can be a card)
5. **Study all the modules** in framework/: which classes are object-like, and which already have a view (ux/Content/Object is the object card built 09-28). A table: class, has a view?, is worth one?
6. **A default view, automatically:** a view that walks an instance's own properties and renders a best guess as nested items. Property names show with a leading dot (`.children`, `.nav`); the instance shows as "a Page". It can be overridden with the owner's pattern `Thing.View` (`class Thing { static View = class extends View {…} }`, as `thing.view`).
7. **Instance tracking, opt-in:** `Class.track(this)` in the constructor, so a doc page can show live instances.
8. **First uses:** a live Page object on /framework/core/Page/ (name, "instance of Page", children, nav, files…), and the App (current route and settings).
9. **Write the pattern into the `code` skill** (an OOP section: `Thing.View`, `track`, the default view), briefly.

## Rules
Keep v1 of anything you restyle reachable. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test, merge.mjs, a fresh-eyes review, and screenshots at 1920 and 400. At most 3 minions; budget about $12. Post progress on card 2026/09/29/item-ui-and-object-views-icon-items-tree. task-mastermind-page-system owns core/Page content, so coordinate before adding the Page object there.

# `sustain.mjs --restart` must run outside Servex's process tree

**Why:** at 1:44 PM on 09-28 and 1:27 PM on 09-29, an agent ran `node Servex/sustain.mjs --restart` from its own shell. The chain was Servex → claude → bash → node sustain → taskkill. `taskkill /pid <servex> /t /f` killed the caller's own chain (every agent) before it reached Servex, so Servex kept running the old code and no agent was revived. Evidence: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lew42\servex\logs\sustain.log` has "killing Servex 32996" and no "back as pid" line. The same command, started from outside the tree with `Win32_Process.Create` (restart-outside-132916.log), worked.

## Do
1. In `sustain.mjs`, `--restart` on win32 re-launches itself (`--restart-detached`, the same flags) through `Win32_Process.Create` (PowerShell `Invoke-CimMethod`, ShowWindow 0, spawned with `windowsHide:true`), so its parent is WmiPrvSE, never Servex. Then it exits and prints the log path. The detached copy does today's work.
2. The `restart_servex` tool (`Servex/agents/ops.js`) goes through the same path.
3. `kill()`: check that taskkill succeeded, and that `alive(servex)` is false after 5 seconds. Otherwise log it loudly and try a plain `taskkill /pid /f` on the root.
4. Prove it on a private Servex: start the restart from a process INSIDE that Servex's tree, and show the pid changing.
No window may ever appear.

Land: merge.mjs, a one-line note in `Servex/doc/` on restarts, and finish-task. Model: Sonnet, medium. Fence: Servex/sustain.mjs, Servex/agents/ops.js, Servex/doc/*restart*.

**There is no File or Directory class anywhere.** A file is a plain path string; a folder is a
nested object built on the fly. Three places draw files, and all three call the same `files()`.

## Data

| What | Where | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| The whole site's file list | `/directory.json`, written by [Server/plugins/Directory.js](/Server/plugins/Directory.js) | `{name, type: "dir"\|"file", children}` | Dev server only; production has none. Ignores every `.json` file. |
| Reading it | [core/Page/Markdown.js](/framework/core/Page/Markdown.js) `tree()`, `node(dir)` | the raw JSON node | The one reader; `ext/files/fs.js` and `ext/AITask` reuse it. [ai2/groups.js](/framework/ai2/groups.js) fetches `/framework/directory.json` itself. |
| A list of paths → a folder tree | [ext/files/files.js](/framework/ext/files/) `nest()` | `{ "a.js": "path", dir: {…} }` | Also used by [ext/Doc](/framework/ext/Doc/)'s Docs tab. |
| A folder's files, as a page log | [Server/plugins/PageFiles.js](/Server/plugins/PageFiles.js) | `{"file": "x.png"}` lines in `page.jsonl` | Appends when a file appears or goes. |
| Writing a file | [ext/Saver/FileSaver.js](/framework/ext/Saver/) | `socket.async_rpc("write", path, text)` | Dev only; JSON documents. |

## UI

| What the reader sees | Where | Built on |
|---|---|---|
| A tree + the clicked file's source | [ext/files](/framework/ext/files/) `files()` | its own `tree()`, `rows()`, `source()` |
| `<any path>/fs/`, full screen, no site nav | [ext/files/fs.js](/framework/ext/files/) via `Page.fs_folder()` in [core/Page](/framework/core/Page/) | `files()` + `/directory.json` |
| A module's **Files** tab (tree, prose, source) | [ext/Doc](/framework/ext/Doc/) `Doc.js` | `files(…, { about })`, plus an "Open full screen" link to `/fs/` |
| An AI 2 card's folder | [core/Page/Log.js](/framework/core/Page/) `draw_folder()` (card.js calls it) | `files()` |
| Workspace documents | [ext/Panel/Workspace](/framework/ext/Panel/Workspace/) `documents.js` | FileSaver; saved panel layouts, not files |
| Icon items and trees (being built) | `ui/item`, branch `worktree/item-ui` | details/summary rows |

- **Duplicated:** walking `directory.json` into a path list (fs.js `list()`, Markdown.js, ai2/groups.js); tree rows (`ext/files` `rows()` vs `ext/Doc`'s own tree vs the coming `ui/item` tree).
- **Missing:** a File or Directory object; a line anchor (`#L42`); a context menu; a `file_link()` helper; the site nav on `/fs/` (it hides it).

# What emptied node_modules at 13:46: `git worktree remove --force` went through a junction

**Proven, not ranked.** At **13:46:47** the `servex-docs-tab` task mastermind (Claude session
`6ba7761f-91ad-4c62-a59e-9f66a03a6138`) cleaned up its worktree with this command:

```
cd C:/Code/lew42/monorepo && git merge --no-edit worktree/servex-docs-tab 2>&1 | tail -10 && git worktree remove ../worktrees/servex-docs-tab --force 2>&1 && git branch -d worktree/servex-docs-tab 2>&1
```

That worktree's `node_modules` and `Servex/node_modules` were **junctions into the main tree**.
The session had made them by hand 21 minutes earlier with `cmd /c mklink /J`. Git for Windows
(2.47.1) deletes a worktree folder by folder, and it went *into* the junctions instead of just
unlinking them. It emptied the main tree's `node_modules`. Then it stopped partway through
`Servex/node_modules` with `error: failed to delete 'C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/servex-docs-tab': Invalid argument`,
most likely on a locked `claude.exe`.

Nothing broke right away, because the running Servex already had `express` loaded in memory.
The crash loop began at **13:53:25**, when another session (`7eedf4fd…`, chip-context-fix)
called `restart_servex`. The new Servex process could not find `express`.

None of the five old junction worktrees in the brief did this. Neither did worktree-up, Pool.js,
merge.mjs, ExitWorktree or npm. The junction was made by hand, outside every script. So the
guard has to check at deletion time. Checking only when a worktree is created would not have
caught this one.

2. Agents make junctions by hand when `take_worktree` has none free. A better answer from the pool, a shared node_modules via `NODE_PATH`-free resolution, or a sanctioned `worktree-up --no-server`, would take away the reason to do it.

index 00000000..245a01d7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/public/framework/core/track/track.js
@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+/**
+ * track(Klass) — installs opt-in instance tracking on a class: `Klass.track(instance)`,
+ * called once from that class's own constructor, remembers the instance;
+ * `Klass.instances()` reads them all back, live.
+ *
+ *   import { track } from "../track/track.js";
+ *   track(Widget);                              // once, at module scope
+ *   class Widget { constructor(){ Widget.track(this); } }
+ *   Widget.instances()                          // → every live Widget
+ *
+ * Not every class should do this — most never call `track()` at all, so most
+ * classes pay nothing and show up nowhere. Opt in only where "see every one of
+ * these" is actually useful (the owner, 2026-09-29).
+ *
+ * A WeakRef set, not a plain array: several classes in this framework build
+ * throwaway instances that live for one render and are then dropped (a `Page`
+ * built just to draw a preview, `Page.drew_content()`'s own copy). A plain
+ * array would hold every one of those forever and the tracked list would only
+ * grow. A `WeakRef` lets the instance go once nothing else holds it;
+ * `instances()` drops the dead ones as it reads, so the list is always
+ * "what's actually still alive" — never a leak, never stale.
+ */
+export function track(Klass){
+	const refs = new Set();
+
+	Klass.track = function(instance){
+		refs.add(new WeakRef(instance));
+		return instance;
+	};
+
+	Klass.instances = function(){
+		const live = [];
+		for (const ref of refs){
+			const instance = ref.deref();
+			instance ? live.push(instance) : refs.delete(ref);
+		}
+		return live;
+	};
+
+	return Klass;
+}
+
+export default track;

+# Relation to core/Item
+
+The owner's own words: "I know the item... class like core/item is based on persistence.
+However, those could be kind of merged together, but also they could be kind of separate."
+
+This looks at both and recommends: **keep them separate.** Not touched — `core/Item` itself is
+untouched by this task, on purpose (the brief's own rule).
+
+## What each one actually is
+
+| | `core/Item` | `ui/item` (this module) |
+|---|---|---|
+| Runs where | Headless — node or browser, no DOM at all | Browser only — it IS a DOM row |
+| Holds state | Yes — `data`, `items` (a `List`), a `parent`, listeners (`on`/`emit`) | No — the browser's own `<details open>` is the only state, and that's native, not this module's |
+| Wire format | `{ type, id, data, items }`, saved through a `Saver` | None — nothing to save, nothing to load |
+| Used for | A node of a document that PERSISTS: Panel, an editor Block | One line on a screen: an icon, a name, maybe a right end, maybe a fold |
+
+They share an English word by coincidence, not by design: `core/Item` is a fact about **data**
+("this thing is part of a saved tree"); `ui/item` is a fact about **a row's own markup**
+("this element is an icon, a name and an end, laid out one way"). A `core/Item` never draws
+itself — something else (`ext/Panel`'s views) reads its data and builds DOM. `ui/item` never
+persists anything — it has nothing to persist.
+
+## Why not merge
+
+1. **Different layers would gain baggage they don't need.** Every `core/Item` subclass (Panel,
+   an editor Block) would carry a DOM factory it may never call; every plain `ui.item()` call —
+   most of them, on most doc pages — would drag in `List`, a `Saver` contract and an `id` nobody
+   asked for. `core/` runs in node today (`core/Item/readme.md`: "headless, runs in node") —
+   importing `ui/item.js`, which touches `document.createElement` on its very first line via
+   `View`, would break that outright.
+2. **The wire format is a contract with real callers already.** `{ type, id, data, items }` is
+   read by `Item.open()`, every `Saver`, and `Item.register()`'s name table. Folding a rendering
+   concern into that class risks a field colliding with `data` (a saved item that happens to have
+   a property called `icon` or `name` already, for its own reasons) — a coincidence-of-name bug
+   exactly like the ones `code.js`'s "Names that collide with core" section warns about, one
+   layer down.
+3. **Nothing is lost by keeping them apart.** A `core/Item`-backed tree that wants to LOOK like
+   `.item` rows can already do that the way `ux/Tree` wears `ui/tree`'s `.ui-tree-*` classes: the
+   behavior class reads its own data and calls `ui.item({ icon: node.icon, name: node.text, … })`
+   for each row. That is a normal import, not a merge — and it is the natural next step if
+   `ext/Panel` or an editor Block ever wants this look, which this task does not build.
+
+## The recommendation
+
+**Keep `core/Item` (persistence) and `ui/item` (a row's markup) as two separate, unmerged
+things.** If a persisted tree (Panel, a future editor) wants to render its nodes as `.item` rows,
+its own view class calls `ui.item()` per node — the same relationship `ux/Tree` already has with
+`ui/tree`, and no change to either module.

+# Reuse — could an existing row just wear `.item`?
+
+The brief's rule: "reuse, don't add a fourth tree" — study what already draws an icon-plus-name
+row, and say where `.item` could replace one CHEAPLY, without restyling anything this pass. Four
+modules looked at; one is a good, cheap fit; one is a fit with a real behavior cost; two are not
+a fit at all. Nothing below was changed — `ux/Tree`, `ext/files` and `ux/Content/Disclosure` are
+all still exactly what they were before this task.
+
+## Good, cheap fit: `ux/Content/Disclosure`'s own row
+
+[`Disclosure.js`](/framework/ux/Content/Disclosure/Disclosure.js) already builds almost exactly
+what `ui/item`'s branch case builds — a `<summary>` holding an icon and a title, native
+expand/collapse, no script:
+
+```js
+summary(() => {
+	if (it.icon) icon(it.icon);
+	span.c("ux-content-title", it.title);
+});
+```
+
+That is `.item`'s row, hand-written a second time with different class names. Swapping
+`summary.c("ux-content-disclosure", ...)`'s inner two lines for `summary.c("item", () => { icon;
+name; })` would cost one small edit and gain the caret and the icon/name alignment work already
+done here — Disclosure's own `stack`/`gap`/`box`/`scheme`/`marker` words all live on the
+CONTAINER, not the row, so they would still work unchanged. **Left undone this pass** because the
+brief says keep v1 of anything reachable reachable, and Disclosure's five new words are still
+being built (its own `variants/` page, landed the same week) — a good next task, not a same-task
+edit to a module in flight.
+
+## A fit with a real cost, not a free one: `ext/files`' tree
+
+[`files.js`](/framework/ext/files/files.js)'s rows (`.file-name`, `.file-dir-name`) are visually
+the same idea — an icon, a label, a folder that opens — but the OPEN/SHUT state is not native:
+`rows()` toggles a `.file-dir`'s own `open` CSS class by hand, in a click listener that ALSO has
+to know not to fire when the click was really a row selection (`show()`, which reads
+`e.target.closest(".file-name")` on the whole tree). Swapping the folder row for `.item`'s
+`<details>`/`<summary>` branch would mean the BROWSER now owns open/shut, which is a real rewrite
+of that click-routing, not a class swap — `.item`'s classes could still be worn on the leaf
+`.file-name` rows for the icon/name look with no behavior change at all, cheaply, but the folder
+rows are where the real saving would be and also where the real work is. **Left as a finding**,
+not a fix: worth a task of its own, not a drive-by inside this one.
+
+## Not a fit: `ux/Tree`
+
+[`Tree.js`](/framework/ux/Tree/Tree.js)'s row carries drag (a grip), a star "default" mark, `+`/
+`×` act buttons, a roving tabindex and a live selection class — five things `.item` does not have
+and was never asked to. The two ALREADY share the one idea that transfers for free — a caret and
+an icon share one square frame, centred with `line-height: 1` — because this module copied that
+exact reasoning from `ui/tree/tree.js`'s own comment rather than reinventing it. Actually wearing
+`.item` on a `Tree` row would mean either giving `.item` all five of those extra slots (turning a
+one-line component into a tree-editor component) or stripping them from `Tree` (a real feature
+loss, not a refactor). Neither is "cheap," so this stays untouched.
+
+## Not a fit: `ux/Content/Concepts`
+
+[`Concepts.js`](/framework/ux/Content/Concepts/Concepts.js)'s tiles (`a.c("btn ux-content-tile")`)
+are icon-over-or-beside-name cards in a WRAPPING GRID — "what a page is made of," meant to be
+scanned as a wall, not read down as a list. `.item` fills its row and reads top to bottom by
+design; forcing it into a tile grid would fight that default on every tile. Different shape for a
+different job — left alone.
+
+## The one-line summary
+
+Only `ux/Content/Disclosure` is a same-pass-cheap swap, and it wasn't touched because the module
+is mid-build elsewhere this week. `ext/files` is worth doing, at the cost of a real behavior
+rewire. `ux/Tree` and `ux/Content/Concepts` are not `.item` candidates at all — they solve
+different problems that happen to also involve an icon and a name.

+import { div, a, span, button, icon, details, summary, is } from "../../core/View/View.js";
+import { css } from "../parts.js";
+
+/**
+ * item({ icon, name, href, end, open, children }) — one row: an optional icon, then
+ * a name. Put the class `.item` on anything and this is the whole layout system: it
+ * fills its row by default, flat — no border, no background, a light hover wash.
+ * Add `.inline` yourself (`item({ … }).ac("inline")`) to make it hug its own content
+ * instead, like a chip sitting inside a line of text; add `.boxed` for the ordinary
+ * button look (background, border) framework.css gives every plain control.
+ *
+ *   item({ icon: "description", name: "readme.md", href: "/readme.md" })
+ *   item({ icon: "folder", name: "core", open: true, children: [
+ *       { icon: "description", name: "View.js", href: "/core/View/View.js" },
+ *   ]})
+ *   item({ name: "Page", end: "menu" })                    // a right-side ⋯ button
+ *   item({ name: "Docs", href: "/framework/", end: "arrow" }) // a right-side →, for a link
+ *
+ * `children` makes this a TREE NODE: the row becomes a native `<summary>` inside a
+ * `<details>` — the summary IS the row (the owner's words), and the browser does the
+ * expand/collapse, no script required. `href` is ignored when `children` is set; an
+ * item is a link OR a branch, never both, in this first version.
+ *
+ * `children` is an array of the same `{ icon, name, … }` shape, nested to any depth
+ * for a file-tree-style indent, or a function that draws its own content instead —
+ * called once, inside the row's children box, for a caller who wants to build that
+ * part by hand (its own loop, its own markup).
+ *
+ * `end` is `"menu"` (a small ⋯ button — wire its `click` yourself, this only draws
+ * it), `"arrow"` (a plain → glyph, for a link row), or a function that draws
+ * anything else there.
+ *
+ * A row that is one of an array `children` always reserves the caret's own width,
+ * blank when that row has no children of its own — a leaf sitting beside a branch
+ * (a file next to a folder, both children of the same folder) lines its icon up
+ * with its sibling's, the way a real file tree does. `sibling` is that flag; you
+ * never pass it by hand — the recursion above sets it for you.
+ */
+function item({ icon: glyph, name, href, end, open, children } = {}, sibling){
+	const kids = children != null;
+	const caret = kids || sibling;
+
+	// The row's own insides — shared between the plain-row and the summary-row case,
+	// so a branch and a leaf line up on the same icon and name columns.
+	const inside = () => {
+		if (caret) span.c("item-caret", kids ? "▸" : "");
+		if (glyph) icon(glyph).ac("item-icon");
+		span.c("item-name", name);
+		end_part(end);
+	};

+		return details.c("item-node", $node => {
+			if (open) $node.attr("open", "");
+			summary.c("item", inside);
+			div.c("item-children", () => {
+				is.fn(children) ? children() : children.forEach(child => item(child, true));
+			});
+		});
+	}
+
+	const $row = (href ? a : div).c("item", inside);
+	if (href) $row.href(href);
+	return $row;
+}
+
+function end_part(end){
+	if (!end) return;
+	if (is.fn(end)) return end();
+
+	if (end === "arrow") return icon("arrow_forward").ac("item-end");
+
+	if (end === "menu")
+		return button.c("item-end", () => icon("more_vert"))

+			// row click the caller wired up — wiring what the menu itself does is theirs.

+	   boxed bar next to the flat leaf rows below it (the owner, 2026-09-29: "reads
+	   like a stack of buttons instead of a file tree"). The class .item beats a bare
+	   summary selector on specificity alone, in the same layer, so these lines win
+	   regardless of load order — reset every property that rule set, not just the
+	   ones that looked wrong in a screenshot, or the leftover would resurface on
+	   hover (the inset shadow survives a background/border reset on its own,
+	   because nothing had reset it too — NO BACKTICKS IN THIS COMMENT, it lives
+	   inside a css(...) template literal and one backtick blanks the whole site). */
+	.item {
+		display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5em;
+		width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; min-height: 0;
+		padding: 0.3em 0.6em; border-radius: var(--radius);
+		color: inherit; text-decoration: none;
+		background: none; border: none; box-shadow: none;
+	}
+	.item.inline { display: inline-flex; width: auto; }
+
+	a.item:hover, summary.item:hover { background: var(--wash); }
+

+	   is the same boxed look this whole rule exists to turn off — only a KEYBOARD
+	   focus draws the ring now. */
+	.item:focus { outline: none; }
+	.item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--prim); outline-offset: -2px; }
+
+	/* The boxed look, back as an opt-in — the exact rule .item resets above, so
+	   .item.boxed reads identically to a plain button on this site. */
+	.item.boxed { background-color: var(--fill-a08); border: 1px solid var(--fill-a32); }
+	.item.boxed:hover { border-color: var(--prim); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 999px var(--fill-a08); }
+
+	/* The UA's own disclosure triangle is one bullet too many now that .item-caret
+	   draws the fold inside the row — Firefox and Chrome both drop it under
+	   list-style: none (the spec routes a summary's marker through display:

+	   branch (fold, then icon) still land their names on the same column — the same
+	   reasoning ui/tree's --ui-tree-frame recorded: line-height: 1 centres the glyph
+	   in a box exactly its own em square, not its taller inherited line box. */

+		flex: 0 0 auto;
+		display: grid; place-items: center;
+		width: 1.3em; aspect-ratio: 1; line-height: 1;
+	}
+	.item-caret {
+		color: var(--subtle);
+		transform: rotate(0deg); transition: transform 0.1s;
+	}
+	.item-node[open] > .item > .item-caret { transform: rotate(90deg); }
+
+	.item-name { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
+
+	.item-end { flex: 0 0 auto; margin-inline-start: auto; display: flex; align-items: center; }
+	button.item-end {
+		background: none; border: none; padding: 0.2em; min-height: unset;
+		border-radius: var(--radius); color: inherit; cursor: pointer;
+	}
+	button.item-end:hover { background: var(--wash); }

+	   of its own padding, the same reasoning ui/tree and ext/files both already use. */
+	.item-children { padding-inline-start: var(--item-indent, 1.25em); }
+}`);

+export { item };

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+# item — one row: an optional icon, then a name
+
+The owner's own words: "it's just a single line, an icon, and a name." `item()` is that row,
+plus two things that ride along for free: a right-side end (a ⋯ menu or a → for a link), and a
+tree, when it has children — built on the browser's own `<details>`/`<summary>`, so the open and
+shut state needs no script at all.
+
+## Use
+
+```js
+import { ui } from "/app.js";
+
+ui.item({ icon: "description", name: "readme.md", href: "/framework/ui/item/" });
+
+ui.item({ icon: "folder", name: "core", open: true, children: [
+	{ icon: "description", name: "View.js", href: "/framework/core/View/", end: "arrow" },
+] });
+```
+
+`children` is an array of the same shape, nested to any depth (a file tree), or a function that
+draws its own content instead. `end` is `"menu"` (a ⋯ button — wire its click yourself, this only
+draws it), `"arrow"` (a plain →, for a link row), or a function for anything else. Add `.inline`
+yourself (`ui.item({ … }).ac("inline")`) for a row that hugs its own content instead of filling
+the line — a chip inside a line of text rather than a row in a list. Add `.boxed` for the
+background-and-border look every plain `<button>` on the site already has — `.item` is flat by
+default (no border, no background, a light hover wash), because a tree of boxed rows reads as a
+stack of buttons, not a tree.
+
+## Watch out
+
+- **`children` and `href` don't mix in this first version.** A branch is a `<summary>`, and its
+  `href` is never read — an item is a link OR a tree node, not both yet: [item.js](item.js).
+- The padding is a control's own, tightened on the sides — not a page-region `.pad` and not a
+  card's `--pad-card`, because a row's size is about its own text, the same reasoning every
+  button and nav item already follows: [item.js](item.js), the padding note beside the CSS.
+- `core/Item` is a different thing with a similar name — a persistence base class, not this.
+  Kept separate, on purpose: [doc/core-item.md](doc/core-item.md).
+
+## More
+
+- [Overview](/framework/ui/item/) — the framework's own folder tree, drawn live, and all seven variants side by side.
+- [doc/reuse.md](doc/reuse.md) — where `.item` could replace a row in `ux/Tree`, `ux/Content/Disclosure` or `ext/files`, at low risk, in a later pass.
+- [doc/core-item.md](doc/core-item.md) — `core/Item` compared, and the recommendation.
+- Back to [UI](/framework/ui/).
