@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+import View, { div, span, details, summary } from "../../../core/View/View.js";
+import { item } from "../../../ui/item/item.js";
+
+/**
+ * class DefaultView extends View — give it any real object and it draws a tree of
+ * `.item` rows, the same shape as a file tree: a header row naming the class, then
+ * one row per own property, its name written with a leading dot (`.children`,
+ * `.title`). A property whose value is a plain value (a string, a number, a
+ * boolean) shows that value inline, right after the name. A property whose value
+ * is an object, an array or a Map becomes an EXPANDABLE row — its own properties /
+ * entries are not looked at, or drawn, until you actually click it open, so a huge
+ * object graph (a `Page`, whose `.children` holds a Map of more `Page`s, whose
+ * `.parent` points straight back) costs nothing until you go looking, and never
+ * loops forever: a value already on the path you're expanding shows "↺ already
+ * open above" instead of opening again.
+ *
+ *   new DefaultView({ subject: somePage })      // this is the whole call
+ *   view(somePage)                              // the usual way in — see below
+ *
+ * Functions, DOM/View nodes, and a property that is declared but never set
+ * (`undefined`) are skipped, same as `ObjectCard` (`Object.js`, beside this
+ * file) does — nothing to usefully show for any of the three.
+ *
+ * **The override.** A class that wants its own look defines `static View`:
+ *
+ *   class Widget { … }
+ *   Widget.View = class extends DefaultView { render(){ … } };
+ *
+ * and `view(thing)` finds it automatically — `thing.constructor.View` reaches an
+ * inherited one too, because a JS static is on the constructor's own prototype
+ * chain, the same as any other inherited member.
+ */
+export default class DefaultView extends View {
+
+	render(){
+		const subject = this.subject;
+		const klass = typeof subject === "function" ? subject : subject?.constructor;
+		const label = subject && typeof subject !== "function" ? (subject.name ?? subject.title) : null;
+		const article = /^[aeiou]/i.test(klass?.name ?? "Object") ? "an " : "a ";
+
+		item({
+			icon: "data_object",
+			name: article + (klass?.name ?? "Object"),
+			end: label ? () => span.c("item-end muted", String(label)) : undefined,
+		});
+
+		div.c("ux-content-defaultview-rows", () => this.properties(subject, new Set()));
+	}
+
+	/* Every own property worth a row, skipping the noise ObjectCard already skips:
+	 * `undefined` (declared but never set — nothing there), functions (behaviour,
+	 * not state), and DOM/View nodes (there's a live element to look at instead —
+	 * showing its guts here is never what you wanted). */
+	properties(subject, path){
+		if (!subject || typeof subject !== "object") return;
+
+		Object.keys(subject).forEach(name => {
+			const value = subject[name];
+			if (value === undefined) return;   // declared but never set — nothing to show
+			if (typeof value === "function") return;
+			if (value?.el || value instanceof Node) return;
+			this.row(name, value, path);
+		});
+	}
+
+	row(name, value, path){
+		if (value !== null && typeof value === "object") return this.expandable(name, value, path);
+
+		return item({ name: "." + name, end: () => span.c("item-end muted", this.describe(value)) });
+	}
+
+	/* An object/array/Map property: a row that looks exactly like item()'s own
+	 * `children` form (same classes, so the CSS is the same), except the inside is
+	 * built once, the first time it's actually opened — never before. `path` is
+	 * every object already being drawn above this row on THIS branch; a value
+	 * already in it is a cycle back to an ancestor, so it gets a plain note
+	 * instead of opening into itself forever. */
+	expandable(name, value, path){
+		if (path.has(value)){
+			item({ name: "." + name, end: () => span.c("item-end muted", "↺ already open above") });
+			return;
+		}
+
+		details.c("item-node", $node => {
+			summary.c("item", () => {
+				span.c("item-caret", "▸");
+				span.c("item-name", "." + name);
+				span.c("item-end muted", this.describe(value));
+			});
+
+			const $kids = div.c("item-children");
+			let opened = false;
+
+			$node.el.addEventListener("toggle", () => {
+				if (opened || !$node.el.open) return;
+				opened = true;
+				$kids.append(() => this.entries(value, new Set(path).add(value)));
+			});
+		});
+	}
+
+	entries(value, path){
+		if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.forEach((v, i) => this.row(String(i), v, path));
+		if (value instanceof Map) return value.forEach((v, k) => this.row(String(k), v, path));
+		if (value instanceof Set) return [...value].forEach((v, i) => this.row(String(i), v, path));
+		return this.properties(value, path);
+	}
+
+	/* One line for a value that ISN'T being expanded: the value itself for a
+	 * primitive, else how many things are inside, so an unopened row still says
+	 * something ("Array(3)", "Map(12)") rather than nothing at all. */
+	describe(value){
+		if (value === undefined) return "undefined";
+		if (value === null) return "null";
+		if (typeof value === "string") return this.cut(JSON.stringify(value));
+		if (typeof value === "number" || typeof value === "boolean") return String(value);
+		if (Array.isArray(value)) return `Array(${value.length})`;
+		if (value instanceof Map) return `Map(${value.size})`;
+		if (value instanceof Set) return `Set(${value.size})`;
+		if (typeof value === "object")
+			return value.constructor && value.constructor !== Object ? `${value.constructor.name} {…}` : "{…}";
+		return this.cut(String(value));
+	}
+
+	cut(text, max = 40){ return text.length <= max ? text : text.slice(0, max - 1) + "…"; }
+}
+
+/* `view(thing)` — the one call most code should use instead of `new DefaultView(…)`
+ * directly: it picks `thing.constructor.View` when that class (or one it extends)
+ * declares one, else falls back to this plain, best-guess tree. */
+export function view(thing){
+	const Klass = thing?.constructor;
+	return Klass?.View ? new Klass.View({ subject: thing }) : new DefaultView({ subject: thing });
+}

+export { DefaultView };

# What emptied node_modules at 13:46, and guards so it can't again

**What happened:** Servex crash-looped from 13:53 to 15:02 on 09-29 ("Cannot find package 'express'", then "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk"). The repo-root `node_modules` was empty (dir mtime 13:46), and `Servex/node_modules` was damaged. servex-mastermind-opus restored both with npm install. Nearly every agent died.

**Already found (mastermind-servex-4):** five old worktrees still had `node_modules` as a JUNCTION into the main tree: live-card-wide, live-preview, live-reply, servex-crash and servex-monitor, all under C:/Code/lew42/worktrees. They were made before the 09-22 fix in `Server/worktree-up.mjs:117`. Those links were removed (link only) at about 15:20. Deleting through a junction, or running `npm ci` or `npm install` inside a worktree whose node_modules is a junction, empties the main tree. Suspects for 13:46, to check: `worktree-up.mjs` or `npm ci` run in one of those five; `git worktree remove` or worktree-down of one of them; Claude Code's EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree (the chip-context-fix worktree in .claude/worktrees was removed at about 13:53, but it was made at 13:46); Pool.js take/return/prune; merge.mjs cleanup; a resumed check-consensus or recursive-pairs (their worktree dirs changed at 13:45). Evidence: task.jsonl files for 09-29, `.worktree-logs/`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\lew42\servex\logs\`, the git reflog, and the mtimes of `Servex/node_modules`.

## Do

**Proven, not ranked.** At **13:46:47** the `servex-docs-tab` task mastermind (Claude session
`6ba7761f-91ad-4c62-a59e-9f66a03a6138`) cleaned up its worktree with this command:

```

That worktree's `node_modules` and `Servex/node_modules` were **junctions into the main tree**,
hand-made 21 minutes earlier with `cmd /c mklink /J`.

The crash loop began at **13:53:25**, when another session (`7eedf4fd…`, chip-context-fix)
called `restart_servex`. The new Servex process could not find `express`.

None of the five old junction worktrees in the brief did this. Neither did worktree-up, Pool.js,
merge.mjs, ExitWorktree or npm. The junction was made by hand, outside every script. So the
guard has to check at deletion time. Checking only when a worktree is created would not have

# Contract v2: one rule for "needs you", shared by the page and Servex (2026-09-29)

This contract replaces `contract.md`. That old contract invented new `ask` and `answer` verbs. But the cards already have widgets for this: the Question and Decision widgets from `ux/Content`, which write `place`, `answer` and `chose` lines. The owner answers with the widget that is already drawn on the card. So `card_ask` places one of those widgets, and one pure function decides what is waiting.

**Worktree:** `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\needs-you` (branch `worktree/needs-you`, site at http://localhost:53478/). It is current with michael/dev. Commit only your own files (`git add <paths>`, never `-A`). ⚠ The worktree's own server writes stray lines into `public/framework/ai/**/page.jsonl` and `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl`, so never commit those.

## 1. The rule: `public/framework/ai2/needs-rule.js` (pure, with no DOM and no `/app.js` import)

Minion F makes this file, by MOVING `card_needs()` and `is_blocker()` out of `ai2/needs.js`. `needs.js` then imports them from here. The file is imported by the browser (`./needs-rule.js`) and by Servex (`../../public/framework/ai2/needs-rule.js`, the same way `Cards.js` imports `fold.js`).

`card_needs(id, lines, meta) -> [{card, ask, kind, title, question, options, hint, at, control, from}]`. An item is open when it is one of these:
- a `place` of `…/Decision/Decision.js` with no `chose` line for its id (the control is `decision`);
- a `place` of `…/Question/Question.js` with no `answer` line for its id (the control is `reply`);
- a legacy `{"ask": {id, title, question, options, from}}` line with no `{"answer": {"ask": id}}` line (yesterday's sweep wrote 6 of these; `control` is `decision` when it has options, `reply` when it doesn't);
- a card of `type: "question"` (pseudo-id `card`), or a card whose last non-owner message ends in "?" (pseudo-id `last`), in both cases with no answer, **and no `{"reviewed": {"at"}}` line newer than it**.
- It drops out when the card's status is `done` or `archived`.

The kinds rank as `blocker` → `decision` → `question` → `fyi`. The item's `from` comes from the `place` line or the `ask` line.

## 2. Asking: `card_ask({card, question, options?, title?, from?})` (Servex MCP tool, `Cards.ask()`)

It appends ONE `place` line. With `options`, that is a Decision: `{"place": {"module": "/framework/ux/Content/Decision/Decision.js", "id": "d-<base36>", "ask": question, "options": options, "title"?, "from"?, "at"}}`. Without options, it is a Question: `{"place": {"module": "/framework/ux/Content/Question/Question.js", "id": "q-<base36>", "ask": question, "title"?, "from"?, "at"}}`. It returns `{ok, id: <card>, ask: <place id>}`. Check the real `place` fields that Decision.js and Question.js read, and match them exactly.

## 3. Answering wakes the asker (inside `Cards.append()`)

Any appended `chose: {decision: id, option}`, `answer: {question: id, text}` or legacy `answer: {ask: id, text}` line is matched to the `place` or `ask` line with that id. `agents.send(from, "The owner answered your question on card <card> (\"<ask>\"): <answer>", {from: "owner", reply_to: "card <card>"})`. When there is no `from`, it goes to the card's attached non-minion agents (like `forward()`). The result includes `woke: [...]`.

## 4. The list: `list_waiting()` (MCP tool) and `GET /waiting` (HTTP)

Both run `card_needs` over every card that is not done, and return the items ranked and then newest first. This is the same set the Needs you tab and the rail's "Needs review" filter show.

## 5. Reviewed

The "Reviewed ✓" control on a card appends `{"reviewed": {"at": <ISO>, "by": "owner"}}` through `/card/append`. That clears only the heuristic items (`card` and `last`). A placed Question or Decision is cleared only by answering it.

body:
verdict: fix

1. [fix] Servex/sustain.mjs relaunch_detached (~line 190): when the WMI hop fails, PowerShell's error text in `res.stderr` is thrown away, but the note says "see the console output above", and there is nothing above it. Put `res.status` and `res.stderr` into the `note(...)`. Otherwise a failed hop becomes the same kind of silent failure this task was meant to end.
2. [note] Requirement 4 (the proof) is only described in prose in Servex/doc/restart.md. task.jsonl records the first attempt, which leaked into the real Servex, but no line shows the old and new pid from the run that passed. Add one log line with both pids, or the log file, so the claim can be checked.
3. [note] Servex/doc/restart.md is 38 lines, where the brief asked for "a one-line note". The detail is good, but it could be a three-line note (the bug, the fix, the SERVEX_HOME trap), with the long explanation kept in the sustain.mjs comment, which already says it all.
4. [note] Servex/readme.md was edited, and it is outside the fence (sustain.mjs, ops.js, doc/*restart*). The edit is a harmless one-line pointer, but it is still outside the fence.
5. [note] Servex/doc/restart.md says ops.js "needs no change", but the diff rewrites the restart_servex description in Servex/agents/ops.js:29-34. The new text is correct, because the real outcome now lands in sustain.log, so the doc sentence should say that instead.
6. [note] Servex/sustain.mjs kill(): `stop()` (line ~86) now blocks for up to 5s per pid through Atomics.wait. That is fine for a CLI, but `--stop` with many dev servers can take a while when a pid lingers. It is only worth knowing, not changing.
7. [note] Requirement 1 is met: win32 `--restart` goes through Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process.Create with ShowWindow [uint16]0, and powershell is spawned with windowsHide. `--dry-run` correctly stays in-tree. Pinning SERVEX_HOME with `cmd /c set "..."&&` is the right catch, and a simpler route would not avoid it.

# Minion C — every system page links its files

Load the `minion` skill first, then `code` and `content`.

Read: [../owner-words.md](../owner-words.md), [../requirements.md](../requirements.md), and the
`ext/fs/readme.md` in the worktree (how `file_link(path, line?)` works and what url it makes).
The card: `public/framework/ai/2026/09/29/file-system-file-and-directory-objects-f/`.

**Work in the worktree `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\file-system`** (its server: http://localhost:55895/).
Commit by exact path. Every Node spawn sets `windowsHide: true`.

## The owner's words

> "for all these system pages, make sure to reference any files … in any of these readmes, on any
> of these pages, we could reference just a file path with a specific helper function to make a link."
> "when we're referencing a specific method … it might often be better to just reference … the class
> doc page for class dot method."

## Deliverables

1. **Servex and Server source is readable in /fs, on the dev server only.** Today
   `/Servex/readme.md` and `/Server/doc/collab.md` answer 404: only `public/` is served. Add a dev
   server plugin in `Server/plugins/` that serves `Servex/**` and `Server/**` as read-only text
   (never `node_modules`, dotfiles, `.env`, keys; a path that escapes those two dirs is refused), and
   lists them the way `/directory.json` lists `public/`, so `/fs/` can show their tree. Make
   `file_link("/Servex/Servex.js", 40)` open them. Server changes go live only on a restart: test on
   the worktree's own server (you may restart the WORKTREE's server; never the main one, port 80 or
   Servex). Production has no such route; the link then says "dev server only", no broken fetch.
2. **The system pages link their files** through `file_link`, as a short "Files" line or list near
   the top of each (show the files, not a paragraph about them): `/framework/servex/` (its parts →
   `Servex/*.js`, `Servex/readme.md`, `Servex/agents/`), `/framework/core/Page/` (Page.class.js,
   Log.js, Markdown.js, words.js), `/framework/ai2/`, `/framework/dev/`. A method named in prose links
   its class-doc member page where one exists (`/framework/core/Page/api/…`; check the real url), a
   line number only where no member page exists.
3. **The `content` or `documentation` skill** gets one line: name a file with `file_link`, a method
   with its class-doc page. Append it to that skill's `improvements.md` instead if editing the skill
   itself would clash; say which.

## Fence
Yours: `Server/plugins/<one new file>.js` and its registration line, the four pages' `page.js`
files named above, one line in a skill. Not yours: `ext/fs`, `ext/files`, `ext/highlight`
(minion B's), `core/Page/*.js` code (page-system's; its page.js content only).

## Done means
Every link you add, clicked on the worktree server, opens the file in /fs (a headless probe
that follows them all). Zero console errors on the four pages. One screenshot of
`/framework/servex/` at 1920. Commit, log in `task.jsonl` beside this brief, five-line report.
Budget: about $3.

# Dictate page spacing analysis

## Layout gaps and their sources

| Gap | Element | Rule | Selector | File | Computed value (400px) |
|-----|---------|------|----------|------|------------------------|
| Large blank band below tabs | `.tab-bar` container spacing | `--pad-y` | `.page` grid | `Page.css:178` | 24px top padding + 24px bottom padding on page |
| Excessive left/right margins | `.page.doc-section` padding | `--gutter-x` | `.page` | `Page.css:173` | 32px left, 32px right (clamped to floor since 4% of 400 = 16px < 2em floor) |
| Tabs text cut off ("PLAYGROUN…") | Tab container width | implicit; tab text flows to edge | `.tab-bar` flex container | `Doc.css` (tabs module) | 400px viewport, no padding on tabs, text overflows |
| "Folder" label isolation | Block spacing after tabs | `--gap` or margin + inherited padding | `.page-fs-link` parent | Framework layout | Default block margin + page padding = ~24px above/below |

## The exact changes

### 1. Reduce top padding in tab panel (smallest, highest impact)
- **Selector:** `.tab-panel`
- **Property:** `padding-top` (or modify the flex gap that creates the band)
- **From:** Currently inherits page's `--pad-y: clamp(1.5em, 4%, 3em)` = 24px at 400px
- **To:** `0px` or `var(--gap)` (14px)
- **Why:** The tab panel content area has no reason to pay the full page padding again; the `.doc-well` (header) already paid it above

### 2. Allow cards to use their own width, not parent's
- **Selector:** Cards/sections using `--pad` token
- **Property:** `padding` (where using `--pad`)
- **From:** `var(--pad)` = `calc(clamp(1em, 2.6% - 1.1em, 4em) * var(--size))` (resolves % against PARENT)
- **To:** `var(--pad-card)` = `calc(clamp(1rem, 2%, 2em) * var(--size))` or convert to `cqi` inside a container-query context
- **Why:** At 400px, parent `2.6%` = ~10.4px − 1.1em = negative, clamps to 1em = 16px. But a card's own 2% of its own width makes more sense and doesn't depend on whether the parent is full-width or narrow.

### 3. Prefer container-query units for responsive padding
- **Property:** Padding on card-like elements
- **From:** `2.6%` (percentage of parent)
- **To:** `1.6cqi` (container query inline)
- **Caveat:** Only works if the card's own closest ancestor is marked `container-type: inline-size`. The framework currently does NOT mark `.page` or `.tab-panel` as containers, so cqi reads the **viewport**, not the card — a 250px card at 3440 ends up at the same 32px as a 1400px card.
- **Simplest fix:** Change `--pad` formula to use a pure length clamp without percentage, or mark the actual card containers as `container-type: inline-size` and rebase all padding to `cqi`.

## The `--pad` token analysis

**Does percentage pad resolve against parent?** ✓ Yes. In CSS, `padding: 2.6%;` resolves the percentage against the containing block's **width**. At 400px parent, `2.6% = 10.4px`. That is the CSS spec (CSSOM spec §4.4).

**Can a container-query unit (cqi) on an element resolve against ITSELF?** ✓ Yes, BUT only if it has a declared `container-type`. Without one, `cqi` resolves against the **viewport inline size** (the root container), not the element's own width. Spec: CSS Containment Module Level 3, §7.1.

**Smallest correct design for "a card's padding follows the card's own width":**
```css
/* Option A: Pure length, no percentage (safest) */
--pad: calc(clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2em) * var(--size));
/* Reads viewport, scales with screen, not parent width */

/* Option B: Container query (requires setup) */
.card { container-type: inline-size; }
.card { --pad: calc(clamp(1rem, 8cqi, 2em) * var(--size)); }
/* Only works if EVERY card is marked container-type: inline-size */

## 3. The `--pad` token question

**Does a percentage padding resolve against the parent, not the card's own width?** For an ordinary block element, no — CSS resolves a percentage padding against the width of the element's own **containing block**, and for a normal in-flow block that containing block's width equals the element's own parent's content-box width, which (for a plain single-column card) usually *is* the card's own width too, so `--pad`/`--pad-card`'s existing percentage form is correct there — matches `framework.css:270-279`'s own comment and `--pad-card`'s design.

**Where it actually misfires** is exactly the case the owner names — "more columns." Put that same card as a flex or grid **item** in a multi-column row, and its containing block for percentage purposes is the **flex/grid container's** content box (the whole row), not the item's own shrunk track width (CSS Flexbox spec §4, CSS Grid spec §10 — an item's percentage padding is resolved against its containing block, which is the *container*, before the item's own size is even known; this is intentional, to avoid a circular "padding depends on width depends on padding" loop). So a 3-column row and a 1-column row report the *same* percentage-padding value per card, even though each card is a different width — precisely what the owner suspected, just one level more specific than "percentages resolve against the parent" (they resolve against the *containing block*, and a flex/grid item's containing block is the whole container, not its own column).

**Can `cqi` resolve against the element itself?** No — by spec (CSS Containment Module Level 3), a container query unit resolves against the nearest **ancestor** established as a query container (`container-type: inline-size` or `size`); an element can never be its own query container, the same anti-circularity rule as above. So `cqi` on a card's own padding needs a wrapper **one level up** wearing `container-type: inline-size`; the card itself just reads `cqi`.

**Smallest correct design** for "a card's padding follows the card's own width, in any layout": give every card a **1px shell it already needs for other reasons** (a border, a background, a rounded corner — `.card`/`.surface` already have one) and put `container-type: inline-size` on *that* shell, then define the card's own padding in `cqi` on its inner content, e.g. `--pad-card: clamp(1rem, 2.6cqi, 2em)`. That one extra container wrapper is unavoidable — no unit resolves an element's own box against itself — but it costs nothing beyond a class already on every card.

The pad token:

1. **Does a percentage pad resolve against the parent?** Not exactly: it resolves against the element's *containing block* (CSS 2.1 §8.4, css-box-4). In normal block flow and in flexbox, that is the parent's content box. In a grid, it is the item's own grid area (css-grid-1 §9). In a test, `padding-left: 10%` gave 120 px on a 400 px block inside a 1200 px parent, 120 px on a flex item that was one of three in a 1200 px row, but **40 px** on a grid item in one 400 px track. So your suspicion is right for flex and block, and wrong for grid.
2. **Where it's written doesn't change that.** `--pad` is an unregistered custom property on `:where(*)`, so the `%` is pasted into `padding` and resolved on whichever element uses it. The bigger problem is `2.6% - 1.1em`: it stays on its 1em floor until the containing block is wider than about 80em (~1292 px). So every card gets a flat 1em whatever its width. `--pad` is a word for page regions. `--pad-card` (`clamp(1rem, 2.6%, 2em)`, framework.css:303) already exists for cards.
3. **Can `cqi` on an element resolve against itself?** No. css-contain-3 says a container unit uses the nearest *ancestor* query container, and falls back to the small viewport if there is none. An element that sets `container-type: inline-size` cannot read its own width that way. Measured: `10cqi` on a 400 px container gave 120 px (from its 1200 px ancestor), or 140 px (from the 1400 px viewport) when there was no ancestor container. On its **child** it gave 40 px. A card-level `@container` query has the same limit: it reads the card's parent.
4. **The smallest correct design, with no extra markup: make the side padding grid tracks.** `.card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: var(--p) minmax(0, 1fr) var(--p); padding-block: var(--pad-card) } .card > * { grid-column: 2 }` with `--p: clamp(1rem, 4%, 2em)`. A percentage in a grid track resolves against the card's **own** width (measured: 10% of a 400 px card = 40 px). `.page` already works this way with its `main`/`wide` tracks. The one catch: the card becomes a grid, so a card that was a flex row needs checking.
5. **The other option: an inner wrapper.** Make the card the container (`container-type: inline-size`) and pad its one inner wrapper with `cqi`. That is exact too, but every card's JS needs the extra element. For Dictate today, rows 1–4 above are the fix. The pad token isn't what's wrong on this page.

The pad token:

1. **Does a percentage pad resolve against the parent?** Not exactly: it resolves against the element's *containing block* (CSS 2.1 §8.4, css-box-4). In normal block flow and in flexbox, that is the parent's content box. In a grid, it is the item's own grid area (css-grid-1 §9). In a test, `padding-left: 10%` gave 120 px on a 400 px block inside a 1200 px parent, 120 px on a flex item that was one of three in a 1200 px row, but **40 px** on a grid item in one 400 px track. So your suspicion is right for flex and block, and wrong for grid.
2. **Where it's written doesn't change that.** `--pad` is an unregistered custom property on `:where(*)`, so the `%` is pasted into `padding` and resolved on whichever element uses it. The bigger problem is `2.6% - 1.1em`: it stays on its 1em floor until the containing block is wider than about 80em (~1292 px). So every card gets a flat 1em whatever its width. `--pad` is a word for page regions. `--pad-card` (`clamp(1rem, 2.6%, 2em)`, framework.css:303) already exists for cards.
3. **Can `cqi` on an element resolve against itself?** No. css-contain-3 says a container unit uses the nearest *ancestor* query container, and falls back to the small viewport if there is none. An element that sets `container-type: inline-size` cannot read its own width that way. Measured: `10cqi` on a 400 px container gave 120 px (from its 1200 px ancestor), or 140 px (from the 1400 px viewport) when there was no ancestor container. On its **child** it gave 40 px. A card-level `@container` query has the same limit: it reads the card's parent.
4. **The smallest correct design, with no extra markup: make the side padding grid tracks.** `.card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: var(--p) minmax(0, 1fr) var(--p); padding-block: var(--pad-card) } .card > * { grid-column: 2 }` with `--p: clamp(1rem, 4%, 2em)`. A percentage in a grid track resolves against the card's **own** width (measured: 10% of a 400 px card = 40 px). `.page` already works this way with its `main`/`wide` tracks. The one catch: the card becomes a grid, so a card that was a flex row needs checking.
5. **The other option: an inner wrapper.** Make the card the container (`container-type: inline-size`) and pad its one inner wrapper with `cqi`. That is exact too, but every card's JS needs the extra element. For Dictate today, rows 1–4 above are the fix. The pad token isn't what's wrong on this page.

# Each page lists its own files in its page.jsonl: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`. Today one giant `directory.json` (3.3 MB) lists the whole site. Every page fetches it, and on the phone it costs seconds (see card 2026/09/29/experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa).

## The shape the owner wants
1. **Each folder's page.jsonl lists that folder's own entries:** one line per file or subfolder DIRECTLY inside it, e.g. `{"file": "readme.md"}` / `{"dir": "doc"}`. Not the sub-folders' contents; they're in the sub-folders' own page.jsonl. So loading a page gets its listing for free, and deeper levels load on demand.
2. **Changes APPEND:** when the dev server's watcher (Server/watch.js, Server/plugins/Directory.js) sees a file or folder added, append `{"file": "x"}`; when one is removed, append `{"removed": "x"}` (latest line wins). Never rewrite the file.
3. **A backfill:** a one-time node script writes the current listing into each folder's page.jsonl. Decide which folders get one (every folder under public/ except dated task folders, node_modules and assets?), weighing the "don't clutter the tree" concern. Propose the rule, then apply it.

Keep directory.json for now, and stop depending on it for rendering.

## Traps (these have burned us)
- **The watcher must IGNORE its own writes** to page.jsonl, or it loops. Also: on Windows, a READ fires a change event (memory: "reload-on-read"), so filter by real content change.
- **Concurrent appends:** use the append path (Servex /card/append or the dev server's append), never read-modify-write.
- **Live reload:** hold it during the backfill (`node Server/hold.mjs on "page-files-log backfill"`).

# Each page lists its own files in its page.jsonl: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`. Today one giant `directory.json` (3.3 MB) lists the whole site. Every page fetches it, and on the phone it costs seconds (see card 2026/09/29/experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa).

## The shape the owner wants
1. **Each folder's page.jsonl lists that folder's own entries:** one line per file or subfolder DIRECTLY inside it, e.g. `{"file": "readme.md"}` / `{"dir": "doc"}`. Not the sub-folders' contents; they're in the sub-folders' own page.jsonl. So loading a page gets its listing for free, and deeper levels load on demand.
2. **Changes APPEND:** when the dev server's watcher (Server/watch.js, Server/plugins/Directory.js) sees a file or folder added, append `{"file": "x"}`; when one is removed, append `{"removed": "x"}` (latest line wins). Never rewrite the file.

- **Live reload:** hold it during the backfill (`node Server/hold.mjs on "page-files-log backfill"`).

The pad token:

1. **Does a percentage pad resolve against the parent?** Not exactly: it resolves against the element's *containing block* (CSS 2.1 §8.4, css-box-4). In normal block flow and in flexbox, that is the parent's content box. In a grid, it is the item's own grid area (css-grid-1 §9). In a test, `padding-left: 10%` gave 120 px on a 400 px block inside a 1200 px parent, 120 px on a flex item that was one of three in a 1200 px row, but **40 px** on a grid item in one 400 px track. So your suspicion is right for flex and block, and wrong for grid.
2. **Where it's written doesn't change that.** `--pad` is an unregistered custom property on `:where(*)`, so the `%` is pasted into `padding` and resolved on whichever element uses it. The bigger problem is `2.6% - 1.1em`: it stays on its 1em floor until the containing block is wider than about 80em (~1292 px). So every card gets a flat 1em whatever its width. `--pad` is a word for page regions. `--pad-card` (`clamp(1rem, 2.6%, 2em)`, framework.css:303) already exists for cards.
3. **Can `cqi` on an element resolve against itself?** No. css-contain-3 says a container unit uses the nearest *ancestor* query container, and falls back to the small viewport if there is none. An element that sets `container-type: inline-size` cannot read its own width that way. Measured: `10cqi` on a 400 px container gave 120 px (from its 1200 px ancestor), or 140 px (from the 1400 px viewport) when there was no ancestor container. On its **child** it gave 40 px. A card-level `@container` query has the same limit: it reads the card's parent.
4. **The smallest correct design, with no extra markup: make the side padding grid tracks.** `.card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: var(--p) minmax(0, 1fr) var(--p); padding-block: var(--pad-card) } .card > * { grid-column: 2 }` with `--p: clamp(1rem, 4%, 2em)`. A percentage in a grid track resolves against the card's **own** width (measured: 10% of a 400 px card = 40 px). `.page` already works this way with its `main`/`wide` tracks. The one catch: the card becomes a grid, so a card that was a flex row needs checking.
5. **The other option: an inner wrapper.** Make the card the container (`container-type: inline-size`) and pad its one inner wrapper with `cqi`. That is exact too, but every card's JS needs the extra element. For Dictate today, rows 1–4 above are the fix. The pad token isn't what's wrong on this page.

| Network | Before (uncompressed) | After (gzip) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|

## What this does and doesn't fix

Compression (deliverable 1) is real and lands: every response is about half
the bytes. It does **not** make the placed table appear instantly on a slow
connection — Fast 3G is genuinely slow (1.6 Mbps), and this page loads on the
order of 550 small module files (per servex-mastermind-opus's CPU-incident
measurement, below) on top of the compressed `directory.json`; no amount of
compressing one file changes that there are hundreds of requests. The
`priority: "low"` hint on the `directory.json` fetch (deliverable 2) should
help on a real phone, where the browser is choosing what to fetch first among
real concurrent requests — that part isn't independently isolated in this
table, because isolating it requires two different code versions, and running
another cross-server comparison hit the same worktree-data problem above.
Reading the actual draw path (`core/Page/Log.js` `draw_placed()` /
`draw_md()`) also shows nothing there directly `await`s `directory.json` — the
delay comes from the browser's connection pool being contended, not from an
explicit block. See `task.jsonl` for that reading, logged as it happened.

## The CPU incident, same day

The first version of `Server/compress.js` (committed, then live in the main
tree) called `zlib.createBrotliCompress()` at brotli's **default quality —
11, the maximum**, fresh on every single request, never cached.
servex-mastermind-opus caught the dev server on `:3104` at 350–590% CPU with
the owner's fans spinning and named the fix. Measured directly:
compressing `directory.json` (3.3MB) at quality 11 costs **4464ms of CPU**;
quality 4 costs **11ms** — about 400x less — and the rewritten
`compress.js` also caches the compressed bytes per file (keyed by path +
mtime + encoding), so that cost is paid once per file, not once per request.
20 repeat fetches of the cached file cost 0.22s of CPU total afterward
(~11ms each — the one uncached compression, then free). Full account in
`task.jsonl`.

This contract replaces `contract.md`. That old contract invented new `ask` and `answer` verbs. But the cards already have widgets for this: the Question and Decision widgets from `ux/Content`, which write `place`, `answer` and `chose` lines. The owner answers with the widget that is already drawn on the card. So `card_ask` places one of those widgets, and one pure function decides what is waiting.

Commit only your own files (`git add <paths>`, never `-A`). ⚠ The worktree's own server writes stray lines into `public/framework/ai/**/page.jsonl` and `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl`, so never commit those.

## 1. The rule: `public/framework/ai2/needs-rule.js` (pure, with no DOM and no `/app.js` import)

Minion F makes this file, by MOVING `card_needs()` and `is_blocker()` out of `ai2/needs.js`. `needs.js` then imports them from here. The file is imported by the browser (`./needs-rule.js`) and by Servex (`../../public/framework/ai2/needs-rule.js`, the same way `Cards.js` imports `fold.js`).

`card_needs(id, lines, meta) -> [{card, ask, kind, title, question, options, hint, at, control, from}]`. An item is open when it is one of these:
- a `place` of `…/Decision/Decision.js` with no `chose` line for its id (the control is `decision`);
- a `place` of `…/Question/Question.js` with no `answer` line for its id (the control is `reply`);
- a legacy `{"ask": {id, title, question, options, from}}` line with no `{"answer": {"ask": id}}` line (yesterday's sweep wrote 6 of these; `control` is `decision` when it has options, `reply` when it doesn't);
- a card of `type: "question"` (pseudo-id `card`), or a card whose last non-owner message ends in "?" (pseudo-id `last`), in both cases with no answer, **and no `{"reviewed": {"at"}}` line newer than it**.
- It drops out when the card's status is `done` or `archived`.

The kinds rank as `blocker` → `decision` → `question` → `fyi`. The item's `from` comes from the `place` line or the `ask` line.

## 2. Asking: `card_ask({card, question, options?, title?, from?})` (Servex MCP tool, `Cards.ask()`)

It appends ONE `place` line. With `options`, that is a Decision: `{"place": {"module": "/framework/ux/Content/Decision/Decision.js", "id": "d-<base36>", "ask": question, "options": options, "title"?, "from"?, "at"}}`. Without options, it is a Question: `{"place": {"module": "/framework/ux/Content/Question/Question.js", "id": "q-<base36>", "ask": question, "title"?, "from"?, "at"}}`. It returns `{ok, id: <card>, ask: <place id>}`. Check the real `place` fields that Decision.js and Question.js read, and match them exactly.

## 3. Answering wakes the asker (inside `Cards.append()`)

Any appended `chose: {decision: id, option}`, `answer: {question: id, text}` or legacy `answer: {ask: id, text}` line is matched to the `place` or `ask` line with that id. `agents.send(from, "The owner answered your question on card <card> (\"<ask>\"): <answer>", {from: "owner", reply_to: "card <card>"})`. When there is no `from`, it goes to the card's attached non-minion agents (like `forward()`). The result includes `woke: [...]`.

## 4. The list: `list_waiting()` (MCP tool) and `GET /waiting` (HTTP)

Both run `card_needs` over every card that is not done, and return the items ranked and then newest first. This is the same set the Needs you tab and the rail's "Needs review" filter show.

## 5. Reviewed

The "Reviewed ✓" control on a card appends `{"reviewed": {"at": <ISO>, "by": "owner"}}` through `/card/append`. That clears only the heuristic items (`card` and `last`). A placed Question or Decision is cleared only by answering it.

# Before / after — the measurement

Method: headless Playwright (CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`), same live
server (`localhost:8137`, real data), same URL
(`/framework/ai2/2026/09/29/experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa/`).
"Before" and "after" are the same server and the same code — the one thing
that changes is the `Accept-Encoding` request header (`identity` = simulates
the original uncompressed responses; normal browser default = gzip, what
`Server/compress.js` now answers with). "Time" is how long until the page's
placed markdown (`.page-log-md`, the thing that was arriving late) is in the
DOM. Script: `Server/compress.js`'s sibling — kept in the session scratchpad,
not the repo (script itself not committed; numbers here are the record).

| Network | Before (uncompressed) | After (gzip) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fast 3G | 23.8s, 3.46MB | 16.7s, 1.60MB | ~30% faster, 54% fewer bytes |
| Wi-Fi-like | 3.1s, 4.25MB | 2.5s, 2.01MB | ~20% faster, 53% fewer bytes |

(An earlier attempt compared the live server against a throwaway worktree
server instead — invalid, because that worktree has no `cards.jsonl`/socket
data of its own and 404s on this route. This table replaces it.)

## What this does and doesn't fix

Compression (deliverable 1) is real and lands: every response is about half
the bytes. It does **not** make the placed table appear instantly on a slow
connection — Fast 3G is genuinely slow (1.6 Mbps), and this page loads on the
order of 550 small module files (per servex-mastermind-opus's CPU-incident
measurement, below) on top of the compressed `directory.json`; no amount of
compressing one file changes that there are hundreds of requests. The
`priority: "low"` hint on the `directory.json` fetch (deliverable 2) should
help on a real phone, where the browser is choosing what to fetch first among
real concurrent requests — that part isn't independently isolated in this
table, because isolating it requires two different code versions, and running
another cross-server comparison hit the same worktree-data problem above.
Reading the actual draw path (`core/Page/Log.js` `draw_placed()` /
`draw_md()`) also shows nothing there directly `await`s `directory.json` — the
delay comes from the browser's connection pool being contended, not from an
explicit block. See `task.jsonl` for that reading, logged as it happened.

## The CPU incident, same day

The first version of `Server/compress.js` (committed, then live in the main
tree) called `zlib.createBrotliCompress()` at brotli's **default quality —
11, the maximum**, fresh on every single request, never cached.
servex-mastermind-opus caught the dev server on `:3104` at 350–590% CPU with
the owner's fans spinning and named the fix. Measured directly:
compressing `directory.json` (3.3MB) at quality 11 costs **4464ms of CPU**;
quality 4 costs **11ms** — about 400x less — and the rewritten
`compress.js` also caches the compressed bytes per file (keyed by path +
mtime + encoding), so that cost is paid once per file, not once per request.
20 repeat fetches of the cached file cost 0.22s of CPU total afterward
(~11ms each — the one uncached compression, then free). Full account in
`task.jsonl`.

verdict: fix

verdict: fix

1. [fix] `PageLog.listing()` (worktree `core/Page/Log.js:188-195`) does not do what the minion's own decision log says it chose. `task.jsonl` line 3 records: "What does Page.listing() return for a page.jsonl with no file lines?" → chose "null, so the caller falls back to directory.json." The shipped code only returns `null` when the fetch itself fails (`reader.loaded` false); whenever a page.jsonl exists but has zero `file` lines — a real, common shape, e.g. a chat-only AI2 card's log at `ai/2026/09/19/a-153628/page.jsonl` in the worktree, which has `title`/`text` lines and no `file` line at all — `PageLog.Listing.from()` still builds and returns a real (non-null) `Listing` with empty `files`/`dirs`/`pages`. Every caller (`groups.js`'s `day()`, `task_at()`/`look()`, `ask.js`/`sessions.js`'s `threads()`) then reads that as "confirmed empty" and never falls back to `directory.json`, silently hiding real content exactly the way the decision log says it must not. The doc comment on `listing()` even states the wrong behavior out loud: "A log with no `file` lines is an empty folder." 7. [note] `Servex/agents/card-assistant.md` is deleted and its text moved to `every-prompt/page-assistant.md`. Grep any live code or docs that still point at the old file before merging. `Servex/agents/*.js` looked clean.
8. [note] `External.deliver()` rewrites the whole `registry.json` on every inbox line (`touch()`, `External.js:108`), only to update `last_at`. A chatty card means a full registry rewrite per message. Dropping `touch()` from deliver is simpler.
9. [note] Only prose measurements are in the diff (`doc/page-pairs.md` around diff line 1926, `fix2/proof.md`). The 2-second inbox proof, the before/after process-and-MB table, and the "recycled context under 10k" number should each be one linked line in the landing, so they can be checked.
10. [note] `Global.js`: `direct_child()` treats every `parent === "dispatcher"` agent as a root child, so all task-masterminds' landings still reach master-assistant. That matches today's tree, but it is most of the old feed's volume, and worth a glance after a day of use.

verdict: fix

1. [fix] Deliverable 1 is not met as the owner wrote it. A child pair is not spawned by its parent page's mastermind: the first prompt on a page creates the pair, and the tree link is only a `parent` field written into layers.json (Servex/agents/Layers.js:934-967). The work's own Known limits admit this (Servex/agents/doc/page-pairs.md:1977). Either build the spawn-by-parent link, or put it to the owner as an open decision on the card. A note buried in a doc is not enough.
2. [fix] The owner named the ids `mastermind-<page>`, but the code mints `manager-<page>` (Layers.js:956; roles.js `page-mastermind` keeps prefix "manager"). The doc calls this "a naming decision, not the owner's word" (page-pairs.md:1992). Rename the ids, or get the owner's yes, before landing.
3. [fix] Deliverable 2 says the root assistant loads the same single skill as every other page assistant. It still reads its own `master-assistant.md` (Global.js `system("master-assistant.md")`; page-pairs.md:1982). Merge the two texts, or record that the owner accepted two.
4. [note] Deliverable 5, safe quick edits: the rule "only files inside your own directory that no claim covers" lives only in the prompt (page-assistant.md:144-162). Nothing checks the edited paths before `merge.mjs` runs. The root assistant (Global.js:653) has no built-in tools and no `take_worktree`, so it cannot make quick edits at all.
5. [note] Deliverable 6, fresh-not-compacted: `master-assistant` is skipped by `Layers.sweep()` (Layers.js:1466), and Global only restarts it once a day. So the Opus root never gets a checkpoint however large its context grows. This is admitted at page-pairs.md:1995. It is the most-used assistant, so it is the one that most needs this rule.
6. [note] Each plain page's chat is written to `public<page>ai/chat.jsonl`, inside the live-reloaded tree (Layers.js:1016). fix2/chat-reload-probe.txt shows that appending to an existing chat file triggers no reload. But its control test shows that creating a NEW file does trigger one, so the first send on any page probably reloads the page. A path under Servex's home would avoid this, and would also keep `ai/` folders out of site directories.
7. [note] `POST /api/page-ai` takes `from` straight from the request body (Layers.js:1113, 1119). Any local caller can therefore post a prompt labelled as the owner. The same goes for `send_to_agent`'s self-declared `from` (tools.js:135): Policy now gives a registered external id the owner's reach (policy.js `message()`), so if Policy trusts that argument rather than a caller id stamped by Servex, anyone can claim a tab's id. Check which of the two Policy uses.
8. [note] `Policy.kind()` reads registry.json from disk on every message check (policy.js `registered_external`), and `External.route()` runs `cards.fold()` on every fresh prompt on every card (External.js:416). Both are fine at today's traffic. A small in-memory set of external ids would make both checks free.
9. [note] External rows are buried as "gone" when Servex restarts (External.js:315-324), so a tab has to call `register_session` again. The skill text asks tabs to re-arm their Monitor every turn but never tells them to re-register. Add that one line to servex-mastermind/SKILL.md and every-prompt/SKILL.md, or a restart will silently cut off every tab.
10. [note] Simpler: Layers.js grew by about 900 lines. `page_path`, `context`, `card_of`, `path_of` and `inside` each map between card ids and page paths separately. If a card were always keyed by its page path (`/framework/ai/<card>/`), most of that branching would go away. Worth weighing before more callers depend on the two key shapes.

# Phone load, before and after — the card page in `experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa`

Same page both times: `/framework/ai2/2026/09/29/experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa/`, on
the live site (`http://monorepo.localhost`), headless Chrome throttled with Chrome DevTools'
own official network presets. 3 runs each, median reported (raw runs are in `task.jsonl`).

| Throttle | When | ms to table | Bytes | `directory.json` fetched? | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fast 3G | Before | never in 90s (borderline ~75–95s across repeat tries — see below) | 1.54 MB | No | not tracked |
| Fast 3G | After | never in 90s, same as before | 1.55 MB | No | 422 |
| Wi-Fi-like | Before | 1.7s | 9.6 MB | **Yes**, ~530 KB | not tracked |
| Wi-Fi-like | After | 1.4–1.7s (about the same) | 14.1–17.4 MB (**up**, not down) | **No** | 1,321–2,197 (very high, and swings a lot run to run) |

## The one-sentence read

`directory.json` is gone from this page's load (the goal), but it has been replaced by well
over a thousand small `page.jsonl` requests on Wi-Fi and 422 on Fast 3G — more total bytes on
Wi-Fi, not fewer, and the Fast 3G table still never appears inside 90 seconds, unchanged from
before.

## Detail

- **Fast 3G "never in 90s" is real, not a probe bug.** A follow-up diagnostic (screenshot every
  15s) showed the table missing at 15/30/45/60s and present by 75s/90s in one run — so the true
  number is borderline, around 75–95 seconds, not literally infinite. It did not get better after
  the merge; both before and after time out the same way at the 90s mark used here.
- **Why Fast 3G is slow, both before and after:** at the 90s mark, roughly 150 tiny requests were
  still pending — one `page.jsonl` per `ai/` task folder, plus a few `.js` module files.
  Fast 3G's 562.5ms round-trip latency, multiplied across hundreds of small sequential requests
  competing for a handful of connections per origin, costs far more time than the bytes alone
  would suggest. (One pending entry, a long-lived `/api/stream` connection, is not part of this —
  it's a stream that never finishes by design.)
- **The AFTER request count is a flag, not a footnote.** Requests jumped from a single
  `directory.json` fetch to 422 (Fast 3G) and 1,300–2,200 (Wi-Fi-like, and quite unstable between
  runs) per page load, and Wi-Fi total bytes went UP by roughly 50–80%. That reads as this page
  eagerly fetching many folders' `page.jsonl` rather than only the one folder it needs "for
  free" plus loading deeper folders on demand, which was the whole point of the change (see the
  parent brief's shape, item 1: "not the sub-folders' contents"). Worth a look before calling this
  task's fix finished — it may be a page (this ai2 card view) that still walks the whole tree
  eagerly, rather than the `page.jsonl` mechanism itself being wrong.
- BEFORE's request count wasn't tracked (the probe didn't measure it until this AFTER run was
  requested with that column added), and the fix is already merged into the main site, so a true
  apples-to-apples BEFORE request count can no longer be taken. The diagnostic pass taken before
  the merge did already show on the order of 150+ small pending requests at Fast 3G's 90s mark,
  which is the same shape of problem, just not a matching total count.

## Method

Probe: `pfl-measure.mjs` (Playwright + CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`), in the session
scratchpad, not the repo. Presets used (Chrome DevTools' official values, since the earlier task
this reuses named "Fast 3G"/"Wi-Fi-like" but never actually ran or recorded numbers for them):

- Fast 3G: 1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up, 562.5 ms round-trip latency
- Wi-Fi-like: 30 Mbps down, 15 Mbps up, 2 ms round-trip latency

"ms to table" = time from navigation start until a `<table>` with more than one row is visible.
Full raw numbers, the diagnostic screenshots, and the Wi-Fi top-5-bytes breakdown are logged in
this task's `task.jsonl`.

# Nested tasks: parallel and series, with a picture that shows the flow

**Owner's words:** [owner-words.md](/framework/ai/2026/09/29/lifecycle-nothing-left-running-nested-ta/owner-words.md) (09-29, about 5:35 PM). Every sentence is traced in [../lifecycle/refine/coverage.md](../lifecycle/refine/coverage.md). This task covers items 5–10 of [../lifecycle/refine/brief.md](../lifecycle/refine/brief.md). The sibling task `lifecycle` covers the rest.

## What the owner asked
- A task can have **subtasks, to any depth**. Completion % **aggregates from the subtasks**.
- **Parallel and series, mixed.** For example, phase 1 is N tasks in parallel, and phase 2 (itself parallel) starts once they're all done. In other words, dependencies.
- **Each spawned mastermind session is automatically a task**, and its minions are its subtasks. (The owner offered this as a suggestion. Build it; it's the natural source of the tree.)
- **The visual** must make clear whether a set of tasks runs in parallel or in series, how it all flows, what's in flight, what it's waiting on, and the %. The owner: "I'm not sure exactly how those should look". So try two or three designs as live demos, pick one, and show the alternatives one click down.

## Build on what exists
- The data is task.jsonl. spawn_agent's `task: {dir}` already opens a child's log, and `parent` links agents. Add `parent_task` and `after: [task ids]` (the series edges) to line 1, and derive the tree. Don't invent a second store.
- The view goes in `ext/AITask` (the task.jsonl viewer), with the item/tree work from task-mastermind-item-ui (landed 09-29): [Item](/framework/ui/item/) icon rows, [DefaultView](/framework/ux/Content/Object/), `core/Page/object.js`.
- `%` for a leaf is its step/steps (the task.jsonl `step` field). For a parent, it's the weighted mean of its children, and landed = 100.
- Coordinate with `lifecycle`: it logs agent and task start/end. Read that log if it has landed; don't duplicate it.
- **Minions write into their parent's log:** page-system found a page_work minion's steps written into its own task.jsonl (17:36), so its ledger showed "step 2 of 7", which wasn't its plan. Each minion gets its own task dir as a subtask; a parent never shares its log.

## Deliverables
1. The data rule (parent_task, after) written by spawn_agent, and by the sub-mastermind skill for hand-spawned minions.
2. A live tree of today's real tasks (09-29 has several masterminds with minions), showing parallel vs series, in flight, waiting on, and %.
3. A demo page with a made-up two-phase plan (phase 1: three parallel, phase 2: two parallel after them), routed, at 1280 and 1920.
4. One doc page on the model, linked from ext/AITask's readme.

## Fence
The files are `public/framework/ext/AITask/**`, the task-opening code in Servex (the spawn_agent `task` option) for the two new fields only, and `.claude/skills/sub-mastermind/SKILL.md` for one line.
Stay out of Servex/Heartbeat.js and the lifecycle reaper.
Use a worktree and `Server/merge.mjs`. Load the `page` skill before the view.

## Done means
The owner opens the AITask view and sees today's tasks as a tree, and can tell at a glance which ran in parallel, which waited, what's in flight, and the %.

# File system: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`; the first two-thirds are about files.

Start from what exists:
- `ext/files` (`files.js`, `fs.js`) — the file explorer, landed 09-28 with Panels removed, a real tree and `<path>/fs`. Walkthrough: /framework/ai/2026-09-28/file-explorer-fs/walkthrough/
- the class-doc Files tab (`ext/Doc`)
- the AI 2 card folders (`Log.js` `draw_folder()`)

## Asks
1. **Audit, briefly:** what file and directory data structures exist today (in fs.js? in directory.json?), where each file UI lives, and what's duplicated. As a table.
2. **The data first, then the UX.** Clear classes, named with the `naming` skill: e.g. `File` and `Directory` (a path, a name, children, and read, fetch and render), plus a tree built from them. A file's default view is an icon item. Decide whether this becomes a new ext (e.g. `ext/fs`, "file system") that ext/files' UI sits on, or whether ext/files grows. Keep ext/files' current users working.
3. **Operations,** as far as the static site allows (reads everywhere; writes only through the dev server on localhost): read, fetch, render, and a right-click context menu (copy path, open in /fs, open raw).

6. **Every system page links its files** through this (page-system's pages, the Servex docs).

Keep v1 of the explorer reachable. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test with links followed, merge.mjs, a fresh-eyes review, and screenshots at 1920, 3440 and 400. At most 3 minions; budget about $12. | What | Where | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

| What the reader sees | Where | Built on |
|---|---|---|

| `<any path>/fs/`, full screen, no site nav | [ext/files/fs.js](/framework/ext/files/) via `Page.fs_folder()` in [core/Page](/framework/core/Page/) | `files()` + `/directory.json` |
| A module's **Files** tab (tree, prose, source) | [ext/Doc](/framework/ext/Doc/) `Doc.js` | `files(…, { about })`, plus an "Open full screen" link to `/fs/` |
| An AI 2 card's folder | [core/Page/Log.js](/framework/core/Page/) `draw_folder()` (card.js calls it) | `files()` |
| Workspace documents | [ext/Panel/Workspace](/framework/ext/Panel/Workspace/) `documents.js` | FileSaver; saved panel layouts, not files |
| Icon items and trees (being built) | `ui/item`, branch `worktree/item-ui` | details/summary rows |

# Each page lists its own files in its page.jsonl: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`. Today one giant `directory.json` (3.3 MB) lists the whole site. Every page fetches it, and on the phone it costs seconds (see card 2026/09/29/experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa).

## The shape the owner wants
1. **Each folder's page.jsonl lists that folder's own entries:** one line per file or subfolder DIRECTLY inside it, e.g. `{"file": "readme.md"}` / `{"dir": "doc"}`. Not the sub-folders' contents; they're in the sub-folders' own page.jsonl. So loading a page gets its listing for free, and deeper levels load on demand.
2. **Changes APPEND:** when the dev server's watcher (Server/watch.js, Server/plugins/Directory.js) sees a file or folder added, append `{"file": "x"}`; when one is removed, append `{"removed": "x"}` (latest line wins). Never rewrite the file.
3. **A backfill:** a one-time node script writes the current listing into each folder's page.jsonl. Decide which folders get one (every folder under public/ except dated task folders, node_modules and assets?), weighing the "don't clutter the tree" concern. Propose the rule, then apply it.
4. **Readers switch over:** core/Page (Log.js already reads `{"file"}` lines), core/Page/Markdown.js, ai2/groups.js, ext/files/fs.js, the drawer's sessions.js walk, and the Router's children lookup read the page's own page.jsonl, falling back to directory.json while it still exists. Keep directory.json for now, and stop depending on it for rendering.

## Traps (these have burned us)
- **The watcher must IGNORE its own writes** to page.jsonl, or it loops. Also: on Windows, a READ fires a change event (memory: "reload-on-read"), so filter by real content change.
- **Concurrent appends:** use the append path (Servex /card/append or the dev server's append), never read-modify-write.
- **Live reload:** hold it during the backfill (`node Server/hold.mjs on "page-files-log backfill"`).

## Rules

# Each page lists its own files in its page.jsonl: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`. Today one giant `directory.json` (3.3 MB) lists the whole site. Every page fetches it, and on the phone it costs seconds (see card 2026/09/29/experiment-3-models-read-the-dictate-spa).

## The shape the owner wants
1. **Each folder's page.jsonl lists that folder's own entries:** one line per file or subfolder DIRECTLY inside it, e.g. `{"file": "readme.md"}` / `{"dir": "doc"}`. Not the sub-folders' contents; they're in the sub-folders' own page.jsonl. So loading a page gets its listing for free, and deeper levels load on demand.
2. **Changes APPEND:** when the dev server's watcher (Server/watch.js, Server/plugins/Directory.js) sees a file or folder added, append `{"file": "x"}`; when one is removed, append `{"removed": "x"}` (latest line wins). Never rewrite the file.
3. **A backfill:** a one-time node script writes the current listing into each folder's page.jsonl. Decide which folders get one (every folder under public/ except dated task folders, node_modules and assets?), weighing the "don't clutter the tree" concern. Propose the rule, then apply it.
4. **Readers switch over:** core/Page (Log.js already reads `{"file"}` lines), core/Page/Markdown.js, ai2/groups.js, ext/files/fs.js, the drawer's sessions.js walk, and the Router's children lookup read the page's own page.jsonl, falling back to directory.json while it still exists. Keep directory.json for now, and stop depending on it for rendering.

## Traps (these have burned us)
- **The watcher must IGNORE its own writes** to page.jsonl, or it loops. Also: on Windows, a READ fires a change event (memory: "reload-on-read"), so filter by real content change.
- **Concurrent appends:** use the append path (Servex /card/append or the dev server's append), never read-modify-write.
- **Live reload:** hold it during the backfill (`node Server/hold.mjs on "page-files-log backfill"`).

# Is Servex project-aware?

**Mostly not yet.** The proxy, the ports and dev-server supervision already work per project. Almost everything else (cards, the assistants, the page AI, worktrees, the task loop) is wired to the monorepo through one `REPO` constant or a `public/framework/ai` path. And today Servex can't even tell which project a request came from: the monorepo's `ServexProxy.js:57` deletes the `host` header before forwarding.

| Area | Per project today? | What's wired to the monorepo |
|---|---|---|
| Project list, ports, proxy, dev servers, their logs | **yes** | only the scan root `C:/Code` (`Servex.js:73`) |
| Health, the monitor, Whisper | machine-wide, which is right | — |
| Usage bars | no | writes `public/framework/ai/usage.json`; it's machine data, so it belongs in Servex's home |
| Cards and card routes | no | `cards/Cards.js:22`, a fixed `public/framework/ai` root |
| Prompt log, dispatcher | no | one global `prompts` log (`Servex.js:132`) |
| Fast assistant, page AI (Layers), global mastermind | no | `cwd: REPO`, monorepo skills and groups files (`Assistant.js:7`, `Layers.js:10`, `Global.js:17`) |
| Agent spawns | partly | follows `cwd` if given, otherwise defaults to Servex's own folder |
| Worktree pool, lifecycle reaper, task loop | no | `Pool.js:40` finds the repo from Servex's own git; `Lifecycle.js` imports `Server/*.mjs` |
| Experts, readme chain, pages | no | `experts.json:10`, `readme-chain.js:29`, `pages.js:8` |
| Socket, `/ask/turn` | per project by construction | they live in each site's own dev server (`Server/plugins/`), not in Servex |

## Decisions

1. **Key everything by the request's Host.** Host → project name (`ReverseProxy.name`, `:91`) → project root (`servex.project(name).dir`). The Servex socket and every voice session take that root, so project A's transcriptions and sessions are saved under A's folder and can never mix with B's. To make this possible, `ServexProxy.js` stops deleting `host` and sets `x-forwarded-host`, and Servex trusts that header only from loopback.
2. **One Servex process hosts every project's agents, for now.** The owner is right: one memory gate, one monitor and one queue see the whole machine, and the fans are a machine problem. Split later only if one project's agents starve another's.
3. **One seam replaces the `REPO` constant:** `servex.project(host).root`, plus a small per-project config (`.servex.json`: where cards live, which skills to use). Cards, assistants, Layers, the pool and the task loop each take a root instead of importing one.

## For a new site to "just start working"

- [ ] It has a `package.json` under `C:/Code` (Servex finds it and gives it `<name>.localhost`).
- [ ] It loads the framework's shell (dictation, the ✦ rail and the drawer come from `/framework/`), or includes the one `<script>` that does.
- [ ] Servex reads its Host and resolves its root (decision 1).
- [ ] Its cards go to `<root>/ai/` (from `.servex.json`, or that default).
- [ ] Its agents spawn with `cwd = <root>`, so the SDK loads that project's own CLAUDE.md and skills. With none, they fall back to the framework's.
- [ ] A worktree pool is created lazily for it, the first time a task asks.
- [ ] A smoke test proves it: dictate a line on `<new>.localhost`, and see it land in that site's session file, not the monorepo's.

1. [fix] Item 4 ("don't respond while the owner is still talking") only exists on the sending side. Nothing reads `floor` yet: `Servex/agents/Assistant.js:92` calls `heard()` on every `type: "prompt"` and answers at once. The captured run shows this: `c-cues/posted-pause.json` posts a `"floor": "speaking"` prompt, and today the assistant would answer it straight away. Servex was outside the minion's fence, so the fix may be a handoff to voice-sessions rather than more code here. [fix] Item 5 ("audio cues to the fast model") has the same gap. `Assistant.words()` (`Servex/agents/Assistant.js:114`) builds the model's input from `sentences`/`text` only, so the model never sees `entry.cues`. A message typed straight after the mic goes off also gets that session's cues, because `mic_on_at` is only cleared inside `stamp()`. Anything that adds up pause time across entries will double-count it. Either say in `floor.md` that the next entry carries the closed version, or set `quiet_since` so the closed version starts where the open one was cut off.

# smoke-uncommitted — minion brief

Load the `minion` skill first. Parent: task-mastermind-node-reliability-2. Log in this dir's task.jsonl.

## The owner's words
"smoke.mjs (run by merge.mjs) follows links from /framework/ai2/ into card dirs that exist only UNCOMMITTED in the main tree, so every worktree merge fails on them with "Page Load Error" (mastermind-page, today). Make smoke report such a target as "skipped: exists uncommitted in the main tree" instead of failing, and while you are there make merge.mjs refuse a Git-Bash-mangled page path (one containing "Program Files/Git/") with a message naming MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1."

## Fence
Work ONLY in the worktree `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/node-reliability` (branch `worktree/node-reliability`). Files: `Server/smoke.mjs`, `Server/merge.mjs`, and `Server/doc/` lines about them. Nothing else. Never edit the main tree C:/Code/lew42/monorepo.

## Deliverables
1. `smoke.mjs`: when a loaded url fails (any error), map its pathname to a dir under `public/` (e.g. `/framework/ai/2026-09-28/x/` → `public/framework/ai/2026-09-28/x/`). If that dir (or its page.js / page.jsonl) does NOT exist in the worktree but DOES exist in the MAIN tree (the repo that holds smoke.mjs: `path.resolve(here, "..")`) as untracked or modified there (`git -C <main> status --porcelain -- <that dir>` non-empty), print `skip <url>  (skipped: exists uncommitted in the main tree)` and do not count its errors. Apply it to followed links and canaries alike. Keep it cheap: one git call per failing url only.
2. `merge.mjs`: before anything else (before taking the lock), if any path argument contains `Program Files/Git/` (either slash), exit 1 with: `refused: "<arg>" was rewritten by Git Bash. Rerun as MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 node Server/merge.mjs ...`. (smoke.mjs's own strip stays.)
3. Proof in `proof.txt` here: (a) smoke run against a url whose dir is uncommitted in the main tree only, e.g. one of `git -C C:/Code/lew42/monorepo status --short | grep '^??' | grep framework/ai/` dirs that has a page.js → shows `skip`; (b) a url that truly 404s still FAILs; (c) `node Server/merge.mjs C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/node-reliability "C:/Program Files/Git/framework/ai2/" --dry-run` → refused message. Run smoke against the worktree's own dev server: start it DETACHED with windowsHide (`node Server/worktree-up.mjs`'s start logic, or `PORT=61687 node server.js` from the worktree root, backgrounded) and KILL it when done. Use `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for every Git Bash call that passes a /path.
4. Update the header comments of both files (one short paragraph each). Commit in the worktree by exact path. Do not merge; report done to your parent.

Budget: $3. Sonnet. No new npm deps. Every process you spawn: windowsHide.

# Minion: audio/ down to three tools, and one live demo

Load the `minion`, `code` and `page` skills first. The owner's words and the full ask: [../requirements.md](../requirements.md) (read it all). Card dir: `public/framework/ai/2026/09/29/audio-a-library-of-audio-parts-transcrip/`.

**Work in the worktree only:** `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\audio-consolidate` (branch `worktree/audio-consolidate`, its server at http://localhost:53292/). Commit there by exact path. Never touch the main tree `C:\Code\lew42\monorepo` except your own task.jsonl.

## Fence (phase 1)
`public/framework/audio/**` only. NOT `ux/Dictate/` or `ext/drawer/` — another minion is fixing those right now; Dictate is phase 2, you will be woken for it.

## Deliverables (phase 1)
1. **MicStream absorbs MicPicker, LevelMeter and PushToTalk.** Device choice becomes a MicStream setting; level becomes a value MicStream's View shows (the meter bar); push-to-talk becomes a `mode` (`hold` | `toggle`). One class, parts as static subclasses (the `code` skill). Find every caller of the three old classes (`grep -r` across `public/`) and move it. The old classes become thin aliases re-exporting from MicStream, or are removed once nothing imports them.
2. **Keep v1 reachable.** The current /framework/audio/ index and the old part pages stay clickable under `/framework/audio/v1/` (declared in `children:`), so the owner can compare.
3. **ONE live demo at the top of /framework/audio/**: pick a mic, see the level move, hold-to-talk or toggle, the transcript appears (partial grey → settled), optionally record and play back. Every part visibly doing its job, each part's live state View beside it (MicStream, Recorder, Transcriber). Level 1 = the demo, then the three tools as icon tiles, one click to each. Transcriber: use the existing engines (Whisper | Chrome); don't change their internals beyond what MicStream needs.
4. **Readme**: the three tools, the web API each wraps (getUserMedia + AudioWorklet/AnalyserNode, MediaRecorder, Whisper server / SpeechRecognition), and a small diagram of how Dictate will assemble them (MicStream → Transcriber, Recorder optional). Update each tool's readme and `doc/`.

## Proof
- Headless Playwright with a fake media stream (`--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream --use-fake-device-for-media-stream`) against http://localhost:53292/framework/audio/: the level value moves, hold mode starts/stops, the Recorder produces a blob. Scripts go in your session scratchpad, named `audio-*.mjs`.
- Zero console errors on /framework/audio/, /framework/audio/v1/, and every tool page.
- Screenshots at 400 and 1920 of /framework/audio/, into this dir (`shot-400.png`, `shot-1920.png`). Open them and judge them.
- Every process you spawn: `windowsHide: true`. Stop anything you start.

## Budget
Sonnet, about $3. Log steps and decisions in your task.jsonl as you go. When phase 1 is committed and proven, end your turn with a 5-line summary (what moved, callers changed, proof paths) and wait — do not merge; I merge.

# budget-heartbeat — minion brief

Load the `minion` skill first. Parent: task-mastermind-node-reliability-2. Log in this dir's task.jsonl.

## The owner's words
Today: "Budgets enforced by the heartbeat (draft in draft/): a task's dollar cap from its brief or task.jsonl; at the cap the heartbeat stops spawning for it and the parent is told once."
From the brief (requirements.md 20:35, one dir up): "At 100%, it messages the mastermind once: 'budget reached: land what you have, or write in task.jsonl why you need more, and how much'. At 150%, it stops the task's minions (not the mastermind, so it can still land) and posts a line on card live. A brief without a budget gets a default by role."

## Fence
Worktree `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/node-reliability` only (branch `worktree/node-reliability`). Files: new `Servex/Budget.js`, `Servex/Heartbeat.js` (one hook), `Servex/Servex.js` (spawn refusal only), `Servex/doc/` one new `budget.md` + one line in `Servex/readme.md`. Never edit the main tree C:/Code/lew42/monorepo. Never restart the real Servex.

## Start from
The draft one dir up: `draft/Budget.js` and `draft/heartbeat-budget.diff` (read them; they already do cost/budget/100%/150% and the once-only log lines).

## Deliverables
1. Land the draft as `Servex/Budget.js` + the Heartbeat hook.
2. **Stops spawning at the cap (missing from the draft).** At >= 100% a spawn whose `parent` is the task's owner, or any live descendant of it, is REFUSED (not queued: a queued spawn would wait forever) with the reason `budget: <slug> spent $X of $Y — land, or raise budget_usd in task.jsonl`. Hook it where `spawn()` consults `same_as`/`admit` in `Servex/Servex.js`; Budget keeps an in-memory set of over-cap owners refreshed each sweep (and computed on first need after a restart). A spawn with no parent, or the owner itself being revived, is not refused. A raised `budget_usd` lifts it on the next sweep.
3. **The parent is told once.** At 100% tell the owner (draft text) AND the owner's own parent agent (from the agents registry), each once; the `{"log":{"budget":"reached"}}` line is the memory.
4. Proof in `proof.txt` here: a scratch run with `SERVEX_HOME=<temp dir> SERVEX_PORT=18090 SERVEX_PROXY_PORT=18080 SERVEX_PROXY_INTERNAL=18079 SERVEX_NO_GATE=1 SERVEX_NO_ASSISTANT=1 SERVEX_NO_POOL=1`, or a pure node script calling Budget's exported functions with a fake agents object — show: (a) under cap nothing happens; (b) at 100% owner + parent told, one log line, and a second sweep adds nothing; (c) a child spawn of the owner is refused with the reason; (d) raising budget_usd lifts the refusal; (e) at 150% descendants stopped, owner not. Also boot the scratch Servex once and `GET /agents` to prove it starts; kill it. Every process: windowsHide.
5. `Servex/doc/budget.md`: what it does, the three rules, how to raise a budget, 20 lines at most. Commit by exact path in the worktree. Do not merge. End your turn with a 5-line report.

Budget: $5. Sonnet. No new npm deps.

Load the `minion` skill first. Parent: task-mastermind-node-reliability-2. Log in this dir's task.jsonl.

## The owner's words
"Pool cleanup and prune: 70 worktrees; prune every worktree whose branch is fully merged into michael/dev and whose agent is stopped or gone; take_worktree must work again."

Code: worktree `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/node-reliability` only: `Servex/Pool.js` (salvage ~line 215, baseline/dirt ~384), `Server/worktree-down.mjs`, `Server/worktree-sweep.mjs`, new `Server/worktree-prune.mjs`, their docs (`Server/doc/`, `Servex/doc/`). Never `--force`, never delete a branch that isn't merged, never `git stash/reset`. Also drop its `.worktrees.json` entry and Servex pool slot if one exists. Print one line per worktree: `pruned` / `skip: <reason>`.
2. Same log-noise rule in `Pool.js` return/salvage and `worktree-down.mjs`.
3. Find WHY `take_worktree` says the pool is full (read Pool.js; likely a cap counted over all worktrees or dead holders) and fix it so it works after the prune. Proof = the fix's reasoning in one line + (after merge, the parent will call take_worktree).
4. Proof in `proof.txt`: the `--dry` output, then a real run's output, `git worktree list | wc -l` before and after. Do the real run ONLY on the main tree's worktrees with the script from YOUR worktree (`node C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/node-reliability/Server/worktree-prune.mjs --root C:/Code/lew42/monorepo` or equivalent). Commit code by exact path in your worktree. Do not merge. End with a 5-line report.

Budget: $5. Sonnet. Every process: windowsHide. Use MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 in Git Bash for /paths.

# Icon system: one way to size, frame and lay out icons: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md`; read them in full. Suspected: too many custom implementations of icon layout CSS, and vertical alignment keeps breaking.

## Asks
1. **An audit** (cheap Sonnet or Haiku minions): every icon use on the site (Material Icons; the `icon()` factory and its callers), and the CSS that lays each out: padding on the icon or its parent, width and height, line-height, vertical-align or flex alignment, and background and hover. Group them into patterns, and count the one-off implementations. As a table, with screenshots of the misaligned ones.
2. **The facts first:** are Material Icons fixed width? When does an icon need a FRAME (a fixed em-sized box, centred both ways), and when not? The frame's size must come from the font size (em), so increasing the container's font size scales the icon, the frame and the padding together.
3. **One system, with a demo of each** (reuse ui/ and item-ui's icon items; keep new CSS minimal):
   - an icon alone (no frame / framed);
   - an icon BUTTON: flush (no background), with a background, a hover background, and a TOGGLE (on = lit background, off = dim);
   - a RAIL of icon buttons, mixed flush and backed;
   - ICON ITEMS in a list: with and without a background. With a background it needs padding; without one, gap only. The hover background's EDGE must line up with the parent's edges and padding.
   Everything aligned vertically and horizontally at 3 font sizes.
4. **Migrate the worst offenders** to the system (the top one-offs from the audit); list the rest.
5. A short "icons" section in the css skill (through the Servex architect; send it the text).

## Rules
Keep v1 reachable. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test, merge.mjs, one fresh reviewer, and screenshots at 400 and 1920. At most 2 minions; budget about $12, hard. Coordinate with task-mastermind-item-ui's icon items (it has landed; build on it).
