# Icon facts — measured, not guessed

Every claim below was checked by running code, not by reading the CSS and assuming. The
script is [`measure-icons.mjs`](#how-this-was-measured) at the bottom of this page.

## 1. Material Icons ARE fixed-width — every glyph is a perfect square

**Check:** loaded the real site (`/framework/ui/item/`, which already pulls in the real
Material Icons `.woff2` the same way every page does — `core/App/Font.js`), then rendered
10 different icon names (`description`, `folder`, `arrow_forward`, `more_vert`, `close`,
`check`, `mic`, `settings`, `search`, `menu`) at `font-size: 24px; line-height: 1`, and
read `getBoundingClientRect()` on each.

**Result:** all 10 came back **exactly 24×24px** — width equal to height equal to the
font size, no variation between a wide glyph (`arrow_forward`) and a narrow one
(`close`). This is by design: Material Icons ships every glyph on a fixed 24×24 grid, so
**the font itself is monospaced for icons** the way a monospace font is for letters.

**What this means:** you never need to fix an icon's width by hand (a `width: 1em` some
callers add, e.g. `dropdown.css:82`, `Panel/toolbar.css:123`, `item.js`'s `.item-icon`,
is not wrong, just unnecessary for width alone — see the FRAME section below for why you
still might want it).

## 2. The icon's own box is exactly the font size; `line-height` changes the LINE, not the glyph

**Check:** same render, compared `line-height: 1` against `line-height: normal` on the
same 10 glyphs.

**Result:** the icon's own `getBoundingClientRect()` height did not change between the
two — still 24px either way. `line-height` on an inline element doesn't resize *that
element's* box; it resizes the invisible "line box" the browser builds around every
inline run on that line (glyph + surrounding text together). `framework.css`'s
`.icon { line-height: 1; }` (`framework.css:562`) exists to stop the icon from *quietly
inflating that shared line box* to whatever the icon font's own line metrics are — not to
resize the icon itself, which was already exactly 1em.

## 3. An icon does NOT sit centred against adjacent text by default — it needs a nudge or a frame

**Check:** built a row of plain text, a Material Icon (`line-height: 1`), and more plain
text, all at the same font size, and compared the icon's box against the row's own line
box.

**Result:** the icon (24px tall) sits flush with the TOP of the row's line box (28px
tall, from the text's own `line-height: normal`, ≈1.15). Its bottom lands about 4px
*above* the row's bottom edge — i.e., a plain icon reads as sitting slightly high and
looking disconnected from the baseline the letters sit on.

**This is exactly the bug the owner described** ("the vertical alignment is often a
problem"), and it is why real call sites hand-patch it — the one found in this audit is
`imagine/paging/paging.css:1020`:
`.paging-expand-head .icon { vertical-align: -0.15em; }` — a hand-tuned nudge, marked
`/* control */`, that exists only because the default position is wrong. It is a
symptom, not a fix others can reuse: the next caller has to rediscover the same offset.

## 4. When an icon needs a FRAME, and when it doesn't

A **frame** is a fixed square box (in `em`, so it scales with the container's font size)
that the icon is centred inside, both ways — `display: grid; place-items: center;` (or
flex) on a box sized `width/height: 1.3em` or similar, NOT on the icon itself.

**Needs a frame:**
- **A button that is only an icon** (no visible label) — a frame gives it a real click
  target bigger than the glyph's own ink, and centres the glyph inside that target both
  ways. `ui/item/item.js`'s `.item-caret, .item-icon` already does exactly this —
  `width: 1.3em; aspect-ratio: 1; display: grid; place-items: center; line-height: 1;`
  — and it's the cleanest example on the site today. Copy this, don't reinvent it.
- **A row of icon+label items that must line up in a column** (a file tree, a menu) —
  the frame is what makes every icon's right edge (where the label starts) land on the
  same x no matter how wide that particular glyph visually looks, and it reserves the
  same width for a caret/fold triangle so leaves and branches still line up
  (`item.js`'s own comment explains this: "a leaf next to a folder... lines its icon up
  with its sibling's").
- **A toggle / lit button** (the owner's "on = lit, off = dim" idea) — the lit background
  needs a fixed box to fill; you can't apply a background to a bare inline glyph and get
  a clean edge.

**Doesn't need a frame:**
- **An icon inline with text it's labelling** (a link, a menu row's own label, a
  breadcrumb) — here the fix is the small vertical-align nudge (fact 3), not a frame; a
  frame would add unwanted extra width before the label. Most of the one-offs in this
  audit (`.page-crumbs .icon`, `.page-related-link .icon`, `.omnibox-card .icon`, etc.)
  are this case and just set `font-size`, correctly.

**Frame size, in em:** `1.3em` square is what `item.js` already uses and reads well; the
Panel toolbar's icon-only button frame (`Panel/toolbar.css:103`) uses `1.7em`, sized for
a bigger click target. Recommend **picking one of these as the site default** (probably
`1.3em` for an inline icon-item, a bigger one like `1.6`–`1.7em` for a standalone icon
BUTTON that needs a generous tap target) rather than the current spread of ad hoc
numbers. Because both are `em`, raising the container's `font-size` scales the icon, the
frame, and any padding around it together — which is the exact "cascade through" the
owner asked for.

## How this was measured

[`measure-icons.mjs`](measure-icons.mjs) — a headless Playwright script (never drives

# Streamed input: what Chat does today, and what it would take

**Today, nothing you are saying reaches the chat until it is sent.** While you talk, Whisper's growing guess is written into the text box only (`ext/Chat/Mic.js`, re-guessed every `guess_ms`, 0.9 s). The box sends by itself at a natural pause: 2.5 s of quiet after a finished sentence (`paragraph_pause_ms`), or 2.5 s of silence (`pause_send_ms`), with long stretches cut at 1200 characters or 60 s. Only then does one owner line land in the log, and only then do the assistants hear it. So on a phone, the words sit in the box, which is why the box felt like the whole screen.

**What streaming would take, in three small pieces (not built here; it is more than small):**

1. **The line shape already exists.** A chat line with the same `at` and `fix: true` replaces the earlier words in place (`ext/Chat/Chat.js`, `chat_line()`). The desktop AI tab already streams the assistant's replies this way. The owner's words could do the same: post a first line as soon as there are words, then `fix` lines with the same `at` as the guess grows, and a final one at the pause.
2. **Mic.js** would post those draft lines through a new `on_draft(text, at)` next to `deliver()`, and clear the box as soon as the first draft is in the log, so the words move from the box into the chat bubble while you speak.
3. **Servex** (`Servex/agents/Sessions.js`) would need a `draft` verb that writes the line but does NOT wake the assistants; only the final line (today's `say`) wakes them. Without that, every guess would cost two agent turns.

Roughly one task: Mic.js plus one Servex verb plus a restart, and a proof that no draft wakes an agent.

+# The rules: when to frame an icon, and which class for what
+
+The owner's own words: "I don't think necessarily every icon needs a frame... so just look
+into that and figure out... show examples of either way."
+
+## Is Material Icons fixed width?
+
+**Yes.** Material Icons is a ligature font — `icon("star")` prints the literal word "star" and
+the font swaps a glyph in for it — and every glyph in it is drawn inside the same 24×24 advance
+box, however much of that box the ink actually fills. So two icons sitting side by side, with no
+frame at all, already share the same width and already line up horizontally. That fact rules
+out the single biggest reason someone reaches for a frame ("so the icons line up") — they
+already do.
+
+## So when does a frame earn its place?
+
+Three real reasons, and a frame should exist only when one of them is true for the icon in
+question:
+
+1. **A click target.** A glyph alone renders at whatever `font-size` it inherited — often
+   smaller than the roughly 2em (32px at a 16px base) that a pointer or a thumb wants to aim at.
+   The frame is the square box that gives the click/tap area its real size, and it is also
+   where a background and a hover live, because a bare `<span>` has nowhere for either to sit
+   without changing the glyph itself.
+2. **Vertical centring against something taller.** The icon's own `line-height: 1` (in
+   `.icon`, framework.css) keeps it from growing whatever line box it sits in, but it does
+   nothing to CENTRE the glyph inside a taller box around it — a button, a list row. That
+   centring is `place-items: center` on the frame, not a property of the icon.
+3. **A consistent box in a grid of them.** A rail or toolbar where every slot has to measure
+   the same width — so a glyph that visually looks lighter or heavier still sits in a column
+   that lines up with its neighbours' boxes, not just their glyphs.
+
+An icon riding inline with a sentence ("★ Starred") needs **none** of these — it is not a click
+target, it is not centred against anything taller than itself, and it is not one slot in a grid.
+That case keeps using plain `.icon`, unframed, exactly as before this task.
+
+## The one token: `--icon-frame`
+
+`--icon-frame: 1.6em` is declared once, in `framework.css`, right beside `.icon`'s own
+`font-size: 1.25em` — both rules read the same ancestor's font-size, which is what makes
+`.ui-icon-frame` and `.ui-icon-btn` scale together with the glyph when a container's font-size
+changes (the page's "three sizes" demo proves this live: 14px, 18px, 28px containers, same
+markup, everything scales). 1.6em leaves visible room for a background and padding around the
+1.25em glyph without the frame crowding it.
+
+`ui/item`'s own tree-row frame (`.item-icon`, `.item-caret`) is a **tighter** 1.3em — a row read
+many-in-a-column wants the icon closer to the name beside it than a standalone button does. That
+was a deliberate, already-shipped choice (2026-09-29), not an inconsistency: two different
+contexts, two different numbers, both derived from the same underlying idea. A later pass could
+point `.item-icon` at `--icon-frame` too with an override, but that edit is outside this task's
+fence (`public/framework/ui/item/` was not touched).
+
+## Which class for what
+
+| Need | Class |
+|---|---|
+| An icon riding inline with text | `.icon` (unchanged, no frame) |
+| An icon alone, needing a visible frame | `.ui-icon-frame` |
+| A clickable icon, no background until hover | `.ui-icon-btn` |
+| A clickable icon that should already read as its own surface | `.ui-icon-btn.ui-icon-btn-bg` |
+| An on/off icon button | `.ui-icon-btn` + `aria-pressed="true"/"false"`, toggled on click |
+| A row of icon buttons, some flush, some backed | `.ui-icon-rail` around any mix of the above |
+| An icon beside a name in a list | `ui.item({ icon, name, … })` — a different module, not this one |
+
+## Migrated (this task's second pass, after the audit)
+
+- **The inline-alignment bug** (facts.md §3: an icon sits ~4px high against the text beside
+  it) is now fixed ONCE, in `.icon` itself (`framework.css`, `vertical-align: -0.15em`) —
+  the exact value one real caller, `imagine/paging/paging.css:1020`, had already hand-tuned.
+  That caller's own nudge is deleted; it now inherits the shared default. `vertical-align`
+  only ever moves an inline box against surrounding text, so every frame/button that
+  centres its icon with `place-items`/`align-items` (this module's own, `ui/item`'s,
+  Panel's) was never touched by the old per-caller nudges and is not touched by this
+  change either.
+- **`ext/Panel`'s duplicate stylesheet** (audit one-off #2: `toolbar.css` and
+  `controls.css` carried a byte-for-byte identical `.panel-btn`/`.panel-bar`/`.panel-pop`
+  block, so a fix to one never reached the other) is deduplicated: `controls.css` is now
+  the one real copy (it is what `workspace.js`, the module's front door, loads);
+  `toolbar.css` is an empty stylesheet with a comment pointing at it. `.panel-btn` itself
+  was **not** rewired onto `.ui-icon-btn` — it already has the same flush/hover/lit-toggle
+  shape (built 2026-08-16, before this module existed), but also its own opacity-fade bar
+  reveal and `:has()` square detection that `.ui-icon-btn` has no reason to know about, and
+  it has real callers across the rail, a seam's menu, the drag grip and the inspector. A
+  full class swap risked exactly the "v1 behaviour unchanged" rule this task was given, for
+  a cosmetic win (one shared class name) this task's budget did not cover. `controls.css`
+  now says so, next to the rule.
+
+## Not migrated yet
+
+- **`core/App/mode.css`'s `.mode-btn`** — the floating mode-switch pill. Looked at it:
+  `position: fixed`, its own `border-radius: 999px` (a full circle, not `.ui-icon-btn`'s
+  `var(--radius)`), a drop shadow, and a background that is always on (never flush) with a
+  colour-only hover (not a fill change). That is four real differences from
+  `.ui-icon-btn.ui-icon-btn-bg`, not a rename — listed here rather than forced.
+- **`core/Search/Search.css`'s Omnibox** (`.omnibox-bar > .icon`, `.omnibox-card .icon`) —
+  its own pill padding, not checked against the vertical-align fix yet.
+- **`imagine/scenes/scenes.css`'s `.scene-bar`** — hides its icon glyph entirely
+  (`font-size: 0`) and fakes a `/` divider with CSS `content`. The audit's own read: this is
+  probably a "use `icon("chevron_right")` like everywhere else" fix, not a frame/button
+  question at all — worth a direct look before touching it.
+- **The hero-icon size variants** (`ext/AITask/nested.css`, `ux/Content/content.css`'s
+  `.w1`/`.w2`/`.w3`) — three near-identical big-display-size blocks that could share one
+  `--icon-hero` token. Low risk, cosmetic only; not touched.
+- `ui/item`'s own `.item-icon`/`.item-caret` frame (1.3em) — reused as-is in this page's list
+  demo, not rebuilt onto the shared `--icon-frame` token; a real edit, just outside this
+  task's fence (`public/framework/ui/item/` was not in it).
+- `ui.js` — the one-line import that would make `ui.icon` importable like `ui.item` is a
+  follow-up, not this fence.

+# icon — one frame, one button, one rail
+
+The owner's own words: too many one-off pieces of CSS building "icon layout" across the site,
+and vertical and horizontal alignment kept breaking. `ui/icon` is three classes that answer it,
+built around the `icon()` the site already has — nothing new to draw the glyph itself.
+
+## Use
+
+```js
+import { icon, button, div } from "/app.js";
+import "/framework/ui/icon/icon.js";   // registers the three classes; ui.js wiring is next
+
+div.c("ui-icon-frame", () => icon("star"));                       // framed, centred both ways
+button.c("ui-icon-btn", () => icon("favorite")).attr("type", "button");   // flush, clickable
+button.c("ui-icon-btn ui-icon-btn-bg", () => icon("home")).attr("type", "button"); // backed
+```
+
+A toggle button is the same `.ui-icon-btn`, with `aria-pressed` carrying the on/off state —
+"true" lights the background, "false" dims the icon. A rail is `.ui-icon-rail` around any mix of
+flush and backed buttons; it only supplies the gap between them. All three are sized in `em`,
+off the one token `--icon-frame` (declared beside `.icon` in `framework.css`), so raising a
+container's `font-size` scales the icon, the frame and the button together — see it live at
+three sizes on the page below.
+
+## Watch out
+
+- **Are Material Icons fixed width? Yes.** Every glyph in the font sits in the same 24×24
+  advance box, so two icons already line up horizontally with no help from a frame. A frame
+  earns its place for a click target, for vertical centring against something taller than the
+  glyph's own line box, or for a row where every slot — icon or not — has to measure the same.
+  [doc/icons.md](doc/icons.md) has the full reasoning.
+- **`.icon` itself gained one line: `vertical-align: -0.15em`.** Nothing renames or replaces it
+  — an icon riding inline with text still just wears `.icon` — but it now sits centred against
+  that text instead of ~4px high, the exact bug the owner named. `doc/icons.md` "Migrated" has
+  the measurement and the one real caller (`imagine/paging/`) whose own hand-tuned nudge this
+  replaced. A frame or a flex/grid button (this module's, `ui/item`'s, Panel's) was never
+  affected by that bug or this fix — `vertical-align` only moves an INLINE box.
+- **Icon items in a list are `ui/item`, not this module.** `ui.item({ icon, name, … })` already
+  has the row, the 1.3em tree-row frame and the `.boxed` background-with-padding look; this
+  page's list demo reuses it rather than building a second one.
+- **`ui.js` is not wired up yet.** This task's fence is this module, `framework.css`'s icon
+  block and `ui/page.js`'s `children:` — the one-line addition to `ui.js` that makes `ui.icon`
+  importable the way `ui.item` is happens in the next pass (the mastermind's migration step).
+  Until then, import `icon.js` directly, as the page itself does.
+
+## More
+
+- [Overview](/framework/ui/icon/) — the rail, the button range, the list, all three sizes side
+  by side.
+- [doc/icons.md](doc/icons.md) — fixed width or not, when a frame earns its place, the token.
+- Back to [UI](/framework/ui/).

# Icon facts — measured, not guessed

Every claim below was checked by running code, not by reading the CSS and assuming. The
script is [`measure-icons.mjs`](#how-this-was-measured) at the bottom of this page.

## 1. Material Icons ARE fixed-width — every glyph is a perfect square

**Check:** loaded the real site (`/framework/ui/item/`, which already pulls in the real
Material Icons `.woff2` the same way every page does — `core/App/Font.js`), then rendered
10 different icon names (`description`, `folder`, `arrow_forward`, `more_vert`, `close`,
`check`, `mic`, `settings`, `search`, `menu`) at `font-size: 24px; line-height: 1`, and
read `getBoundingClientRect()` on each.

**Result:** all 10 came back **exactly 24×24px** — width equal to height equal to the
font size, no variation between a wide glyph (`arrow_forward`) and a narrow one
(`close`). This is by design: Material Icons ships every glyph on a fixed 24×24 grid, so
**the font itself is monospaced for icons** the way a monospace font is for letters.

**What this means:** you never need to fix an icon's width by hand (a `width: 1em` some
callers add, e.g. `dropdown.css:82`, `Panel/toolbar.css:123`, `item.js`'s `.item-icon`,
is not wrong, just unnecessary for width alone — see the FRAME section below for why you
still might want it).

## 2. The icon's own box is exactly the font size; `line-height` changes the LINE, not the glyph

**Check:** same render, compared `line-height: 1` against `line-height: normal` on the
same 10 glyphs.

**Result:** the icon's own `getBoundingClientRect()` height did not change between the
two — still 24px either way. `line-height` on an inline element doesn't resize *that
element's* box; it resizes the invisible "line box" the browser builds around every
inline run on that line (glyph + surrounding text together). `framework.css`'s
`.icon { line-height: 1; }` (`framework.css:562`) exists to stop the icon from *quietly
inflating that shared line box* to whatever the icon font's own line metrics are — not to
resize the icon itself, which was already exactly 1em.

## 3. An icon does NOT sit centred against adjacent text by default — it needs a nudge or a frame

**Check:** built a row of plain text, a Material Icon (`line-height: 1`), and more plain
text, all at the same font size, and compared the icon's box against the row's own line
box.

**Result:** the icon (24px tall) sits flush with the TOP of the row's line box (28px
tall, from the text's own `line-height: normal`, ≈1.15). Its bottom lands about 4px
*above* the row's bottom edge — i.e., a plain icon reads as sitting slightly high and
looking disconnected from the baseline the letters sit on.

**This is exactly the bug the owner described** ("the vertical alignment is often a
problem"), and it is why real call sites hand-patch it — the one found in this audit is
`imagine/paging/paging.css:1020`:
`.paging-expand-head .icon { vertical-align: -0.15em; }` — a hand-tuned nudge, marked
`/* control */`, that exists only because the default position is wrong. It is a
symptom, not a fix others can reuse: the next caller has to rediscover the same offset.

## 4. When an icon needs a FRAME, and when it doesn't

A **frame** is a fixed square box (in `em`, so it scales with the container's font size)
that the icon is centred inside, both ways — `display: grid; place-items: center;` (or
flex) on a box sized `width/height: 1.3em` or similar, NOT on the icon itself.

**Needs a frame:**
- **A button that is only an icon** (no visible label) — a frame gives it a real click
  target bigger than the glyph's own ink, and centres the glyph inside that target both
  ways. `ui/item/item.js`'s `.item-caret, .item-icon` already does exactly this —
  `width: 1.3em; aspect-ratio: 1; display: grid; place-items: center; line-height: 1;`
  — and it's the cleanest example on the site today. Copy this, don't reinvent it.
- **A row of icon+label items that must line up in a column** (a file tree, a menu) —
  the frame is what makes every icon's right edge (where the label starts) land on the
  same x no matter how wide that particular glyph visually looks, and it reserves the
  same width for a caret/fold triangle so leaves and branches still line up
  (`item.js`'s own comment explains this: "a leaf next to a folder... lines its icon up
  with its sibling's").
- **A toggle / lit button** (the owner's "on = lit, off = dim" idea) — the lit background
  needs a fixed box to fill; you can't apply a background to a bare inline glyph and get
  a clean edge.

**Doesn't need a frame:**
- **An icon inline with text it's labelling** (a link, a menu row's own label, a
  breadcrumb) — here the fix is the small vertical-align nudge (fact 3), not a frame; a
  frame would add unwanted extra width before the label. Most of the one-offs in this
  audit (`.page-crumbs .icon`, `.page-related-link .icon`, `.omnibox-card .icon`, etc.)
  are this case and just set `font-size`, correctly.

**Frame size, in em:** `1.3em` square is what `item.js` already uses and reads well; the
Panel toolbar's icon-only button frame (`Panel/toolbar.css:103`) uses `1.7em`, sized for
a bigger click target. Recommend **picking one of these as the site default** (probably
`1.3em` for an inline icon-item, a bigger one like `1.6`–`1.7em` for a standalone icon
BUTTON that needs a generous tap target) rather than the current spread of ad hoc
numbers. Because both are `em`, raising the container's `font-size` scales the icon, the
frame, and any padding around it together — which is the exact "cascade through" the
owner asked for.

## How this was measured

[`measure-icons.mjs`](measure-icons.mjs) — a headless Playwright script (never drives
the owner's own browser tabs; launches its own hidden Chromium) that loads the real site,
injects the 10 test glyphs, and reads `getBoundingClientRect()` / `getComputedStyle()`
on each. Raw output is inline in the sections above; nothing here is estimated.

+# The rules: when to frame an icon, and which class for what
+
+The owner's own words: "I don't think necessarily every icon needs a frame... so just look
+into that and figure out... show examples of either way."
+
+## Is Material Icons fixed width?
+
+**Yes.** Material Icons is a ligature font — `icon("star")` prints the literal word "star" and
+the font swaps a glyph in for it — and every glyph in it is drawn inside the same 24×24 advance
+box, however much of that box the ink actually fills. So two icons sitting side by side, with no
+frame at all, already share the same width and already line up horizontally. That fact rules
+out the single biggest reason someone reaches for a frame ("so the icons line up") — they
+already do.
+
+## So when does a frame earn its place?
+
+Three real reasons, and a frame should exist only when one of them is true for the icon in
+question:
+
+1. **A click target.** A glyph alone renders at whatever `font-size` it inherited — often
+   smaller than the roughly 2em (32px at a 16px base) that a pointer or a thumb wants to aim at.
+   The frame is the square box that gives the click/tap area its real size, and it is also
+   where a background and a hover live, because a bare `<span>` has nowhere for either to sit
+   without changing the glyph itself.
+2. **Vertical centring against something taller.** The icon's own `line-height: 1` (in
+   `.icon`, framework.css) keeps it from growing whatever line box it sits in, but it does
+   nothing to CENTRE the glyph inside a taller box around it — a button, a list row. That
+   centring is `place-items: center` on the frame, not a property of the icon.
+3. **A consistent box in a grid of them.** A rail or toolbar where every slot has to measure
+   the same width — so a glyph that visually looks lighter or heavier still sits in a column
+   that lines up with its neighbours' boxes, not just their glyphs.
+
+An icon riding inline with a sentence ("★ Starred") needs **none** of these — it is not a click
+target, it is not centred against anything taller than itself, and it is not one slot in a grid.
+That case keeps using plain `.icon`, unframed, exactly as before this task.
+
+## The one token: `--icon-frame`
+
+`--icon-frame: 1.6em` is declared once, in `framework.css`, right beside `.icon`'s own
+`font-size: 1.25em` — both rules read the same ancestor's font-size, which is what makes
+`.ui-icon-frame` and `.ui-icon-btn` scale together with the glyph when a container's font-size
+changes (the page's "three sizes" demo proves this live: 14px, 18px, 28px containers, same
+markup, everything scales). 1.6em leaves visible room for a background and padding around the
+1.25em glyph without the frame crowding it.
+
+`ui/item`'s own tree-row frame (`.item-icon`, `.item-caret`) is a **tighter** 1.3em — a row read
+many-in-a-column wants the icon closer to the name beside it than a standalone button does. That
+was a deliberate, already-shipped choice (2026-09-29), not an inconsistency: two different
+contexts, two different numbers, both derived from the same underlying idea. A later pass could
+point `.item-icon` at `--icon-frame` too with an override, but that edit is outside this task's
+fence (`public/framework/ui/item/` was not touched).
+
+## Which class for what
+
+| Need | Class |
+|---|---|
+| An icon riding inline with text | `.icon` (unchanged, no frame) |
+| An icon alone, needing a visible frame | `.ui-icon-frame` |
+| A clickable icon, no background until hover | `.ui-icon-btn` |
+| A clickable icon that should already read as its own surface | `.ui-icon-btn.ui-icon-btn-bg` |
+| An on/off icon button | `.ui-icon-btn` + `aria-pressed="true"/"false"`, toggled on click |
+| A row of icon buttons, some flush, some backed | `.ui-icon-rail` around any mix of the above |
+| An icon beside a name in a list | `ui.item({ icon, name, … })` — a different module, not this one |
+
+## Migrated (this task's second pass, after the audit)
+
+- **The inline-alignment bug** (facts.md §3: an icon sits ~4px high against the text beside
+  it) is now fixed ONCE, in `.icon` itself (`framework.css`, `vertical-align: -0.15em`) —
+  the exact value one real caller, `imagine/paging/paging.css:1020`, had already hand-tuned.
+  That caller's own nudge is deleted; it now inherits the shared default. `vertical-align`
+  only ever moves an inline box against surrounding text, so every frame/button that
+  centres its icon with `place-items`/`align-items` (this module's own, `ui/item`'s,
+  Panel's) was never touched by the old per-caller nudges and is not touched by this
+  change either.
+- **`ext/Panel`'s duplicate stylesheet** (audit one-off #2: `toolbar.css` and

+  block, so a fix to one never reached the other) is deduplicated: `controls.css` is now
+  the one real copy (it is what `workspace.js`, the module's front door, loads);
+  `toolbar.css` is an empty stylesheet with a comment pointing at it. `.panel-btn` itself

+  reveal and `:has()` square detection that `.ui-icon-btn` has no reason to know about, and
+  it has real callers across the rail, a seam's menu, the drag grip and the inspector. A
+  full class swap risked exactly the "v1 behaviour unchanged" rule this task was given, for
+  a cosmetic win (one shared class name) this task's budget did not cover. `controls.css`
+  now says so, next to the rule.

+import { css } from "../parts.js";
+
+/**
+ * Three classes, nothing to import and nothing to wire — same shape as ui/badge and
+ * ui/alert: the class list IS the component. Everything here reuses the real icon,
+ * `icon()` from core/View/View.js (a span.material-icons.icon), and the one new
+ * token this task adds beside it in framework.css: `--icon-frame`. Because that
+ * token and the icon's own `font-size: 1.25em` both read the SAME ancestor, raising
+ * a container's font-size scales the icon, the frame and the button together — no
+ * JS, no second number to keep in sync. The facts and the reasoning are in
+ * doc/icons.md.
+ *
+ * .ui-icon-frame            — a fixed em box around one icon, centred both ways.
+ *                              For an icon that must line up with others even when
+ *                              the glyphs themselves are not the exact same width.
+ * .ui-icon-btn               — the frame, clickable: flush (no background) by
+ *                              default, a wash on hover. Add .ui-icon-btn-bg for a
+ *                              button that reads as its own surface before hover too
+ *                              (a rail's current item, say).
+ * .ui-icon-btn[aria-pressed] — the toggle state. A toggle button already needs
+ *                              aria-pressed for screen readers, so that attribute
+ *                              IS the on/off switch — there is no second ".active"
+ *                              class that could fall out of sync with it. "true"
+ *                              lights the background and tints the icon; "false"
+ *                              dims the icon.
+ * .ui-icon-rail               — a row of icon buttons, flush and backed ones mixed
+ *                              freely; it only supplies the gap between them.
+ */
+css(`@layer theme {
+	.ui-icon-frame {
+		display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
+		width: var(--icon-frame); height: var(--icon-frame);
+		line-height: 1; flex: 0 0 auto;
+	}
+
+	.ui-icon-btn {
+		display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
+		width: var(--icon-frame); height: var(--icon-frame);
+		line-height: 1; flex: 0 0 auto;
+		padding: 0; margin: 0; background: none; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius);
+		color: inherit; cursor: pointer;
+	}
+	.ui-icon-btn:hover { background: var(--wash); }
+	.ui-icon-btn:focus { outline: none; }
+	.ui-icon-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--prim); outline-offset: -2px; }
+
+	/* An opt-in background, for a button that should already read as its own
+	   surface — not only once the pointer arrives. */
+	.ui-icon-btn-bg { background: var(--fill-a08); }
+	.ui-icon-btn-bg:hover { background: var(--fill-a32); }
+
+	.ui-icon-btn[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--fill-a32); color: var(--prim); }
+	.ui-icon-btn[aria-pressed="true"]:hover { background: var(--fill-a32); }
+	.ui-icon-btn[aria-pressed="false"] { color: var(--subtle); }
+
+	.ui-icon-rail { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.25em; }
+
+	/* The alignment guide, for the demo page only: a hairline at the row's centre,
+	   toggled by a button on the page itself — no framework behaviour here, just
+	   the one class it adds and removes. */
+	.ui-icon-guide { position: relative; }
+	.ui-icon-guide::before {
+		content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 50%;
+		border-top: 1px dashed var(--prim); opacity: 0.6; pointer-events: none;
+	}
+}`);

+# icon — one frame, one button, one rail
+
+The owner's own words: too many one-off pieces of CSS building "icon layout" across the site,
+and vertical and horizontal alignment kept breaking. `ui/icon` is three classes that answer it,
+built around the `icon()` the site already has — nothing new to draw the glyph itself.
+
+## Use
+
+```js
+import { icon, button, div } from "/app.js";
+import "/framework/ui/icon/icon.js";   // registers the three classes; ui.js wiring is next
+
+div.c("ui-icon-frame", () => icon("star"));                       // framed, centred both ways
+button.c("ui-icon-btn", () => icon("favorite")).attr("type", "button");   // flush, clickable
+button.c("ui-icon-btn ui-icon-btn-bg", () => icon("home")).attr("type", "button"); // backed
+```
+
+A toggle button is the same `.ui-icon-btn`, with `aria-pressed` carrying the on/off state —
+"true" lights the background, "false" dims the icon. A rail is `.ui-icon-rail` around any mix of
+flush and backed buttons; it only supplies the gap between them. All three are sized in `em`,
+off the one token `--icon-frame` (declared beside `.icon` in `framework.css`), so raising a
+container's `font-size` scales the icon, the frame and the button together — see it live at
+three sizes on the page below.
+
+## Watch out
+
+- **Are Material Icons fixed width? Yes.** Every glyph in the font sits in the same 24×24
+  advance box, so two icons already line up horizontally with no help from a frame. A frame
+  earns its place for a click target, for vertical centring against something taller than the
+  glyph's own line box, or for a row where every slot — icon or not — has to measure the same.
+  [doc/icons.md](doc/icons.md) has the full reasoning.
+- **`.icon` itself gained one line: `vertical-align: -0.15em`.** Nothing renames or replaces it
+  — an icon riding inline with text still just wears `.icon` — but it now sits centred against
+  that text instead of ~4px high, the exact bug the owner named. `doc/icons.md` "Migrated" has
+  the measurement and the one real caller (`imagine/paging/`) whose own hand-tuned nudge this
+  replaced. A frame or a flex/grid button (this module's, `ui/item`'s, Panel's) was never
+  affected by that bug or this fix — `vertical-align` only moves an INLINE box.
+- **Icon items in a list are `ui/item`, not this module.** `ui.item({ icon, name, … })` already
+  has the row, the 1.3em tree-row frame and the `.boxed` background-with-padding look; this
+  page's list demo reuses it rather than building a second one.
+- **`ui.js` is not wired up yet.** This task's fence is this module, `framework.css`'s icon
+  block and `ui/page.js`'s `children:` — the one-line addition to `ui.js` that makes `ui.icon`
+  importable the way `ui.item` is happens in the next pass (the mastermind's migration step).
+  Until then, import `icon.js` directly, as the page itself does.
+
+## More
+
+- [Overview](/framework/ui/icon/) — the rail, the button range, the list, all three sizes side
+  by side.
+- [doc/icons.md](doc/icons.md) — fixed width or not, when a frame earns its place, the token.
+- Back to [UI](/framework/ui/).

# Icon audit — every icon use, and the CSS that lays it out Every icon on the site is the same call: `icon(name)` in [`core/View/View.js`](/framework/core/View/View.js) (line 469) — it just returns `name`. It sets no size, no padding, no alignment. **All layout is left to each caller's own CSS** — which is exactly why there are so many different answers to the same small question. Read the measured facts first: [`facts.md`](facts.md) (are icons fixed-width? when does an icon need a frame?). **How this was found:** grep for `icon(` (188 JS files call it), `.icon` as a CSS selector (~95 rules across ~60 stylesheets), and `material-icons`. # Icon facts — measured, not guessed

Every claim below was checked by running code, not by reading the CSS and assuming. The
script is [`measure-icons.mjs`](#how-this-was-measured) at the bottom of this page.

## 1. Material Icons ARE fixed-width — every glyph is a perfect square

**Check:** loaded the real site (`/framework/ui/item/`, which already pulls in the real
Material Icons `.woff2` the same way every page does — `core/App/Font.js`), then rendered
10 different icon names (`description`, `folder`, `arrow_forward`, `more_vert`, `close`,
`check`, `mic`, `settings`, `search`, `menu`) at `font-size: 24px; line-height: 1`, and
read `getBoundingClientRect()` on each.

**Result:** all 10 came back **exactly 24×24px** — width equal to height equal to the
font size, no variation between a wide glyph (`arrow_forward`) and a narrow one
(`close`). This is by design: Material Icons ships every glyph on a fixed 24×24 grid, so
**the font itself is monospaced for icons** the way a monospace font is for letters.

**What this means:** you never need to fix an icon's width by hand (a `width: 1em` some
callers add, e.g. `dropdown.css:82`, `Panel/toolbar.css:123`, `item.js`'s `.item-icon`,
is not wrong, just unnecessary for width alone — see the FRAME section below for why you
still might want it).

## 2. The icon's own box is exactly the font size; `line-height` changes the LINE, not the glyph

**Check:** same render, compared `line-height: 1` against `line-height: normal` on the
same 10 glyphs.

**Result:** the icon's own `getBoundingClientRect()` height did not change between the
two — still 24px either way. `line-height` on an inline element doesn't resize *that
element's* box; it resizes the invisible "line box" the browser builds around every
inline run on that line (glyph + surrounding text together). `framework.css`'s
`.icon { line-height: 1; }` (`framework.css:562`) exists to stop the icon from *quietly
inflating that shared line box* to whatever the icon font's own line metrics are — not to
resize the icon itself, which was already exactly 1em.

## 3. An icon does NOT sit centred against adjacent text by default — it needs a nudge or a frame

**Check:** built a row of plain text, a Material Icon (`line-height: 1`), and more plain
text, all at the same font size, and compared the icon's box against the row's own line
box.

**Result:** the icon (24px tall) sits flush with the TOP of the row's line box (28px
tall, from the text's own `line-height: normal`, ≈1.15). Its bottom lands about 4px
*above* the row's bottom edge — i.e., a plain icon reads as sitting slightly high and
looking disconnected from the baseline the letters sit on.

**This is exactly the bug the owner described** ("the vertical alignment is often a
problem"), and it is why real call sites hand-patch it — the one found in this audit is
`imagine/paging/paging.css:1020`:
`.paging-expand-head .icon { vertical-align: -0.15em; }` — a hand-tuned nudge, marked
`/* control */`, that exists only because the default position is wrong. It is a
symptom, not a fix others can reuse: the next caller has to rediscover the same offset.

## 4. When an icon needs a FRAME, and when it doesn't

A **frame** is a fixed square box (in `em`, so it scales with the container's font size)
that the icon is centred inside, both ways — `display: grid; place-items: center;` (or
flex) on a box sized `width/height: 1.3em` or similar, NOT on the icon itself.

**Needs a frame:**
- **A button that is only an icon** (no visible label) — a frame gives it a real click
  target bigger than the glyph's own ink, and centres the glyph inside that target both
  ways. `ui/item/item.js`'s `.item-caret, .item-icon` already does exactly this —
  `width: 1.3em; aspect-ratio: 1; display: grid; place-items: center; line-height: 1;`
  — and it's the cleanest example on the site today. Copy this, don't reinvent it.
- **A row of icon+label items that must line up in a column** (a file tree, a menu) —
  the frame is what makes every icon's right edge (where the label starts) land on the
  same x no matter how wide that particular glyph visually looks, and it reserves the
  same width for a caret/fold triangle so leaves and branches still line up
  (`item.js`'s own comment explains this: "a leaf next to a folder... lines its icon up
  with its sibling's").
- **A toggle / lit button** (the owner's "on = lit, off = dim" idea) — the lit background
  needs a fixed box to fill; you can't apply a background to a bare inline glyph and get
  a clean edge.

**Doesn't need a frame:**
- **An icon inline with text it's labelling** (a link, a menu row's own label, a
  breadcrumb) — here the fix is the small vertical-align nudge (fact 3), not a frame; a
  frame would add unwanted extra width before the label. Most of the one-offs in this
  audit (`.page-crumbs .icon`, `.page-related-link .icon`, `.omnibox-card .icon`, etc.)
  are this case and just set `font-size`, correctly.

**Frame size, in em:** `1.3em` square is what `item.js` already uses and reads well; the
Panel toolbar's icon-only button frame (`Panel/toolbar.css:103`) uses `1.7em`, sized for
a bigger click target. Recommend **picking one of these as the site default** (probably
`1.3em` for an inline icon-item, a bigger one like `1.6`–`1.7em` for a standalone icon
BUTTON that needs a generous tap target) rather than the current spread of ad hoc
numbers. Because both are `em`, raising the container's `font-size` scales the icon, the
frame, and any padding around it together — which is the exact "cascade through" the
owner asked for.

## How this was measured

[`measure-icons.mjs`](measure-icons.mjs) — a headless Playwright script (never drives
the owner's own browser tabs; launches its own hidden Chromium) that loads the real site,
injects the 10 test glyphs, and reads `getBoundingClientRect()` / `getComputedStyle()`
on each. Raw output is inline in the sections above; nothing here is estimated.

# The Shell, and the dark dev shell: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md` (the dictation may have been cut off; more may follow and will be appended). Read them in full.

## Asks
1. **A general SHELL:** it wraps any page in optional regions: a HEADER, a LEFT sidebar, a RIGHT sidebar and a FOOTER. Every region is optional. Headers and footers are MINIMAL (a thin bar: properties, path, toolbar buttons). Shells NEST (a shell within a shell). The usual patterns are two or three regions.
   - Start from what exists; don't invent a second one: /layouts/shell/ (and its Shell.js), core/Sidebar and its variants, ext/drawer (the right rail), ext/grip (resizing), and the HTML study at /framework/ai/2026/09/29/layout-explorer-3-columns-and-a-study-of/html-study.md (its recommendation for named sidebars: app.left, app.right).
   - It belongs in core (core/Page/layout/ or core/Shell); coordinate with mastermind-page, which owns core/Page and its layout audit.
2. **The DEV SHELL:** Ctrl+\ (today's dev bar shortcut) toggles a DARK-MODE shell around the whole site, which is obviously different from the site. It MERGES the dev bar into it: the dev bar's tools move into the shell's regions. Scrap most of the dev bar's own CSS and lean on the site's CSS and tokens (a dark theme via the existing tokens, not a separate stylesheet world).
   - The default dev shell is left and right sidebars; the header and footer are optional and thin.
   - Nothing breaks for pages underneath; toggling it off returns the page exactly as it was.
3. **Demos:** the Shell with each combination (L, R, L+R, with and without a header and footer, and nested), plus the dev shell on a real page, at 400, 1920 and 3440.

## Rules
Keep the old dev bar reachable as v1 until the owner approves. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test (links followed), merge.mjs, the review skill, and screenshots at 4 widths. At most 2 minions; budget $15, hard. The owner said to use a new mastermind for this.

# Design: the Shell, and the dark dev shell

## The picture

```
 A Shell: four optional regions around the page       The dev shell (Ctrl + \)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ header (thin bar: path, buttons)  opt.   │        │▓ /framework/core/Page/   hold  block ▓│ ← thin, dark
 ├────────┬─────────────────────┬───────────┤        ├▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┬───────────────────┬▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┤
 │ left   │                     │ right     │        │▓ page ▓│                   │▓ chat    ▓│
 │ opt.   │   main: any page    │ opt.      │        │▓ tree ▓│  the site, as-is  │▓ page    ▓│
 │        │   (or another Shell │           │        │▓ struc▓│  (light, pushed   │▓ layout  ▓│
 │        │    → nesting)       │           │        │▓ -ture▓│   inward, never   │▓ ai      ▓│
 ├────────┴─────────────────────┴───────────┤        │▓      ▓│   re-parented)    │▓ (tabs)  ▓│
 │ footer (thin bar)                 opt.   │        ├▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┴───────────────────┴▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┤
 └──────────────────────────────────────────┘        │▓ 1920px · 3 cols · socket ok        ▓│ ← thin, dark
                                                      └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## The parts

| Part | What it is | Where | Starts from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shell** | `new Shell({ header, left, right, footer, main })`; every region optional, each a function or a View; a missing one takes no space; `main` can be another Shell | `core/Shell/` (new) | `/layouts/shell/` (rail + grip), `core/Sidebar` |
| Region sizes | left and right resizable with `ext/grip`, remembered; header and footer are one thin line (about 2rem) | `Shell.css` | `ext/grip` |
| Dark | `color-scheme: dark` on a region; the site's own `light-dark()` tokens flip. No new colours | one line | how `devbar.css` already does it |
| **Dev shell** | Ctrl + \ puts a dark Shell around the whole site. Left: the page tree and structure. Right: the dev bar's tabs (chat, page, layout, ai). Header: path, hold, block, width. Footer: optional status line | `dev/DevShell/` (new) | `dev/DevBar` tools, moved in |
| The page underneath | not moved: the shell is a fixed frame, and `.app` is pushed in by four tokens (like `--devbar` today). Off = those tokens are 0 = exactly as before | `framework.css` `.app` padding | `--devbar` docking |
| v1 | the old dev bar stays, one click away (a "v1" button in the header) until you approve | `dev/DevBar/` untouched | |
| Demos | L · R · L+R · with/without header+footer · nested · the dev shell on a real page, shot at 400, 1920, 3440 | `/framework/core/Shell/` | |

## Decisions

- **A fixed frame that pushes `.app`, not re-parenting the page into the shell.** Re-parenting the live page would risk breaking every page's height and scroll rules; pushing is how the dev bar already works, and turning it off is removing one class. The general Shell (for demos and any page) is a plain grid you wrap content in.
- **One Shell class for both.** The dev shell is `Shell` with a `frame` option (fixed, around the window), so there is one system, not two.
- **Below 34em** the side regions become sheets you open from the header, as the dev bar does today.

# Streamed input: what Chat does today, and what it would take

![Today: the words wait in the box until it sends](shots/phone-before.png)

## Today: your words wait in the box

While you talk, Whisper's growing guess is written into the text box only (`ext/Chat/Mic.js`).

The box sends by itself at a pause: 2.5 s of quiet after a sentence, or 2.5 s of silence.

Only then does your line land in the chat, and only then do the assistants hear it.

## What streaming would take (not built here)

1. **The line shape already exists.** A chat line with the same `at` and `fix: true` replaces earlier words in place (`Chat.js`, `chat_line()`).
2. **Mic.js** would post a draft line as soon as there are words, then `fix` lines as the guess grows, and clear the box.
3. **Servex** would need a `draft` verb that writes the line without waking the assistants. Only the final line (today's `say`) wakes them.

About one task: Mic.js, one Servex verb, a restart, and a proof that no draft wakes an agent.

Note: the dictation-stream task (merged 2026-09-30) now streams the assistants' replies live and draws your words in a live bubble while you speak; this report predates it.

## CHANGE OF DESIGN (the owner, 09-30, relayed by servex-mastermind-opus) — this overrides `@Name` above

1. **References use `#`, not `@`:** `#Servex`, `#Page`. `@` is kept for USERS and AGENTS (`@owner`, `@mastermind-page`).
2. **Generalize:** a CONTROL CHARACTER defines a namespace (`#` = references, `@` = users/agents, more later). Each namespace has a MAP: a plain JS object of name → { icon, url, ...any data }. So: `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` (`#`) and `ext/Mention/maps/people.js` (`@`: owner, and agent roles — mastermind, fast-assistant… may point at /framework/servex/doc/roles.md), and `Mention.js` takes `{ "#": refs, "@": people }`; adding a namespace is adding a map.
3. **Names with spaces** use a bracket form: `#[Page layout]`. Pattern: `/(?<![\w\[])([#@])(\[[^\]\n]+\]|[A-Za-z][\w.-]*[\w])/`. Careful: markdown headings (`# Title`, a `#` then a space) never match; `#` inside a url or a word (`a#b`, `#fff` colours in text are fine to leave as unknown plain text) must not break anything. # @mentions — familiar concepts become icon links everywhere — requirements

Owner's words: `owner-words.md` (read fully). "Everywhere we're referencing the page class, it should be like a little document icon… with the word Page… a link to the core Page class… `@Page` … an automatic mention system where any of those tags automatically get converted to actual references."

## Asks
1. **A registry of concepts**: name → { url, icon } (e.g. `Page` → `/framework/core/Page/`, a document/file icon). Seed it from the systems map on card 2026/09/29/familiar-structure-every-named-system-ge (`systems.md`) and the Concepts tiles; a JSON/JSONL index any page can load cheaply (cached). Capitalised names = classes/systems.
2. **Syntax `@Page`** in any content — markdown (ext/markdown), chat bubbles (ext/Chat), cards, readmes rendered as pages — renders as an ICON ITEM link (icon + name → url; ui/item from item-ui). Unknown `@Name` stays plain text (and gets logged as a candidate).
3. Agents write `@Page` instead of "the page system" — add one line to the content skill via mastermind-servex-8 (skills architect), not directly.
4. First visible use: the AI 2 Needs you / Inbox rows and the chat bubbles show `@Page` etc. as icon items.
5. Keep it tiny: one parser pass after markdown, one registry file; no build step.

## Rules
Pool worktree, smoke (links followed), merge.mjs, one fresh reviewer, shots 400+1920. ≤ 2 minions, budget $8 hard.

## CHANGE OF DESIGN (the owner, 09-30, relayed by servex-mastermind-opus) — this overrides `@Name` above

1. **References use `#`, not `@`:** `#Servex`, `#Page`. `@` is kept for USERS and AGENTS (`@owner`, `@mastermind-page`).
2. **Generalize:** a CONTROL CHARACTER defines a namespace (`#` = references, `@` = users/agents, more later). Each namespace has a MAP: a plain JS object of name → { icon, url, ...any data }. So: `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` (`#`) and `ext/Mention/maps/people.js` (`@`: owner, and agent roles — mastermind, fast-assistant… may point at /framework/servex/doc/roles.md), and `Mention.js` takes `{ "#": refs, "@": people }`; adding a namespace is adding a map.
3. **Names with spaces** use a bracket form: `#[Page layout]`. Pattern: `/(?<![\w\[])([#@])(\[[^\]\n]+\]|[A-Za-z][\w.-]*[\w])/`. Careful: markdown headings (`# Title`, a `#` then a space) never match; `#` inside a url or a word (`a#b`, `#fff` colours in text are fine to leave as unknown plain text) must not break anything. Lookup is case-insensitive.
4. **The map can be derived** from the site (page titles/icons, Concepts tiles, the systems map) — this task: a hand-written map seeded from those, plus a one-line note in doc/ on how a derived map would plug in. Manual entries for things outside the site.
5. **First targets, all must resolve** (to real docs; this dev server answers 200 even for missing pages, so check the file exists on disk): `#Servex` → /framework/servex/, `#Page` → /framework/core/Page/, `#CLAUDE.md` → the root CLAUDE.md's rendered view or /framework/ (say which), `#skills` → /framework/servex/ skills section or .claude/skills, `#MCP`, `#dev-server` → /Server/, `#mastermind`, `#fast-assistant`, `#smart-assistant` → /framework/servex/doc/roles.md (anchor if one exists). The AI chats must render them as icon links.

## The owner, verbatim (09-30, about 1:15 PM)

Okay, so the the AI2 default page, the needs you page, it is sort of a rail, a preview rail, just like the inbox is. Um, also, those these items are are not clear to me what they are. Like the things on the needs you page, how important are these? Like, uh, let's put a score next to each one and rank them by the importance. I don't know if it's Maybe maybe we, we use a, a a one based score system and you render it as a number zero through a hundred or something. I don't know. That just represents the importance where a hundred is, you know, maximum importance and you know one or two are like minimal importance. Um and then, you know, each time we're creating these uh Well, anytime we're creating anything, really, we want to be focusing on the most, the things that are likely to score, you know, as high importance, like influential, important, necessary, blocking, you know, something that's blocking something else. Uh, also, you know, the, so a, a number of these are saying the page system. So I don't know, I haven't seen the page system described like, or worded like that. Well, I mean, I, I know what that is, but I want to see an icon item for, it should just be capital page. I, I think we can assume that if we get the right icon for, you know, this capital page word, when we click on that, that is the page system. So everywhere we're referencing the page class, it should be like probably a little uh, document icon. Like if we can have a little, probably a file icon would work, anything like that, put it, with the you know word page and that is basically a link to the core framework core page class and then every time we're referencing Every time across the entire site, anytime we're writing content and we're referencing the page system, it could automatically appear. Maybe, maybe it's like a username. At page, or yeah, I think at page could be a decent way to create like keywords no matter where they live, you know, it's, it's basically just a map, like the at becomes a, a namespace and you could, you know, use at capital P-A-G-E as the like syntax and then we could have a, an automatic like mention system where any of those tags automatically get converted to actual references. And so maybe for those, you know, quick, that, that'd be like a quick tagging system. And the benefit there is that you could kind of cache or index all the icons, basically, if all you need is the URL, the name and the icon, well, we already have the name based on, you know, that's just it's its name. And so, you know, with basically just an icon and a, a URL, you could easily convert any at reference to a actual thing. That you could click through to and read about.

The brief given to `minion-dictation-stream`: items 1 to 6 of [the owner's words](../voice-session-v-2joydc7/owner-words.md), said by voice in session v-2joydc7. The owner calls this "fundamental to the whole experience."

# /framework/design/ and /framework/code/: knowledge systems you can browse: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

## The idea
Skills hide knowledge in `.claude/skills/`. The owner wants that knowledge **browsable as pages**: one tree of readmes and sub-systems that an agent or a person reads the same way. The skill stays, but thin:
- its description gives agents awareness that it exists;
- its body says "read the readme chain at /framework/design/… (a quick overview follows)".

The knowledge itself moves into the pages.

## Asks
1. **`/framework/design/`: the design system.** Everything that contributes to design when you create anything new:
   - **layout**;
   - **color**;
   - **navigation**: the path, how links look, persistent or switching, transitions;
   - **content**: the iceberg, level of detail, what is foundational, importance and prioritization;
   - **UI**: buttons, toolbars, dropdowns, icons.

   Each is a child page with a readme. It **links** to `/framework/styles/` (the CSS style guide) and `/framework/ui/`, and doesn't duplicate them.
2. **`/framework/code/`: the coding system,** for code in this framework (HTML, CSS, JS):
   - patterns;
   - do's and don'ts;
   - formatting;
   - opinions;
   - the traps that never throw.

   Also an **object-oriented design** page: every class ships a view of its state.
3. **Move the knowledge out of the skills.** Candidates:
   - `content`, `layout`, `page`, `css` and `naming` → design;
   - `code` and `new-css-class` → code.

   Each skill shrinks to a pointer plus a short overview. Don't lose a single rule in the move: check line by line.
4. **Level 1 of each page is visual and structured,** in the familiar-structure style of CLAUDE.md: concept tiles, then the gist, then lists. Use the same docs top-tabs as the other modules.
5. Add both to `/framework/`'s `children:` so they can be found.

## Coordination (important)
- **mastermind-servex-9** is the skills architect. It is writing the proposal for the content/layout/UI/navigation skill structure. Read its card first, and build to it. Skill edits go through it: send it the diff, and it approves.
- **task-mastermind-ai-page** documents the AI system at /framework/ai/, and links here for design and code rather than repeating them.
- **task-mastermind-review**'s review questions per system should live on these pages.

## Rules
- Pool worktree, then `merge.mjs` (smoke test), then the review skill. Screenshots at 400 and 1920.
- Budget: $12, hard. At most 2 Sonnet minions.
- Post a short outline on the card before building.

# The Shell, and the dark dev shell: requirements

The owner's words are in `owner-words.md` (the dictation may have been cut off; more may follow and will be appended). Read them in full.

## Asks
1. **A general SHELL:** it wraps any page in optional regions: a HEADER, a LEFT sidebar, a RIGHT sidebar and a FOOTER. Every region is optional. Headers and footers are MINIMAL (a thin bar: properties, path, toolbar buttons). Shells NEST (a shell within a shell). The usual patterns are two or three regions.
   - Start from what exists; don't invent a second one: /layouts/shell/ (and its Shell.js), core/Sidebar and its variants, ext/drawer (the right rail), ext/grip (resizing), and the HTML study at /framework/ai/2026/09/29/layout-explorer-3-columns-and-a-study-of/html-study.md (its recommendation for named sidebars: app.left, app.right).
   - It belongs in core (core/Page/layout/ or core/Shell); coordinate with mastermind-page, which owns core/Page and its layout audit.
2. **The DEV SHELL:** Ctrl+\ (today's dev bar shortcut) toggles a DARK-MODE shell around the whole site, which is obviously different from the site. It MERGES the dev bar into it: the dev bar's tools move into the shell's regions. Scrap most of the dev bar's own CSS and lean on the site's CSS and tokens (a dark theme via the existing tokens, not a separate stylesheet world).
   - The default dev shell is left and right sidebars; the header and footer are optional and thin.
   - Nothing breaks for pages underneath; toggling it off returns the page exactly as it was.
3. **Demos:** the Shell with each combination (L, R, L+R, with and without a header and footer, and nested), plus the dev shell on a real page, at 400, 1920 and 3440.

## Rules
Keep the old dev bar reachable as v1 until the owner approves. Use a pool worktree, the smoke test (links followed), merge.mjs, the review skill, and screenshots at 4 widths. At most 2 minions; budget $15, hard. The owner said to use a new mastermind for this.

## The owner, verbatim (09-30, about 2:20 PM); the message may have been cut off at the end

All right, here's what I want. This will probably need a new mastermind. I want a dark mode shell around you know, the entire site. And so it's sort of like, it's sort of like the dev bar. Uh, you know, definitely let's use the dev bar and kind of merge that in. However, I don't want, the dev bar kind of have, has its own different theme. Like we can probably scrap most of the dev bar's CSS and lean into our current CSS, but I want it to be dark mode so that, uh, so that it looks different and it's obviously different. And then I think right now the control slash, uh, sorry, control backslash is what launches the dev bar. And that's good. Uh, use that, but it, but now we want the dev bar to include a left sidebar, a footer across. Hmm. Well, so each, you, you could optionally have a header and footer. I kind of think that just having the left and right sidebar should be plenty. However, having like a minimal, a, a very small uh, header and footer that doesn't take up much space, that's, you know, could just be like, you know, properties, path names, toolbar buttons, or whatever could be pretty useful. So I think, you know, we, and then each, so the, the header and footer should be optional. The, uh, the left and right sidebar are also, well, so, the default uh, dev bar or the default shell mode. So, okay, this could be generalized as a shell, right? So you could use this header, left, right, sidebar, and footer system for any, uh, for any page, essentially. Uh, you could wrap any existing page in a shell. And so you could have, you know, shells within shells, essentially, right? So header and footer are optional. Left and right sidebar are really optional, too. Um, Generally, the the three or the two patterns.

# Design: the Shell, and the dark dev shell

## The picture

```
 A Shell: four optional regions around the page       The dev shell (Ctrl + \)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ header (thin bar: path, buttons)  opt.   │        │▓ /framework/core/Page/   hold  block ▓│ ← thin, dark
 ├────────┬─────────────────────┬───────────┤        ├▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┬───────────────────┬▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┤
 │ left   │                     │ right     │        │▓ page ▓│                   │▓ chat    ▓│
 │ opt.   │   main: any page    │ opt.      │        │▓ tree ▓│  the site, as-is  │▓ page    ▓│
 │        │   (or another Shell │           │        │▓ struc▓│  (light, pushed   │▓ layout  ▓│
 │        │    → nesting)       │           │        │▓ -ture▓│   inward, never   │▓ ai      ▓│
 ├────────┴─────────────────────┴───────────┤        │▓      ▓│   re-parented)    │▓ (tabs)  ▓│
 │ footer (thin bar)                 opt.   │        ├▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┴───────────────────┴▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┤
 └──────────────────────────────────────────┘        │▓ 1920px · 3 cols · socket ok        ▓│ ← thin, dark
                                                      └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## The parts

| Part | What it is | Where | Starts from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shell** | `new Shell({ header, left, right, footer, main })`; every region optional, each a function or a View; a missing one takes no space; `main` can be another Shell | `core/Shell/` (new) | `/layouts/shell/` (rail + grip), `core/Sidebar` |
| Region sizes | left and right resizable with `ext/grip`, remembered; header and footer are one thin line (about 2rem) | `Shell.css` | `ext/grip` |
| Dark | `color-scheme: dark` on a region; the site's own `light-dark()` tokens flip. No new colours | one line | how `devbar.css` already does it |
| **Dev shell** | Ctrl + \ puts a dark Shell around the whole site. Left: the page tree and structure. Right: the dev bar's tabs (chat, page, layout, ai). Header: path, hold, block, width. Footer: optional status line | `dev/DevShell/` (new) | `dev/DevBar` tools, moved in |
| The page underneath | not moved: the shell is a fixed frame, and `.app` is pushed in by four tokens (like `--devbar` today). Off = those tokens are 0 = exactly as before | `framework.css` `.app` padding | `--devbar` docking |
| v1 | the old dev bar stays, one click away (a "v1" button in the header) until you approve | `dev/DevBar/` untouched | |
| Demos | L · R · L+R · with/without header+footer · nested · the dev shell on a real page, shot at 400, 1920, 3440 | `/framework/core/Shell/` | |

## Decisions

- **A fixed frame that pushes `.app`, not re-parenting the page into the shell.** Re-parenting the live page would risk breaking every page's height and scroll rules; pushing is how the dev bar already works, and turning it off is removing one class. The general Shell (for demos and any page) is a plain grid you wrap content in.
- **One Shell class for both.** The dev shell is `Shell` with a `frame` option (fixed, around the window), so there is one system, not two.
- **Below 34em** the side regions become sheets you open from the header, as the dev bar does today.

# Inbox: one page extension, used everywhere: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). The refined version is on the card [Now: one inbox everywhere, and refined prompts](/framework/ai/2026/09/30/now-one-inbox-everywhere-and-refined-pro/). Re-read both before each step.

**Queued:** spawn only after the 5-hour usage reset (4:50 PM, 2026-09-30).

## Asks
1. **`core/Page/ext/`: an extension (plugin) system for Page,** modelled on the Server's plugin system (`Server/plugins/`): event-driven hooks, and extensions configured by data (in page.jsonl), not hard-coded. It is the ext pattern for any module or directory. Keep it minimal.
2. **`core/Page/ext/Inbox`:** the first extension. Any page can have an inbox.
   - Messaging a page = appending one line to its page.jsonl: `{inbox: {type: "message"|"question", author, text, at}}`.
   - The author is the agent that sent it. It's like emailing a directory.
   - Build on the page inbox that already landed ([page-inbox](../page-inbox/): notes live under the `inbox` key), and on the drawer inbox steps. Move it; don't rebuild it.
3. **Move the AI 2 Inbox to the new /framework/ai/** as an **Inbox** tab. Keep every useful feature of today's Inbox: the sidebar on click, and read/unread, archive, auto-resolve and search from task ai2-inbox-read. The top-priority items also show on the default dashboard (the Overview).
4. **Needs you is a filter in the Inbox list,** not its own tab with its own UI.
5. **Inbox and Log share one UI:** the rail with previews, and each preview opens its card. Today the three tabs use three different templates. Lean into the Inbox's version.
   - Inbox: real time, only what matters now.
   - Log: everything.
6. **The rail is a base class, overridden per page** with object-oriented overrides. The usage meters live only on the AI page's rail subclass, not on every page's inbox.
7. **Each owner prompt becomes an Inbox card showing its refined version.** Servex hears each owner prompt (the `.claude/prompts/` hook, and voice sessions), runs it through the Refine ladder (`ext/Refine`: raw → structured), and posts or updates a card at the top of the Inbox. The first card was made by hand as the example: see the link above.

## Coordination
- Replaces AI 2's own inbox code once it has moved. AI 2 then redirects, or stays as v1 until the owner approves (todo: "AI 2 merges into /framework/ai/").
- task-mastermind-ai-page owns /framework/ai/: add the Inbox tab together with it.
- task-mastermind-ai2-inbox-read (read/unread, archive, search) lands first. Carry its work over.
- mastermind-servex-9 owns the Servex side of item 7 (the prompt hook, Refine and posting the card). Ask it, or build it in `Servex/` through the pool.

## Rules
- Pool worktree, then `merge.mjs` (smoke test), then the review skill. Screenshots at 400 and 1920.
- Budget: $12, hard. At most 2 Sonnet minions.

## COURSE CORRECTION (2026-09-30 ~14:50, from mastermind-servex-9, relaying the owner)

The owner's newer words (`public/framework/ai/2026-09-30/design-code/owner-words.md`, first paragraph): "the inbox and the needs you, that to me, that sounds like the same thing … I kind of like the inbox better. So let's maybe just forget the needs you page for now. And let's focus on the inbox."

**Everything above this line is cancelled.** Do not redraw Needs you. Instead:

1. `git revert --no-edit 415389de` (your rail commit). Never reset or rewrite history. Needs you goes back to exactly what it was.
2. **A stalled ask becomes an Inbox row.** In `inbox.js`, where the Inbox's list is built (`items()`), add one row per ask whose folded status is `stalled`. Read `/framework/ai/asks.jsonl` with `fold_asks` from `/framework/ai/asks/fold.js`. Give the row an id `ask:<ask id>`, the kind `stalled`, the ask's title, `at` = when it stalled, and its owner. Its link goes to its card (`/framework/ai2/<card>/`, which opens in the Inbox's side pane like every card) when it has one, and otherwise to `/framework/ai/asks/?status=stalled`. It draws with the same `row()` in `faces.js`, with one quiet line: "Stalled · <owner> · silent 2 h".
3. **The importance score decides where it goes.** Rows with a score of 60 or more (stalled asks, blockers, questions a live agent is waiting on) sit at the top, highest score first. Everything else stays newest first, as it is now. Use `importance()` from `needs-rule.js`. `score_for` in needs.js already gives a card row its score.
4. **Unread is bold, read is plain.** A stalled-ask row is bold until you open it once. Remember that it was opened with the Inbox's existing read state, if it has one. If it has none, use `localStorage`, with every read and write wrapped in try/catch.
5. **Auto-resolve, never delete.** The row leaves the Inbox by itself when the ask's status is no longer `stalled` (landed, dropped, building). The ledger keeps every line.
6. Screenshots at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440 of `/framework/ai2/inbox/` and `/framework/ai2/` (Needs you must look unchanged). Write one line per band in your task.jsonl. There must be zero console errors.

New fence: `public/framework/ai2/inbox.js` (the row source), `faces.js` (only a small option on `row()`), `ai2.css` (new rules prefixed `ai2-row-` or `ai2-ask-`), and the `doc/` file that describes the Inbox (update it). `needs.js` and `page.js` only for the revert.

# Inbox: one page extension, used everywhere: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). The example card to post the refined version on is [Now: one inbox everywhere, and refined prompts](/framework/ai2/2026/09/30/now-one-inbox-everywhere-and-refined-pro/) — it's still empty; ask 7 is what fills it. Re-read both before each step.

**Queued:** spawn only after the 5-hour usage reset (4:50 PM, 2026-09-30).

## Asks
1. **`core/Page/ext/`: an extension (plugin) system for Page,** modelled on the Server's plugin system (`Server/plugins/`): event-driven hooks, and extensions configured by data (in page.jsonl), not hard-coded. It is the ext pattern for any module or directory. Keep it minimal.
2. **`core/Page/ext/Inbox`:** the first extension. Any page can have an inbox.
   - Messaging a page = appending one line to its page.jsonl: `{inbox: {type: "message"|"question", author, text, at}}`.
   - The author is the agent that sent it. It's like emailing a directory.
   - Build on the page inbox that already landed ([page-inbox](../page-inbox/): notes live under the `inbox` key), and on the drawer inbox steps. Move it; don't rebuild it.
3. **Move the AI 2 Inbox to the new /framework/ai/** as its **default tab** (the dashboard; the owner, 2026-09-30); the docs live on its System tab. Keep every useful feature of today's Inbox: the sidebar on click, and read/unread, archive, auto-resolve and search from task ai2-inbox-read. The Inbox IS the default tab, so its top-priority items are what the page opens on.
4. **Needs you is a filter in the Inbox list,** not its own tab with its own UI.
5. **Inbox and Log share one UI:** the rail with previews, and each preview opens its card. Today the three tabs use three different templates. Lean into the Inbox's version.
   - Inbox: real time, only what matters now.
   - Log: everything.
6. **The rail is a base class, overridden per page** with object-oriented overrides. The usage meters live only on the AI page's rail subclass, not on every page's inbox.
7. **Each owner prompt becomes an Inbox card showing its refined version.** Servex hears each owner prompt (the `.claude/prompts/` hook, and voice sessions), runs it through the Refine ladder (`ext/Refine`: raw → structured), and posts or updates a card at the top of the Inbox. Post the first one by hand, on the card linked above, as the example.

8. **A card is a whole conversation, and it shows what it's about** (the owner, 2026-09-30). Each Inbox item stands for an entire conversation, which continues in the card's sidebar. The card's body shows at least part of the thing it references, imported live: a page, a module or a screenshot. Build this on the reference system (`#Page`, `/path`, task-mastermind-mentions), so every post makes it obvious what it's talking about.

9. **Chat and card are ONE content model** (the owner, 2026-09-30, the summary of the thread):
   - A card IS a page: a title, a preview and a detail view, backed by its own page.jsonl. It can be a conversation or an AI session, and it has its own inbox, which is its feed of updates.
   - **The two views are two renderings of the same lines and the same content widgets:**
     - **chat mode** (the right sidebar or the mobile rail): informal, with bubbles and rambling allowed;
     - **page mode** (the card): the refined, final, important content.
   - **The flow runs right to left.** While a card is selected and the owner dictates in the sidebar, the AI refines the conversation into that card's page.jsonl. The card then shows the finalized points, and can become a task, a series of tasks, or an update to another page.
   - This replaces a separate "refined prompt card" pathway: item 7's refinement is written INTO the selected card.
   - **Open question for mastermind-servex-9:** voice and dictation sessions are global today (one session follows you across pages), not per directory. Should a session attach to the selected card or page?

- Replaces AI 2's own inbox code once it has moved. AI 2 then redirects, or stays as v1 until the owner approves (todo: "AI 2 merges into /framework/ai/").
- task-mastermind-ai-page owns /framework/ai/: add the Inbox tab together with it.
- task-mastermind-ai2-inbox-read (read/unread, archive, search) lands first. Carry its work over.

## Rules
- Pool worktree, then `merge.mjs` (smoke test), then the review skill. Screenshots at 400 and 1920.
- Budget: $12, hard. At most 2 Sonnet minions.

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

**Queued for after the weekly reset (10 PM, 2026-09-30).** The owner: "when we have time… running out of tokens".

## Asks
1. **A `System` class** (core, capital S): more than a page. A whole system of rules plus its actions and skills. /framework/design, /framework/code, /framework/ui and /framework/ux are instances of it, so an upgrade to the class reaches every system for free. They share the same docs top-tabs. mastermind-servex (the architect) reviews the shape, because design-code just built two of these pages by hand.
2. **/framework/ui/ is the library of approved building blocks:** layouts, widgets, cards, the HTML and which classes to use.
   - Every component is composed only of approved blocks, so there are no unapproved layouts.
   - A new component is fine, but it is built from approved blocks. If a block is missing, the agent requests one.
   - Reuse, never one-off.
3. **Class pills.** Show the CSS classes on each component as small tags, e.g. a section label naming a layout area (two-column, three-column) or a card's `pad`/`flex`. Seeing the classes is how you learn to reproduce a look.

   - Still show the real source beside each template, as the source of truth.
4. **Masonry preview grid:** mixed heights and widths with no voids, the smallest items at the top, and the order running across and then wrapping. It works at the four target widths (~400, ~1000, 1920, 3440). An earlier version may exist outside this repo.
5. **Previews at their native width, scaled:** a zoom that fits a set number per row (dynamic), with a manual slider, so a 3440 layout previews properly.
6. **The tree navigation (asked before):** the left rail previews the siblings and the right rail previews the children, so you drill down through variations. Check whether it was built.
7. **The /framework/ui/card/ page:** the demo renders about 2000 × 200 px and there's wasted space. Screenshot it at 3440, find the empty areas, and make it compact and meaningful. Keep the code beside the template. Every UI kind gets an optimal width.

## How a page becomes a System (checked 2026-09-30)
No swapping is needed. A page is already built as the right class from the start:
- **page.js:** `export default new System({...})`.
- **page.jsonl only:** line 1 carries `{"class": "/framework/core/System/System.js"}`. `PageLog` loads that module BEFORE it constructs anything (`core/Page/Log.js` about line 302, `log_class()`), and falls back to a plain Page if the module is not a Page subclass. The AI 2 cards already use this: `{"class": "/framework/ai2/card.js"}`.

So `System extends Page`. It starts as little more than the shared template: the top tabs, the readme chain, and the concept tiles. Methods get added as they become clear. **/framework/ai/ becomes a System too**, alongside design, code, ui and ux.
