# Plan: the AI page becomes the AI 2 inbox

![the target](plan.png)

**Before:** [AI 2 at 1920](shots/before-ai2-1920.png) has the inbox; [AI at 1920](shots/before-ai-1920.png) has only a placeholder.

**The idea in one line:** the AI 2 inbox becomes a class, `InboxRail`. The AI page's Inbox tab and AI 2 both use it, so nothing is copied and AI 2 keeps working as v1.

## Five small merges, in order

Each one is smoke-tested (`merge.mjs`) and screenshot-checked at 400 and 1920. AI 2 is shot before and after every merge; any difference is a regression and blocks the merge.

1. **`core/Page/ext/`: the extension system** (light, now). A page.jsonl line `{"ext": "Inbox"}` loads `core/Page/ext/Inbox/` and calls its `setup(page)`, the way `Server.use(Plugin)` does. Hooks are events on the page: `line` (each page.jsonl line) and `render`. The drawer's page inbox (`ext/drawer/inbox.js`) moves into `core/Page/ext/Inbox/`; the old file re-exports it. A message is `{"inbox": {type, author, text, at}}`; the older `from` still reads as `author`.
2. **`InboxRail`, the base class** (heavy, after 4:50). AI 2's `board()` closure becomes a class whose parts are methods: the head, the filters (Needs you, search, notes, archived), the rows, the pill, the detail and sub columns. `AIRail extends InboxRail` adds the usage meters, "+ New card" and auto-transcribe. AI 2 switches to `AIRail`, and must look identical.
3. **The Inbox tab on /framework/ai/** (heavy). The tab mounts `AIRail`. Cards open at their real address, `/framework/ai/2026/09/30/<card>/`, beside the rail. Live, sub-cards, read/unread, archive, auto-resolve, search and the Needs you filter all come with the class.
4. **The Log tab, same UI** (after 3). `LogRail extends InboxRail`: one row per task with its status dot; a click opens the task beside the rail. Tabs: Inbox · Log · System.
5. **A card shows what it is about** (after 4). The first refined-prompt card, posted by hand on [Now: one inbox everywhere](/framework/ai2/2026/09/30/now-one-inbox-everywhere-and-refined-pro/); a card's body previews the page it references (`#Page`, `/path`). The Servex prompt hook and Refine belong to mastermind-servex-9.

## Who builds

- Merge 1: one Sonnet minion, now.
- Merges 2 and 3: one Opus minion in one worktree (the refactor is the risky part; it is judged by a pixel check of AI 2).
- Merge 4 and 5: one Sonnet minion, after 3 lands.

## Not now

AI 2 is not redirected. It stays as v1 until the owner approves the move.

## Asks
1. **`core/Page/ext/`: an extension (plugin) system for Page,** modelled on the Server's plugin system (`Server/plugins/`): event-driven hooks, and extensions configured by data (in page.jsonl), not hard-coded. It is the ext pattern for any module or directory. Keep it minimal.
2. **`core/Page/ext/Inbox`:** the first extension. Any page can have an inbox.
   - Messaging a page = appending one line to its page.jsonl: `{inbox: {type: "message"|"question", author, text, at}}`.
   - The author is the agent that sent it. It's like emailing a directory.
   - Build on the page inbox that already landed ([page-inbox](../page-inbox/): notes live under the `inbox` key), and on the drawer inbox steps. Move it; don't rebuild it.
3. **Move the AI 2 Inbox to the new /framework/ai/** as its **default tab** (the dashboard; the owner, 2026-09-30); the docs live on its System tab. Keep every useful feature of today's Inbox: the sidebar on click, and read/unread, archive, auto-resolve and search from task ai2-inbox-read. The Inbox IS the default tab, so its top-priority items are what the page opens on.
4. **Needs you is a filter in the Inbox list,** not its own tab with its own UI.
5. **Inbox and Log share one UI:** the rail with previews, and each preview opens its card. Today the three tabs use three different templates. Lean into the Inbox's version.
   - Inbox: real time, only what matters now.
   - Log: everything.
6. **The rail is a base class, overridden per page** with object-oriented overrides. The usage meters live only on the AI page's rail subclass, not on every page's inbox.
7. **Each owner prompt becomes an Inbox card showing its refined version.** Servex hears each owner prompt (the `.claude/prompts/` hook, and voice sessions), runs it through the Refine ladder (`ext/Refine`: raw → structured), and posts or updates a card at the top of the Inbox. Post the first one by hand, on the card linked above, as the example.

8. **A card is a whole conversation, and it shows what it's about** (the owner, 2026-09-30). Each Inbox item stands for an entire conversation, which continues in the card's sidebar. The card's body shows at least part of the thing it references, imported live: a page, a module or a screenshot. Build this on the reference system (`#Page`, `/path`, task-mastermind-mentions), so every post makes it obvious what it's talking about.

9. **Chat and card are ONE content model** (the owner, 2026-09-30, the summary of the thread):
   - A card IS a page: a title, a preview and a detail view, backed by its own page.jsonl. It can be a conversation or an AI session, and it has its own inbox, which is its feed of updates.
   - **The two views are two renderings of the same lines and the same content widgets:**
     - **chat mode** (the right sidebar or the mobile rail): informal, with bubbles and rambling allowed;
     - **page mode** (the card): the refined, final, important content.
   - **The flow runs right to left.** While a card is selected and the owner dictates in the sidebar, the AI refines the conversation into that card's page.jsonl. The card then shows the finalized points, and can become a task, a series of tasks, or an update to another page.
   - This replaces a separate "refined prompt card" pathway: item 7's refinement is written INTO the selected card.
   - **Sessions stay GLOBAL** (the owner, 2026-09-30: answered). Clicking a link never cuts off dictation. The session is context-aware instead: each navigation is logged as an invisible event ("now on <page>, card <id>"), as are pause start and pause end, all timestamped. So the AI always knows what you are looking at, and refinement goes to the card that is selected when it happens.

# Minion brief: path modules are page extensions (merge 1b)

Load the `minion` skill first, then `code` and `documentation`. Parent: task-mastermind-inbox-ext. Task dir: `public/framework/ai/2026-09-30/inbox-ext/` — read `owner-words.md` (the last section is yours), `plan.md` (merge 1b), and `core/Page/ext/readme.md` in the worktree (merge 1, the extension system you build on).

## The owner's words (verbatim)

> we have some path specific page routes like the MD system. I think we have, I don't know if the, the route specific AI system is built. ... Let's make sure we document in our page system, the core page pages, the um, path specific modules. Those, those really should be extensions, right? Like, so if there's anything that creates a page subdirectory pattern, essentially, like the markdown, like the AI, maybe, uh, I don't remember, we might want like an editor one. So like any page slash edit creates like a whole module and workspace, essentially, like a, a directory for saving things. ... make sure those are documented properly so that we can, you know, see how that works.

## Where you work

Worktree `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\inbox-ext` (branch `worktree/inbox-ext`, server http://localhost:51490/). Commit after each piece. Don't merge; I merge.

## Deliverables, in order

1. **Find them all.** Every module that adds a sub-path or a workspace under any page. Start with `core/Page/Markdown.js`, `core/Page/ai/`, `core/Page/dynamic/`, `core/Page/make/`, and any `/edit` route; grep `route(` in `core/Page/Page.class.js` and `core/Page/*.js` for others. For each: the path it adds, the file that adds it, where it saves, and whether it is built or only planned. Write the list to your task dir as `modules.md` (a table).
2. **Document each as an extension.** On the core/Page pages: `core/Page/ext/readme.md` gets a section "Path extensions" listing each one in a line (the path it adds, where it saves, a link to its own page); the ext demo page shows the list as a table or previews; each module's own readme gets one line saying it is a path extension and linking back.
3. **Move the cheap ones onto `core/Page/ext/`.** "Cheap" means: a module turned on by a hard-coded check in `Page.class.js` that can become a `Page.use(Ext)` or `{"ext": ...}` line with fewer than ~30 changed lines, and every existing url still works. Move files only if the move is a re-export away from safe. For each one you don't move, write the seam in one line (what would have to change) in `modules.md`.
4. **Proof.** Headless (Playwright, `windowsHide: true`) on the worktree server: every url in `modules.md` loads with zero console errors, before and after; the core/Page ext page at 400 and 1920. Shots in `path-ext/shots/`.

## Fence

`core/Page/ext/**`, `core/Page/Markdown.js`, `core/Page/ai/**`, `core/Page/dynamic/**`, `core/Page/make/**`, `core/Page/Page.class.js` (the smallest edits, only for a move), `core/Page/readme.md`, the readmes of the modules you document. Nothing in `ai2/`, `ai/`, `ux/`, Servex.

## Rules

`windowsHide: true` on every process; stop every server you start. Log steps and decisions in your task.jsonl. No cap; do it right. When done, message task-mastermind-inbox-ext: commits, shots, what was moved and what was only documented.

# Minion brief: AI 2 freezes for about 13 seconds on load

Load the `minion` skill first, then `code`. Parent: task-mastermind-inbox-ext. Task dir: `public/framework/ai/2026-09-30/inbox-ext/`. The owner's words are in its `owner-words.md`, in the last section.

## The owner's words (verbatim)

> I think the page just crashed. My cursor is a pointer and it's not changing. Let me duplicate this tab and close it out. Yeah, it's, it's having a hard time loading. The framework AI2 live page

## What we already know

servex-mastermind-opus measured it headless at 1920. After `load`, the main thread is blocked for about 13 s: an evaluate call sent at t+2 s returned at t+17 s. The page has about 4,900 DOM nodes, a 40 MB heap, and three 404s.

The probe is [probe.mjs](probe.mjs) in this folder. Run it with `node probe.mjs <url>`; it uses the global Playwright.

## Where you work

Worktree `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\inbox-ext` (branch `worktree/inbox-ext`, server http://localhost:51490/). Commit there. Don't merge; I merge.

## Deliverables, in order

1. **Find the cause.** Take a CPU profile over the first 20 s of loading `/framework/ai2/` on the worktree server. Use CDP `Profiler.start`/`stop` through Playwright, with `windowsHide: true`. Name the functions that hold the thread, with file, line and self time. Put the top ten in `ai2-hang/profile.md`, with one sentence on why each is slow, e.g. a loop that re-renders every card for every line, a layout thrash, or a render of all 4,900 nodes at once. Also name the three 404s and say whether each one matters.
2. **Fix it, if the fix is small and in AI 2's own files** (`ai2/**`, or `ext/drawer/**` if the cause is there). The goal is main-thread lag under 200 ms after the page settles, and the first rows on screen within 2 s. Keep everything AI 2 shows today. If the fix is large or outside those files, don't build it: write the plan in `profile.md` and message me.
   - **Don't touch** the `board()` closure's structure beyond the fix. Another minion turns it into a class next; keep your change small and local so theirs merges cleanly.
3. **Proof.** Take shots of `/framework/ai2/` at 400 and 1920, before and after, in `ai2-hang/shots/`. They must look the same apart from the fix. Record the probe output before and after in `profile.md`. Zero new console errors.

## Fence

`ai2/**` (smallest edits), `ext/drawer/**` (only if the cause is there), and this folder. Nothing in `core/Page/`, `ai/`, `ux/` or Servex.

## Rules

`windowsHide: true` on every process. Stop any browser or server you start. Log each step in your task.jsonl. When you're done, message task-mastermind-inbox-ext with the cause in one sentence, the commit, and the before and after numbers.

# Grip: the resize handle's zones, and names for the layouts: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

## The widget
The resize handle is **the grip**: [`ext/grip`](/framework/ext/grip/) (grip.js, grip.css). It's ONE system, used everywhere a column resizes. Keep the little orange pill exactly as it is.

## The bug
The grip is a 0.75rem strip placed just INSIDE the rail's edge (grip.css: `width: 0.75rem`, `inset-inline-start: 0`). So it extends left over the rail's own scrollbar and barely at all to the right, and on the AI 2 Inbox you can't grab the preview rail's scrollbar.

## Asks
1. **Two invisible zones:**
   - **Show zone (about 50 px radius):** the separator line and the pill appear.
   - **Grab zone (smaller):** the resize cursor appears and a drag works, even when you're not exactly on the pill. It extends about 5–10 px to the right and up or down, but only about **1 px toward the scrollbar**, so the scrollbar right beside it stays easy to grab.
2. **The same on every grip surface:** check each one (grip-everywhere, 2026-09-29, listed the surfaces), both x and y axes, in both directions.
3. **Names.** The grip's page says in one line what it's called and where it lives, so "where's the resize handle?" is answered with a link. On the same page, name the layout it sits in: the **preview rail** (a flush stack of previews, persistent navigation) beside the **detail**. Reuse names already in [/framework/design/layout/](/framework/design/layout/): "flush stack" is there. Record the names in the design system's naming list, not only here.
4. **No regressions.** Screenshots at 400 and 1920 on each surface. Mobile has no hover, so touch keeps working as it does today.

## Rules
Quick-fix pool: `take_worktree`, then `merge.mjs` (smoke test), then the review skill. Small and clear, so build it directly; there's no plan step. The owner uses AI 2 now, so check /framework/ai2/ first.

# Padding: percentage padding, and wrappers for grid items: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

**Queued for the 10 PM weekly reset (2026-09-30).** Foundational, so no cap. Plan first, with screenshots, on a card.

## The owner's model
- **Responsive padding = percentage padding, not container queries.** A `%` padding resolves against the PARENT's width, so an element can't size its padding from its own container query without an extra wrapper. The owner prefers percentages.
- **The rule:** % padding is right when the parent and the padded element are roughly the same width (a page, a single column, a card that fills its parent). Then the padding tracks the element's own size.
- **Grids and flex columns (2+ columns):** a % on a card resolves against the WHOLE grid, so every card gets huge padding at 3440. So each grid item gets a **wrapper** (a column or section wrapper, one per item), and the card inside it takes % padding against the wrapper. Accept the cost to drag and drop. A single full-width section needs no wrapper.
- Use a wrapper container (cqi) only if a sub-item truly needs to listen to it. The owner sees no strong need for that.

## Today
`framework.css`: `--pad: calc(clamp(1em, 2.6% - 1.1em, 4em) * var(--size))`, already a % of the containing block, plus `--pad-card`, a different band. Memory also mentions "columns cqi pads". Reconcile these with the model above.

## Asks
1. **Write the padding rule as a named sub-system of layout,** in [/framework/design/layout/](/framework/design/layout/): when % padding is right, when a wrapper is needed, and the name of the wrapper class. Show it, don't tell it: screenshots at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440.
2. **Add the wrapper class** (for example a column or section wrapper; check the naming list and css-scopes first). Use it in the grids that need it.
3. **Fix the case the owner saw:** an AI 2 card page ("Dictation: one configurable widget everywhere") whose padding is far too small. Find why it doesn't get the scaling default.
4. **A review question** for the review skill: "does each padded element resolve its % against a parent of about its own width?"

# Padding: percentage padding, and wrappers for grid items: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

**Queued for the 10 PM weekly reset (2026-09-30).** Foundational, so no cap. Plan first, with screenshots, on a card.

## The owner's model
- **Responsive padding = percentage padding, not container queries.** A `%` padding resolves against the PARENT's width, so an element can't size its padding from its own container query without an extra wrapper. The owner prefers percentages.
- **The rule:** % padding is right when the parent and the padded element are roughly the same width (a page, a single column, a card that fills its parent). Then the padding tracks the element's own size.
- **Grids and flex columns (2+ columns):** a % on a card resolves against the WHOLE grid, so every card gets huge padding at 3440. So each grid item gets a **wrapper** (a column or section wrapper, one per item), and the card inside it takes % padding against the wrapper. Accept the cost to drag and drop. A single full-width section needs no wrapper.
- Use a wrapper container (cqi) only if a sub-item truly needs to listen to it. The owner sees no strong need for that.

## Today
`framework.css`: `--pad: calc(clamp(1em, 2.6% - 1.1em, 4em) * var(--size))`, already a % of the containing block, plus `--pad-card`, a different band. Memory also mentions "columns cqi pads". Reconcile these with the model above.

1. **Write the padding rule as a named sub-system of layout,** in [/framework/design/layout/](/framework/design/layout/): when % padding is right, when a wrapper is needed, and the name of the wrapper class. Show it, don't tell it: screenshots at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440.
2. **Add the wrapper class** (for example a column or section wrapper; check the naming list and css-scopes first). Use it in the grids that need it.
3. **Fix the case the owner saw:** an AI 2 card page ("Dictation: one configurable widget everywhere") whose padding is far too small. Find why it doesn't get the scaling default.
4. **A review question** for the review skill: "does each padded element resolve its % against a parent of about its own width?"

# Minion brief: the Inbox shows only what matters (priority 50 and up)

Load the `minion` skill first, then `code`. Parent: task-mastermind-inbox-ext. Task dir: `public/framework/ai/2026-09-30/inbox-ext/`. Read its `owner-words.md`, last section ("Inbox = priority 50+, Log = everything"), before anything.

## The owner's words (verbatim, the part that is yours)

> What goes into the inbox needs to be top priority. And maybe it's even like, um, I don't know, maybe we need a priority filter on top of the inbox. And really, the, maybe the difference between the inbox and the log is just based on that priority. Like log is everything. And inbox is only like priority of 50 and above or, or whatever. And then we have a, a way to score the priority so that only top priority things get to the inbox. Because I'm seeing these cards appear that don't make much sense. This one says six, has a 60. It leads, well, first it leads with like a time, an hourglass with a cross through it. I don't know which icon that is. I don't know what that means, but... Um, the uh, dictation, it says 60, dictation, one configurable widget everywhere, widget first on the page. Uh, that doesn't make much sense to me. I don't remember this.

## What is wrong today

- Only a card with an open need (`needs-rule.js` `importance()`, via `needs.js` `score_for`) and a stalled ask get a real score. Every other row has none, so a "50 and up" filter would be guesswork.
- A **stalled ask** (an ask whose owner agent went quiet, from `ai/asks.jsonl`) scores 60 to 80 (`IMPORTANCE.STALLED_*`) and shows as an unreadable icon (`hourglass_disabled`) plus ledger shorthand the owner doesn't recognise. But the owner has nothing to do about it: CLAUDE.md law 5 says the system revives the quiet agent itself.

## Deliverables, in order (commit each)

1. **One written scoring rule, 0 to 100, for every Inbox row.** In `needs-rule.js` (it is the one rule three callers share), next to `IMPORTANCE`, write down in a short comment table what scores 50 or more: only things the owner must act on (a blocker, an open decision or question an agent is waiting on, a finished task waiting for the owner's look). Everything else, including a card that just updated, a landed task nobody asked the owner about, and a note, scores below 50. Give every row kind a score (`importance()` gets the kinds it doesn't know today), so each row in `items()` (`inbox.js`) has a number.
2. **A stalled ask drops below 50** (the owner has nothing to do; Servex revives the owner agent — queued by mastermind-servex-9, see deliverable 3). It stays in the Log (everything) and in the asks ledger. The one exception: a stalled ask whose text says it needs the owner (a blocker word, as `blocker_signal` already reads) keeps 50+.
3. **A stalled-ask row reads as a plain sentence.** No `hourglass_disabled` icon. Title: what was asked, in words the owner would recognise (use the ask's own words or card title, not the ledger id shorthand). Under it: who owns it and how long it has been quiet, e.g. "Asked of mastermind-servex-9 · quiet 3 h · flagged by Servex". End it "Servex is reviving it" only when the ask's latest line in `asks.jsonl` carries `revived_at` (mastermind-servex-9 is adding that revive; today Servex only marks the stall, so today every stalled row ends "flagged by Servex"). Files: `inbox.js` (the stalled `add({...})`, ~line 780) and `faces.js` if the row face needs it.
4. **Proof.** A table in `priority/scores.md`: every row on today's AI 2 Inbox with its kind, its score before and after, and whether it is in (≥50) or out. Read the "in" list as the owner would: would they want every one of those in front of them? A shot of a stalled row before and after at 1920 in `priority/shots/`. Zero new console errors on `/framework/ai2/`. The existing tests of `needs-rule.js` (grep for its importers under `Servex/` and `ai2/`) still pass.

The **filter itself** (a threshold at the top of the rail, default 50, that the owner can move; Inbox = 50 and up, Log = everything) is built by the rail minion into `InboxRail`. It reads each row's `score`, so your only contract with it is: every row has a numeric `score`.

## Where you work

Worktree `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\inbox-ext` (branch `worktree/inbox-ext`, server http://localhost:51490/). The rail minion works in the same worktree on `ai2/page.js`, `ai2/rail.js`, `ai2.css` and `ux/Inbox/`; stay out of those. Commit after each finished piece. Don't merge; I merge.

## Fence

`ai2/needs-rule.js`, `ai2/inbox.js` (the scoring and the stalled row only), `ai2/faces.js` (the stalled row face only), `ai2/needs.js` if `score_for` must change, and this folder. Servex reads `needs-rule.js` too (`Servex/cards/Cards.js`): don't change any exported function's shape.

## Rules

`windowsHide: true` on every process. Stop any browser or server you start. Log each step and decision in your task.jsonl. When done, message task-mastermind-inbox-ext: the commits, the "in" list, what's left.

# Grip: the resize handle's zones, and names for the layouts: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

## The widget
The resize handle is **the grip**: [`ext/grip`](/framework/ext/grip/) (grip.js, grip.css). It's ONE system, used everywhere a column resizes. Keep the little orange pill exactly as it is.

## The bug
The grip is a 0.75rem strip placed just INSIDE the rail's edge (grip.css: `width: 0.75rem`, `inset-inline-start: 0`). So it extends left over the rail's own scrollbar and barely at all to the right, and on the AI 2 Inbox you can't grab the preview rail's scrollbar.

## Asks
1. **Two invisible zones:**
   - **Show zone (about 50 px radius):** the separator line and the pill appear.
   - **Grab zone (smaller):** the resize cursor appears and a drag works, even when you're not exactly on the pill. It extends about 5–10 px to the right and up or down, but only about **1 px toward the scrollbar**, so the scrollbar right beside it stays easy to grab.
2. **The same on every grip surface:** check each one (grip-everywhere, 2026-09-29, listed the surfaces), both x and y axes, in both directions.
3. **Names.** The grip's page says in one line what it's called and where it lives, so "where's the resize handle?" is answered with a link. On the same page, name the layout it sits in: the **preview rail** (a flush stack of previews, persistent navigation) beside the **detail**. Reuse names already in [/framework/design/layout/](/framework/design/layout/): "flush stack" is there. Record the names in the design system's naming list, not only here.
4. **No regressions.** Screenshots at 400 and 1920 on each surface. Mobile has no hover, so touch keeps working as it does today.

## Rules
Quick-fix pool: `take_worktree`, then `merge.mjs` (smoke test), then the review skill. Small and clear, so build it directly; there's no plan step. The owner uses AI 2 now, so check /framework/ai2/ first.

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

## The widget
The resize handle is **the grip**: [`ext/grip`](/framework/ext/grip/) (grip.js, grip.css). It's ONE system, used everywhere a column resizes. Keep the little orange pill exactly as it is.

## The bug
The grip is a 0.75rem strip placed just INSIDE the rail's edge (grip.css: `width: 0.75rem`, `inset-inline-start: 0`). So it extends left over the rail's own scrollbar and barely at all to the right, and on the AI 2 Inbox you can't grab the preview rail's scrollbar.

Reuse names already in [/framework/design/layout/](/framework/design/layout/): "flush stack" is there. Record the names in the design system's naming list, not only here.
4. **No regressions.** Screenshots at 400 and 1920 on each surface. Mobile has no hover, so touch keeps working as it does today.

verdict: fix

1. [fix] Only two of the four surfaces moved to the one component. The mobile sheet (`ext/drawer/rail.js:53`) and the desktop drawer's AI tab (`ext/drawer/tabs/ai.js:194`) now call `chat()`. The AI 2 card sidebar (Servex `agents/Layers.js` page-ai, the old `assistant-<card>` with its model chooser) and the dev bar's chat mode are not touched, and `/api/page-ai` still does not feed the pair. That was ask 1, the main point of the task.
2. [fix] The font is fixed by adding a style, which is what ask 5 ruled out ("fix it by where it mounts, not by adding CSS"). `ux/Dictate/chat.js:417` `fix_font()` copies `.theme-lew42`'s font onto the mount as an inline style. The real cause is named in `ext/drawer/readme.md:157`: `drawer.js` `build()` queries `.app` before it exists and falls back to `<body>`. Fix `build()` so it waits for the app or uses the View captor chain, then delete `fix_font`.
3. [fix] Every time the drawer's AI tab opens, it leaks a poller and an EventSource. `tabs/ai.js:199` calls `chat()` and never keeps the handle or calls `remove()`. Each re-fill of the drawer runs `ai()` again (`tabs.js:118` → `drawer(this.fill)`), which adds another 1.5 s `Session.watch` poll (`ext/Session/Session.js:102`), another `Session.stream` EventSource and another `subscribe(attach)` listener. The detached widgets keep all of these alive for the life of the page. Call `mount.remove()` when the tab's content is replaced.
4. [fix] Ask 3 is only partly done. `Session.nav()` gets `{from, to}` pages only (`chat.js:486`). There is no card in the event, even though `rail.js:101` `sync_card()` reads the card and then drops it. Nothing in the diff logs `pause start` / `pause end`, and nothing routes refinement to the card that is selected at the time.
5. [fix] Ask 4 is not addressed: chat and card do not yet share one content model. The chat still draws through `Widget`'s own bubble path (`chat.js:588` `draw()` → `panel.say({chat})`), and the diff never renders the card's content widgets from JSONL lines.
6. [fix] Ask 6 is missing. The diff adds no `page.js` that shows the live widget on each surface and how each surface creates it. The readme section (`ux/Dictate/readme.md:662`) is words, not the page the owner asked for.
7. [fix] The diff has no screenshot proof. The brief asks for every surface at 400 and 1920 before each merge, but `shots/` holds only `before-drawer-ai-3440.png`. Nothing proves the mobile rail did not regress, or that the sheet collapses to one line (ask 2).
8. [note] The Sessions tab lists voice sessions "on this page" (`tabs/sessions.js:278`, `Session.recent(page)`). A global session started on another page won't show up there, even when it is the live one. Now that sessions are global, list the browser tab's recent sessions instead.
9. [note] `ago()` is now copied three times (`chat.js:430`, `tabs/sessions.js:249`, rail.js), which breaks law 6. `sessions.js` already imports `chat.js`, so export `ago` from there and have the others import it.
10. [note] `DrawerRailSheetPanel` and `aiV2` still carry the whole old private-session code. Keeping them reachable follows the house rule. But until the old code is actually dead, "one set of code" is not true yet, so say that on the card.
11. [note] The good part: `chat.js`'s single controller (one `sessionStorage` session, `watch()` from line 0 on every mount, `own_ats` de-dupe, `report_nav` dedupe) is simple and is the right core. It fixes the "vanishing messages on rebuild" bug. The drawer thread un-cap (`drawer.css:20`) is also a correct one-line fix for the full-height ask.

**Before, at 3440:** [the card page](shots/before/monorepo-localhost-framework-ui-card/3440.png) draws a 200px-tall card across about 2000px, with its source far off to the right. **At 1920:** [the UI wall](shots/before/monorepo-localhost-framework-ui/1920.png) leaves holes wherever one card in a band is taller than the rest.

All of it is built in one worktree, `worktree/ui-system`, and merged in small pieces, each checked at 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440.

## Wave 1: four builders at once, on separate files

| | What | Owner's ask | Files it may touch |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | `System`, a core class. Design, Code, UI, UX and AI become Systems and share the docs top tabs. | 1 | `core/System/` (new), the five landing `page.js` files |
| **B** | The masonry preview wall: no holes, smallest items first, order runs across. Previews draw at their own width and are scaled down, with a zoom slider. | 4, 5 | `ext/catalog/`, `styles/layouts/masonry/` |
| **C** | Class pills: every component's CSS classes, shown as small tags. A compact card page, with the code beside the template. An ideal width for each kind of component. | 3, 7 | `ui/classes/` (new), `ui/card/`, `ext/demo/` |
| **G** | Padding: the rule for % padding, a wrapper class for grid items, a fix for the AI 2 card's thin padding, and a review question. | padding 1 to 4 | `framework.css` (padding only), `design/layout/` |

## Wave 2: after Wave 1 merges

| | What | Ask | Waits on |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D** | The tree rails: siblings previewed on the left, children on the right, so you can drill down through variations. | 6 | B |
| **E** | The dev bar's Structure tree uses the library's icon tree (`ui/tree`). | 8 | nothing (small) |
| **H** | `/framework/ui/` becomes the library of approved blocks: the rule (built only from approved blocks), the request path for a missing block, and a names index where "what's it called?" is answered by a link. | 2, 10 | A, B, C |
| **F** | Task pages: done items read as green ticks, not disabled boxes; the steps bar keeps a sane width; the Report is free content. | 9 | A |

## Decisions

- **`System extends Doc`, not plain `Page`.** The owner asked for "the same docs top tabs", and `Doc` already draws them as routed child pages. Building a second tab system on `Page` would break law 6. The alternative was `System extends Page`, copying the AI page's hand-built tabs. Doc is itself a Page, so a `{"class": ".../System.js"}` line in page.jsonl still works.
- **The masonry extends `.packed`/`pack()`** (`styles/layouts/masonry/`), which already keeps reading order across. It does not add a second masonry.
- **Padding:** a % padding on a **grid** item already resolves against its own grid area, but on a **flex** item it resolves against the whole row. G measures this before naming the wrapper, and uses the wrapper only where the measurement says it is needed.

The demo stage overhaul, and editing the template source in place.

+## `paper: true` narrows `head`/`foot` to `main`'s own column, and reuses `--well` rather than a framework token
+
+The brief (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper/requirements.md`) drew the nine-grid as three real
+rows and three real columns — `. head .` / `left main right` / `. foot .` — not the plain grid's
+`head head head` / `left main right` / `foot foot foot`, where the header and footer already span
+every column. That difference is not cosmetic: the brief's whole point is that a header's text
+lines up with the paper's own left edge, and a header spanning the full width (even one whose
+*text* was then padded to look aligned) would still sit *over* `left`, which is exactly the "reads
+like it belongs to something else" problem `design-2.md` is about. So paper mode gets its own
+`grid-template-areas`, not a padding trick on the existing one — `head`/`foot` are only ever above/
+below `main`, and the four corners are cells nobody ever puts a box in (the same "no content, no
+box" rule the plain grid already uses for a region you leave out), painted by the grid's own
+background rather than four extra divs.
+
+That background is `--well: light-dark(rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06), rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35))` — not `--tint`
+(0.035, measurably lighter) or `--wash` (0.08, a generic fill used for code blocks and table
+heads), but the *exact* value `ai2.css` and `ext/Doc/Doc.css` already use for their own gray
+header bands. The brief asked to "pick the one that reads as the AI 2 header band's gray" — the
+closest answer wasn't picking between framework.css's two general-purpose tokens, it was reusing
+the specific value two other modules already settled on for this same look. Neither of those files
+exports `--well` as a shared token (it's declared locally in each), so this is a third, separate
+declaration of the same number rather than a new dependency between unrelated modules — if a
+fourth "well" shows up, hoisting all three into one framework.css token is the fix, not something
+this task's fence reaches.
+
+**Paper mode's regions lose their own border** (`.core-shell-head`/`-foot`/`-left`/`-right`
+border: 0, under `.core-shell-paper`). The plain grid's borders are dividing lines for regions
+sitting flush against `main` with nothing between them; paper mode already separates every region
+from the paper with `gap: var(--gap-25)`, so a line AND a gap together would read as two edges
+doing the same job. Only `main` keeps a border — it's the paper's own edge, not a divider.
+
+**Stacking below 34em needed an explicit override, not just "it already works."** The plain grid's
+`@media (width < 34em)` rule (`.core-shell-grid { grid-template-areas: "head" "left" "main"
+"right" "foot"; … }`) matches a paper shell too — it's the same element, one extra class — but
+`.core-shell-grid.core-shell-paper`'s own un-media-gated rule has higher specificity (two classes
+vs. one) and would otherwise keep trying to lay out three columns in a one-column space. The fix
+is one more rule, inside that same media block, restating the identical stacked areas under the
+two-class selector so it wins the specificity tie by coming later in the file — not a new stacked
+shape, the SAME one the plain grid already had.
+
+## The `left`/`right` clamp used to floor at 12rem inside a `container-type` ancestor — fixed by moving the clamp off the ITEM and onto the grid's own COLUMN
+
+First found in the paper demo (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper-demo/requirements.md`):
+`left`/`right` rendered as bare words with no visible rail. `.core-shell-left`/`-right`'s own
+`width: clamp(12rem, var(--core-shell-left-w, 18rem), 50%)` should render at 18rem (288px) by
+default — nothing writes `--core-shell-left-w` until a drag happens — but measured inside
+`ext/demo`'s own `.demo-stage` (a `container-type: inline-size` box, `ext/demo/stage.css`), it
+rendered at exactly 192px, the clamp's own 12rem FLOOR, instead. This reproduced even with a
+literal `width: clamp(12rem, 18rem, 50%)` and no `var()` at all. The same root cause, the other
+direction, had already hit `dev/DevShell`: its own `right` rail holds long paragraphs of real
+text, whose max-content width is "the whole paragraph on one line" (over 1000px), so instead of
+flooring, that side's `auto` TRACK ballooned past the page's own middle and the rail never
+reached the window's edge (`DevShell.css`, before this fix).
+
+**The cause:** CSS Grid sizes an `auto` COLUMN from each item's own preferred (intrinsic) width
+before the grid's final width is known. Resolving that preferred width means resolving the
+item's own `width: clamp(…, 50%)` — and inside a size-containment context (`container-type:
+inline-size` on an ancestor, which every `ext/demo` stage is), that intrinsic-sizing pass
+resolves a percentage against an indefinite size as `0`. `clamp(12rem, 18rem, 0px)` floors to
+12rem; a huge max-content paragraph instead drags the `auto` track the other way. Both symptoms
+are the same bug: an `auto` TRACK asking an ITEM what size it wants, when that item's own size
+depends on a percentage of the very track being measured.
+
+**The fix (this task, in `Shell.css` itself, not a workaround in `page.js` or `DevShell.css`):**
+move the `clamp()` off the item's `width` and onto the COLUMN, as an explicit track size instead
+of `auto` — an explicit track resolves its own percentage against the grid's (already known)
+content box, no item-intrinsic-sizing pass involved, so the floor/balloon bug has nothing left to
+trigger on. `.core-shell-grid` now carries two custom properties, `--core-shell-col-left` /
+`-right`, defaulting to the keyword `auto` (so a MISSING rail still collapses its column to zero
+width — the same "no content, no box" trick this file already uses everywhere else); a media
+query (`width >= 34em`, matching the existing 34em stack breakpoint) sets each one to
+`clamp(12rem, var(--core-shell-left-w, 18rem), 50%)` only when that rail actually exists
+(`.core-shell-grid:has(> .core-shell-left)` / `:has(> .core-shell-right)`). `.core-shell-left`/
+`-right` themselves are now just `width: auto` — they fill whichever column the grid already
+decided on, rather than sizing themselves a second time. Below 34em the existing stacked-layout
+rule still sets `grid-template-columns: 1fr` directly, which wins the cascade over these two
+variables regardless (same selector, later in the file), so phone layout is unaffected.
+
+Both `page.js`'s paper demo and `dev/DevShell/DevShell.css` had local workarounds for this same
+bug (an inline `width` on `$left`/`$right`, and a duplicate `grid-template-columns` +

+`Shell.css`. The paper demo still asks for two specific widths the brief named (the chat box at

+same custom property a drag or `Shell.size()` already writes; this is the intended mechanism,
+not a bypass.

+## `paper: true` narrows `head`/`foot` to `main`'s own column, and reuses `--well` rather than a framework token
+
+The brief (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper/requirements.md`) drew the nine-grid as three real
+rows and three real columns — `. head .` / `left main right` / `. foot .` — not the plain grid's
+`head head head` / `left main right` / `foot foot foot`, where the header and footer already span
+every column. That difference is not cosmetic: the brief's whole point is that a header's text
+lines up with the paper's own left edge, and a header spanning the full width (even one whose
+*text* was then padded to look aligned) would still sit *over* `left`, which is exactly the "reads
+like it belongs to something else" problem `design-2.md` is about. So paper mode gets its own
+`grid-template-areas`, not a padding trick on the existing one — `head`/`foot` are only ever above/
+below `main`, and the four corners are cells nobody ever puts a box in (the same "no content, no
+box" rule the plain grid already uses for a region you leave out), painted by the grid's own
+background rather than four extra divs.

+heads), but the *exact* value `ai2.css` and `ext/Doc/Doc.css` already use for their own gray

+declaration of the same number rather than a new dependency between unrelated modules — if a
+fourth "well" shows up, hoisting all three into one framework.css token is the fix, not something
+this task's fence reaches.

+from the paper with `gap: var(--gap-25)`, so a line AND a gap together would read as two edges
+doing the same job. Only `main` keeps a border — it's the paper's own edge, not a divider.

+`left`/`right` rendered as bare words with no visible rail. `.core-shell-left`/`-right`'s own

+## `paper: true` narrows `head`/`foot` to `main`'s own column, and reuses `--well` rather than a framework token
+
+The brief (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper/requirements.md`) drew the nine-grid as three real
+rows and three real columns — `. head .` / `left main right` / `. foot .` — not the plain grid's
+`head head head` / `left main right` / `foot foot foot`, where the header and footer already span
+every column. That difference is not cosmetic: the brief's whole point is that a header's text
+lines up with the paper's own left edge, and a header spanning the full width (even one whose
+*text* was then padded to look aligned) would still sit *over* `left`, which is exactly the "reads
+like it belongs to something else" problem `design-2.md` is about. So paper mode gets its own
+`grid-template-areas`, not a padding trick on the existing one — `head`/`foot` are only ever above/
+below `main`, and the four corners are cells nobody ever puts a box in (the same "no content, no
+box" rule the plain grid already uses for a region you leave out), painted by the grid's own
+background rather than four extra divs.
+
+That background is `--well: light-dark(rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06), rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35))` — not `--tint`
+(0.035, measurably lighter) or `--wash` (0.08, a generic fill used for code blocks and table
+heads), but the *exact* value `ai2.css` and `ext/Doc/Doc.css` already use for their own gray
+header bands. The brief asked to "pick the one that reads as the AI 2 header band's gray" — the
+closest answer wasn't picking between framework.css's two general-purpose tokens, it was reusing
+the specific value two other modules already settled on for this same look. Neither of those files
+exports `--well` as a shared token (it's declared locally in each), so this is a third, separate
+declaration of the same number rather than a new dependency between unrelated modules — if a
+fourth "well" shows up, hoisting all three into one framework.css token is the fix, not something
+this task's fence reaches.
+
+**Paper mode's regions lose their own border** (`.core-shell-head`/`-foot`/`-left`/`-right`
+border: 0, under `.core-shell-paper`). The plain grid's borders are dividing lines for regions
+sitting flush against `main` with nothing between them; paper mode already separates every region
+from the paper with `gap: var(--gap-25)`, so a line AND a gap together would read as two edges
+doing the same job. Only `main` keeps a border — it's the paper's own edge, not a divider.
+
+**Stacking below 34em needed an explicit override, not just "it already works."** The plain grid's
+`@media (width < 34em)` rule (`.core-shell-grid { grid-template-areas: "head" "left" "main"
+"right" "foot"; … }`) matches a paper shell too — it's the same element, one extra class — but
+`.core-shell-grid.core-shell-paper`'s own un-media-gated rule has higher specificity (two classes
+vs. one) and would otherwise keep trying to lay out three columns in a one-column space. The fix
+is one more rule, inside that same media block, restating the identical stacked areas under the
+two-class selector so it wins the specificity tie by coming later in the file — not a new stacked
+shape, the SAME one the plain grid already had.

+
+First found in the paper demo (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper-demo/requirements.md`):
+`left`/`right` rendered as bare words with no visible rail. `.core-shell-left`/`-right`'s own
+`width: clamp(12rem, var(--core-shell-left-w, 18rem), 50%)` should render at 18rem (288px) by
+default — nothing writes `--core-shell-left-w` until a drag happens — but measured inside
+`ext/demo`'s own `.demo-stage` (a `container-type: inline-size` box, `ext/demo/stage.css`), it
+rendered at exactly 192px, the clamp's own 12rem FLOOR, instead. This reproduced even with a
+literal `width: clamp(12rem, 18rem, 50%)` and no `var()` at all. The same root cause, the other
+direction, had already hit `dev/DevShell`: its own `right` rail holds long paragraphs of real
+text, whose max-content width is "the whole paragraph on one line" (over 1000px), so instead of
+flooring, that side's `auto` TRACK ballooned past the page's own middle and the rail never
+reached the window's edge (`DevShell.css`, before this fix).

+**The cause:** CSS Grid sizes an `auto` COLUMN from each item's own preferred (intrinsic) width
+before the grid's final width is known. Resolving that preferred width means resolving the
+item's own `width: clamp(…, 50%)` — and inside a size-containment context (`container-type:
+inline-size` on an ancestor, which every `ext/demo` stage is), that intrinsic-sizing pass
+resolves a percentage against an indefinite size as `0`. `clamp(12rem, 18rem, 0px)` floors to
+12rem; a huge max-content paragraph instead drags the `auto` track the other way. Both symptoms
+are the same bug: an `auto` TRACK asking an ITEM what size it wants, when that item's own size
+depends on a percentage of the very track being measured.

+move the `clamp()` off the item's `width` and onto the COLUMN, as an explicit track size instead
+of `auto` — an explicit track resolves its own percentage against the grid's (already known)
+content box, no item-intrinsic-sizing pass involved, so the floor/balloon bug has nothing left to
+trigger on. `.core-shell-grid` now carries two custom properties, `--core-shell-col-left` /
+`-right`, defaulting to the keyword `auto` (so a MISSING rail still collapses its column to zero
+width — the same "no content, no box" trick this file already uses everywhere else); a media

+(`.core-shell-grid:has(> .core-shell-left)` / `:has(> .core-shell-right)`). `.core-shell-left`/
+`-right` themselves are now just `width: auto` — they fill whichever column the grid already
+decided on, rather than sizing themselves a second time. Below 34em the existing stacked-layout
+rule still sets `grid-template-columns: 1fr` directly, which wins the cascade over these two
+variables regardless (same selector, later in the file), so phone layout is unaffected.

+## The ☰ and the drawer's own head read as SITE level, not AI 2's (2026-09-30)
+
+The problem (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper/requirements.md`, screenshot
+`1920-drawer.png`): AI 2's own gray header band (its title and tabs) ran to the drawer's
+edge, the floating ☰ still sat inside that same band while the drawer was open, and the
+drawer's own tab row sat at the same height as the page's tab row — so the whole thing
+read as one wide toolbar belonging to AI 2, not as a second piece of site chrome. Three
+changes, `drawer.css` only (no DOM changes — `drawer.js`/`tabs.js` are outside this task's
+fence):
+
+- **The floating ☰ disappears while the drawer is open.** One rule: `body:has(.drawer.on)
+  .drawer-menu { display: none; }`. Two buttons that both close the same rail — the ✕ inside
+  it and a ☰ floating over the page — was itself part of the "this belongs to the page" read.
+  `body`, not `.app`: measured with Playwright that opening the drawer by its routed
+  `?drawer=` url on a cold load hits `drawer.js`'s own documented fallback ("Inside `.app`,
+  not on `<body>`" — that comment names `.app` as the intended mount and `<body>` as what
+  happens when `.app` doesn't exist yet the first time `build()` runs), landing `.drawer.on`
+  as a direct child of `<body>`, not inside `.app` at all. A selector scoped to `.app` would
+  have silently missed exactly that case and left the ☰ showing on a cold `?drawer=` load —
+  `body` is the one ancestor both the normal case and the fallback always share.
+- **The drawer's own head now reads like `core/Sidebar`'s own head** — the "Framework"
+  brand row over its gray filter band — instead of a thin tab strip flush with whatever the
+  page's own header band is doing right next to it. `--darken-2` is the exact token
+  `Sidebar.css`'s own `.sidebar-filter` uses for "a bar, not a card in a rail" (the owner's
+  own direction there, 2026-09-19) — reused here rather than invented, so the two rails at
+  either edge of the screen share one material, not two that happen to look similar.
+  Padding went from `.drawer`'s old flat `0.9em` on every side to `1.1em 0.9em` on the head
+  alone, and `.drawer`'s own padding was removed so the head's gray band can run edge-to-edge
+  (`.drawer-body` restates the `0.9em` inset for everything under it instead). Measured with
+  Playwright at 1920: the left nav's own head (brand row + filter band together) is 103px
+  tall; the drawer's new head is 88px — not a pixel-exact match (the two are structurally
+  different, one row of tabs vs. two stacked rows), but close enough to read as the same
+  WEIGHT of chrome, which is what "a pair of bookends" needs. At 400 the drawer's head is
+  56px, wrapping the tab strip onto two lines inside the same gray band.
+- **The clear edge between page and drawer was already there and is unchanged**:
+  `border-inline-start: 1px solid var(--line)` on `.drawer` itself is the same line
+  `core/Sidebar`'s own `border-right: 1px solid var(--line)` draws on its edge — this task
+  only had to make sure restructuring the padding didn't remove it, which it doesn't (it's on
+  `.drawer`, not on the head or body). What changed is that the drawer's own gray band no
+  longer sits at the SAME ROW as the page's — the two bands are now different heights,
+  which is what stops them reading as one continuous toolbar across the line, not the line
+  itself (it was already there, and already worked, before this task).
+

+`x:1877–1912, y:8–43`; the last real page tab ("Overview" on AI 2) ends at `x:782` — a clear
+1095px gap, nowhere near the ☰. At 400 the ☰ is not rendered at all (`display: none`):

+}` (a decision already on record above, "It docks beside the dev rail…"/mobile-nav section),

verdict: fix
1. [fix] On a global session that started on a card, a refinement can be filed under the wrong card (ask 3).

   `card_at()` (Sessions.js) always returns the card the session *started* on, even after the owner moves to another card: `chat.js` `ensure()` passes `target.card` into `Session.start()`, and `card_at()` returns that stored `s.card` unconditionally.

   Fix: store the starting card as the first `nav` card instead, or keep a separate "homed on a card" flag.
2. [fix] When the owner deselects a card in the sheet, the change is never reported. `rail.js:1119` and `rail.js:1123` pass `this.card_ref?.id`, which is `undefined` when no card is selected. `chat.js` `nav(path, card)` treats `undefined` as "keep the old card", so the deselect is lost. Pass `null` for "no card" (`?.id ?? null`), and let `nav()` tell `undefined` apart from `null`.
3. [fix] A doc comment is now out of date and will mislead the next reader. The `chat.js` class doc (diff lines 669–673) says "`rail.js` is outside this merge's fence and still calls `nav(path)` with no card", but this same diff updates `rail.js` to pass the card. Delete that warning.
4. [note] This diff only covers ask 3 (nav card, pause, refinement card), plus `recent_project` and selection.
   Not in this diff: ask 4 (one content model), ask 6 (the surfaces page), the mobile collapse in ask 2.
   `review/report.md` findings 4–6 still stand unless another merge closed them. The card should say which merge covers which ask.
5. [note] There's a simpler way to catch "pause end".
   `Session.js` `report_pause()` polls `mic_floor.owner` every 400 ms, on every page that loads `chat.js`, for the tab's life.
   `floor.js` already has `mic_on()` — one `on_mic` listener there, next to `on_quiet`, would replace the poll.
   Also: the first mic-on posts an `end` with no `start` before it.
6. [note] `Sessions.js` `nav()` tells the fast assistant "the owner moved to X" even when only the card changed and the page stayed the same (`report_nav` now fires on a card-only change). Wording like "now on X, card Y" would be more accurate.
7. [note] `select()` and `say({selection})` store whatever object the browser sends, including `selection.text`, with no size limit (Sessions.js `select`). A large selected block lands in every `select` line, and in the prefix of every sentence's line. Cap or trim `text`.

+like it belongs to something else" problem `design-2.md` is about. So paper mode gets its own
+`grid-template-areas`, not a padding trick on the existing one — `head`/`foot` are only ever above/
+below `main`, and the four corners are cells nobody ever puts a box in (the same "no content, no
+box" rule the plain grid already uses for a region you leave out), painted by the grid's own
+background rather than four extra divs.
+
+That background is `--well: light-dark(rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06), rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35))` — not `--tint`
+(0.035, measurably lighter) or `--wash` (0.08, a generic fill used for code blocks and table
+heads), but the *exact* value `ai2.css` and `ext/Doc/Doc.css` already use for their own gray
+header bands. The brief asked to "pick the one that reads as the AI 2 header band's gray" — the
+closest answer wasn't picking between framework.css's two general-purpose tokens, it was reusing
+the specific value two other modules already settled on for this same look. Neither of those files
+exports `--well` as a shared token (it's declared locally in each), so this is a third, separate
+declaration of the same number rather than a new dependency between unrelated modules — if a
+fourth "well" shows up, hoisting all three into one framework.css token is the fix, not something
+this task's fence reaches.
+
+**Paper mode's regions lose their own border** (`.core-shell-head`/`-foot`/`-left`/`-right`
+border: 0, under `.core-shell-paper`). The plain grid's borders are dividing lines for regions
+sitting flush against `main` with nothing between them; paper mode already separates every region
+from the paper with `gap: var(--gap-25)`, so a line AND a gap together would read as two edges
+doing the same job. Only `main` keeps a border — it's the paper's own edge, not a divider.
+
+**Stacking below 34em needed an explicit override, not just "it already works."** The plain grid's
+`@media (width < 34em)` rule (`.core-shell-grid { grid-template-areas: "head" "left" "main"
+"right" "foot"; … }`) matches a paper shell too — it's the same element, one extra class — but
+`.core-shell-grid.core-shell-paper`'s own un-media-gated rule has higher specificity (two classes
+vs. one) and would otherwise keep trying to lay out three columns in a one-column space. The fix
+is one more rule, inside that same media block, restating the identical stacked areas under the
+two-class selector so it wins the specificity tie by coming later in the file — not a new stacked
+shape, the SAME one the plain grid already had.
+
+## The `left`/`right` clamp used to floor at 12rem inside a `container-type` ancestor — fixed by moving the clamp off the ITEM and onto the grid's own COLUMN
+
+First found in the paper demo (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper-demo/requirements.md`):
+`left`/`right` rendered as bare words with no visible rail. `.core-shell-left`/`-right`'s own
+`width: clamp(12rem, var(--core-shell-left-w, 18rem), 50%)` should render at 18rem (288px) by
+default — nothing writes `--core-shell-left-w` until a drag happens — but measured inside
+`ext/demo`'s own `.demo-stage` (a `container-type: inline-size` box, `ext/demo/stage.css`), it
+rendered at exactly 192px, the clamp's own 12rem FLOOR, instead. This reproduced even with a
+literal `width: clamp(12rem, 18rem, 50%)` and no `var()` at all. The same root cause, the other
+direction, had already hit `dev/DevShell`: its own `right` rail holds long paragraphs of real
+text, whose max-content width is "the whole paragraph on one line" (over 1000px), so instead of
+flooring, that side's `auto` TRACK ballooned past the page's own middle and the rail never
+reached the window's edge (`DevShell.css`, before this fix).
+
+**The cause:** CSS Grid sizes an `auto` COLUMN from each item's own preferred (intrinsic) width
+before the grid's final width is known. Resolving that preferred width means resolving the
+item's own `width: clamp(…, 50%)` — and inside a size-containment context (`container-type:
+inline-size` on an ancestor, which every `ext/demo` stage is), that intrinsic-sizing pass
+resolves a percentage against an indefinite size as `0`. `clamp(12rem, 18rem, 0px)` floors to
+12rem; a huge max-content paragraph instead drags the `auto` track the other way. Both symptoms
+are the same bug: an `auto` TRACK asking an ITEM what size it wants, when that item's own size
+depends on a percentage of the very track being measured.
+
+**The fix (this task, in `Shell.css` itself, not a workaround in `page.js` or `DevShell.css`):**
+move the `clamp()` off the item's `width` and onto the COLUMN, as an explicit track size instead
+of `auto` — an explicit track resolves its own percentage against the grid's (already known)
+content box, no item-intrinsic-sizing pass involved, so the floor/balloon bug has nothing left to
+trigger on. `.core-shell-grid` now carries two custom properties, `--core-shell-col-left` /
+`-right`, defaulting to the keyword `auto` (so a MISSING rail still collapses its column to zero
+width — the same "no content, no box" trick this file already uses everywhere else); a media
+query (`width >= 34em`, matching the existing 34em stack breakpoint) sets each one to
+`clamp(12rem, var(--core-shell-left-w, 18rem), 50%)` only when that rail actually exists
+(`.core-shell-grid:has(> .core-shell-left)` / `:has(> .core-shell-right)`). `.core-shell-left`/
+`-right` themselves are now just `width: auto` — they fill whichever column the grid already
+decided on, rather than sizing themselves a second time. Below 34em the existing stacked-layout
+rule still sets `grid-template-columns: 1fr` directly, which wins the cascade over these two
+variables regardless (same selector, later in the file), so phone layout is unaffected.
+
+Both `page.js`'s paper demo and `dev/DevShell/DevShell.css` had local workarounds for this same
+bug (an inline `width` on `$left`/`$right`, and a duplicate `grid-template-columns` +
+`width: auto` override, respectively) — both are removed now that the real fix lives in
+`Shell.css`. The paper demo still asks for two specific widths the brief named (the chat box at
+14rem, the nested paper's own rail at the 12rem floor, so it reads narrower than the outer
+18rem default) — it does that the ordinary way, by writing `--core-shell-right-w` /
+`--core-shell-left-w` on the shell itself (`shell.style("--core-shell-right-w", "14rem")`), the
+same custom property a drag or `Shell.size()` already writes; this is the intended mechanism,
+not a bypass.
+
+**What a fresh mastermind should check:** load `/framework/core/Shell/` and confirm the paper
+demo's outer `left` rail is a real ~288px (18rem) wide, not a bare word wrapped tight; load
+`dev/DevShell` (Ctrl + \\) at a wide window and confirm the dark right rail's own right edge sits
+flush against the window's right edge, with no blank strip between it and the glass.

+## The ☰ and the drawer's own head read as SITE level, not AI 2's (2026-09-30)
+
+The problem (`ai/2026-09-30/dev-shell/shell-paper/requirements.md`, screenshot
+`1920-drawer.png`): AI 2's own gray header band (its title and tabs) ran to the drawer's
+edge, the floating ☰ still sat inside that same band while the drawer was open, and the
+drawer's own tab row sat at the same height as the page's tab row — so the whole thing
+read as one wide toolbar belonging to AI 2, not as a second piece of site chrome. Three
+changes, `drawer.css` only (no DOM changes — `drawer.js`/`tabs.js` are outside this task's
+fence):
+
+- **The floating ☰ disappears while the drawer is open.** One rule: `body:has(.drawer.on)
+  .drawer-menu { display: none; }`. Two buttons that both close the same rail — the ✕ inside
+  it and a ☰ floating over the page — was itself part of the "this belongs to the page" read.
+  `body`, not `.app`: measured with Playwright that opening the drawer by its routed
+  `?drawer=` url on a cold load hits `drawer.js`'s own documented fallback ("Inside `.app`,
+  not on `<body>`" — that comment names `.app` as the intended mount and `<body>` as what
+  happens when `.app` doesn't exist yet the first time `build()` runs), landing `.drawer.on`
+  as a direct child of `<body>`, not inside `.app` at all. A selector scoped to `.app` would
+  have silently missed exactly that case and left the ☰ showing on a cold `?drawer=` load —
+  `body` is the one ancestor both the normal case and the fallback always share.
+- **The drawer's own head now reads like `core/Sidebar`'s own head** — the "Framework"
+  brand row over its gray filter band — instead of a thin tab strip flush with whatever the
+  page's own header band is doing right next to it. `--darken-2` is the exact token
+  `Sidebar.css`'s own `.sidebar-filter` uses for "a bar, not a card in a rail" (the owner's
+  own direction there, 2026-09-19) — reused here rather than invented, so the two rails at
+  either edge of the screen share one material, not two that happen to look similar.
+  Padding went from `.drawer`'s old flat `0.9em` on every side to `1.1em 0.9em` on the head
+  alone, and `.drawer`'s own padding was removed so the head's gray band can run edge-to-edge
+  (`.drawer-body` restates the `0.9em` inset for everything under it instead). Measured with
+  Playwright at 1920: the left nav's own head (brand row + filter band together) is 103px
+  tall; the drawer's new head is 88px — not a pixel-exact match (the two are structurally
+  different, one row of tabs vs. two stacked rows), but close enough to read as the same
+  WEIGHT of chrome, which is what "a pair of bookends" needs. At 400 the drawer's head is
+  56px, wrapping the tab strip onto two lines inside the same gray band.
+- **The clear edge between page and drawer was already there and is unchanged**:
+  `border-inline-start: 1px solid var(--line)` on `.drawer` itself is the same line
+  `core/Sidebar`'s own `border-right: 1px solid var(--line)` draws on its edge — this task
+  only had to make sure restructuring the padding didn't remove it, which it doesn't (it's on
+  `.drawer`, not on the head or body). What changed is that the drawer's own gray band no
+  longer sits at the SAME ROW as the page's — the two bands are now different heights,
+  which is what stops them reading as one continuous toolbar across the line, not the line
+  itself (it was already there, and already worked, before this task).
+
+**Closed-state overlap, measured, not assumed (requirement 4).** At 1920 the ☰ sits at
+`x:1877–1912, y:8–43`; the last real page tab ("Overview" on AI 2) ends at `x:782` — a clear
+1095px gap, nowhere near the ☰. At 400 the ☰ is not rendered at all (`display: none`):
+`drawer.css`'s own pre-existing mobile rule, `.app:has(.sidebar) .drawer-menu { display: none;
+}` (a decision already on record above, "It docks beside the dev rail…"/mobile-nav section),
+already hides it below 52em whenever the page has an ancestor `core/Sidebar` — which every

# Decisions: documenting the logic behind the work: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). Re-read them before each step.

**Owner:** mastermind-servex (the system architect). **Queued** behind the probe-task work, for weekly pace. Start it when the week's usage is back under its elapsed share.

## The problem
Agents reason a lot ("if we do this, then that works…"), and almost none of it is documented in a form the owner can see. We pay for that work, so we want to see into it and check that the reasoning is sound.

## The system: one documented path per task
1. **Clean transcription,** then a **refined prompt,** then a **statement outline,** then a **brief.** (These already exist in parts: Refine, the briefs.)
2. **Investigation (for a new topic).** Name the FACTS: high-confidence, verifiable things with a source (for example, "the docs are at this URL", or "live video needs a server and client streaming code"). For a known topic, the readme chain gives the facts.
3. **Shape first:** a quick high-level picture of what will be made, its parts and how they talk to each other. For code, that's the classes, files, imports and API, before anything is built.
4. **Decisions,** each one a named card:
   - what is being decided, and what it influences;
   - the options as a RANKED list, with pros, cons and caveats;
   - a **decision table** (factors × questions, with the answers in the cells).
5. **Weights.** Each option gets a `weight` (default 1, a multiplier). It can be a composite of sub-weights (importance, confidence, probability, relevance), each starting at 1 and multiplied together. Models can agree on sub-weights even where they differ on the total. Several models weigh in; record the mean and the spread (high variance means review it).
6. **Decide without blocking** (CLAUDE.md law 5). Take the best option, RECORD the alternatives, and keep going.
7. **Revisit.** When later work struggles, look back at the recorded decisions. An alternative that would solve the trouble is a reason to switch.

## Guard against analysis paralysis
Cap the depth. Explore caveats one level deep, not every permutation. Past that cap, trust the ranked gut call plus the weighted feedback. A decision with no clear winner (equal weights, high spread) is decided by the simplest option, not by researching more.

## Build on what exists, don't duplicate (CLAUDE.md law 6)
- the `decide` skill and `Server/decide.mjs` (which writes decisions step by step);
- `ux/Content/Decision` (the Decision card UI);
- `core/Page/weight` and `rank()` (proposal-flow);
- the multi-model rating from openrouter-harness phase 2, item 5.

## Deliverables
- The documented path above, as content cards the owner can read, simply named, with structure and drill-down.
- Decision tables as a content widget.
- The skill text: agents produce the shape, the decisions, the ranked options and the tables in their normal work, cheaply.
- One real task shown end to end as the example.

1. **Clean transcription,** then a **refined prompt,** then a **statement outline,** then a **brief.** (These already exist in parts: Refine, the briefs.)
2. **Investigation (for a new topic).** Name the FACTS: high-confidence, verifiable things with a source (for example, "the docs are at this URL", or "live video needs a server and client streaming code"). For a known topic, the readme chain gives the facts.
3. **Shape first:** a quick high-level picture of what will be made, its parts and how they talk to each other. For code, that's the classes, files, imports and API, before anything is built.
4. **Decisions,** each one a named card:
   - what is being decided, and what it influences;
   - the options as a RANKED list, with pros, cons and caveats;
   - a **decision table** (factors × questions, with the answers in the cells).
5. **Weights.** Each option gets a `weight` (default 1, a multiplier). It can be a composite of sub-weights (importance, confidence, probability, relevance), each starting at 1 and multiplied together. Models can agree on sub-weights even where they differ on the total. Several models weigh in; record the mean and the spread (high variance means review it).
6. **Decide without blocking** (CLAUDE.md law 5). Take the best option, RECORD the alternatives, and keep going.
7. **Revisit.** When later work struggles, look back at the recorded decisions. An alternative that would solve the trouble is a reason to switch.

## Guard against analysis paralysis
Cap the depth. Explore caveats one level deep, not every permutation. Past that cap, trust the ranked gut call plus the weighted feedback. A decision with no clear winner (equal weights, high spread) is decided by the simplest option, not by researching more.

## Build on what exists, don't duplicate (CLAUDE.md law 6)
- the `decide` skill and `Server/decide.mjs` (which writes decisions step by step);
- `ux/Content/Decision` (the Decision card UI);
- `core/Page/weight` and `rank()` (proposal-flow);
- the multi-model rating from openrouter-harness phase 2, item 5.

## Deliverables
- The documented path above, as content cards the owner can read, simply named, with structure and drill-down.
- Decision tables as a content widget.
- The skill text: agents produce the shape, the decisions, the ranked options and the tables in their normal work, cheaply.
- One real task shown end to end as the example.

## Asks
1. **`core/Page/ext/`: an extension (plugin) system for Page,** modelled on the Server's plugin system (`Server/plugins/`): event-driven hooks, and extensions configured by data (in page.jsonl), not hard-coded. It is the ext pattern for any module or directory. Keep it minimal.
2. **`core/Page/ext/Inbox`:** the first extension. Any page can have an inbox.
   - Messaging a page = appending one line to its page.jsonl: `{inbox: {type: "message"|"question", author, text, at}}`.

Keep every useful feature of today's Inbox: the sidebar on click, and read/unread, archive, auto-resolve and search from task ai2-inbox-read. The Inbox IS the default tab, so its top-priority items are what the page opens on.
4. **Needs you is a filter in the Inbox list,** not its own tab with its own UI.
5. **Inbox and Log share one UI:** the rail with previews, and each preview opens its card. Today the three tabs use three different templates. Lean into the Inbox's version.

6. **The rail is a base class, overridden per page** with object-oriented overrides. The usage meters live only on the AI page's rail subclass, not on every page's inbox.
7. **Each owner prompt becomes an Inbox card showing its refined version.** Servex hears each owner prompt (the `.claude/prompts/` hook, and voice sessions), runs it through the Refine ladder (`ext/Refine`: raw → structured), and posts or updates a card at the top of the Inbox. Post the first one by hand, on the card linked above, as the example.

8. **A card is a whole conversation, and it shows what it's about** (the owner, 2026-09-30). Each Inbox item stands for an entire conversation, which continues in the card's sidebar. The card's body shows at least part of the thing it references, imported live: a page, a module or a screenshot. Build this on the reference system (`#Page`, `/path`, task-mastermind-mentions), so every post makes it obvious what it's talking about.

9. **Chat and card are ONE content model** (the owner, 2026-09-30, the summary of the thread):
   - A card IS a page: a title, a preview and a detail view, backed by its own page.jsonl. It can be a conversation or an AI session, and it has its own inbox, which is its feed of updates.

The session is context-aware instead: each navigation is logged as an invisible event ("now on <page>, card <id>"), as are pause start and pause end, all timestamped. It costs a few more tokens and buys real insight into the reasoning. It's browsable by the owner (who may weigh in before or after; never blocking) and by later models.

- **Shape rule (code):** stay one-to-one with the underlying technology (the DOM, the platform APIs). Never add a layer that only re-wraps an existing API with no added function. Send it to the code system (/framework/code/) through the architect.

## Added 2026-10-01 (00:40): investigation first, and consensus as near-fact
- **Every prompt, question, task or objective breaks down the same way:**
  1. a title (its name);
  2. its core pillars or principles (with sub-parts);
  3. for each pillar: the major decisions, the factors and the caveats.
- **INVESTIGATING is the first phase, before planning:** what do we know to be true? Ask several models to state facts, and keep the statements most of them agree on (e.g. "you can't do A and B at once": mutually exclusive choices).
- **Decision dependency trees:** "if you choose this format or library, these consequences follow; if you choose that one, those". Models can weigh in on a whole design tree before any code is written. It can run to hundreds of sub-trees, so it must be an iceberg UI: a title, a summary and the weight on top, and you click in only if you care.
- **Consensus as near-fact:**
  - a statement with overwhelming agreement (above 90%) is near-fact;
  - one with overwhelming disagreement (below 10%) is a near-certain "don't".

  Write these as strong rules ("probably always" or "probably never"), but not as absolutes; rare edge cases exist. The thresholds are arbitrary and tunable. Note: this is an AGREEMENT score (0–100% of models), shown beside the weight (the multiplier around 1). Keep the two distinct.
- **Cheap extraction:** give each model a minimal, self-contained input and ask how it would solve or fix X. Get the most knowledge per token.
