# Where the tokens went, and the ten cheapest wins

Looked at 7 days of `spend.json` + `task.jsonl` across 375 tasks (2026-09-25 to today). Total logged spend: **$1,521**.

## 1. Where it went (top sinks)

| Rank | Sink | $ | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Opus running tasks alone, no minions** | $322 (73 tasks) | Opus is the top-level model AND does every step itself — no delegation to Sonnet/Haiku. `2026-09-29/audio` ($100), `process-monitor` ($37), `selection` ($28) are the worst. This is the single biggest pattern: Opus doing Sonnet-sized (or smaller) work end to end. |
| 2 | **Opus overall** | $1,058 of $1,521 (70%) | Opus is set as the default model for most "build a thing" tasks, even plain CRUD/UI work Sonnet handles fine. Sonnet-labeled tasks only total $317. |
| 3 | **servex-mastermind on Fable, long turns** | $116 (one 2026-09-30 run, 271 log lines) | The architect runs on Fable continuously; a single day's session racked up more than most whole tasks. Three separate `servex-mastermind` runs across the week (09-25, 09-28, 09-29) add another $58 on top. |
| 4 | **Fan-outs with many sub-agents on Opus** | `page-system` ($48, 33 agents), `organization` ($37, 17 agents), `file-system` ($44, 8 agents), `audio-consolidate` ($31, 9 agents), `figma-sept-frame` ($46, 7 agents) | Each spawns a double-digit number of agents, several on Opus, for work that reads like Sonnet-tier (settings tabs, file data model, cards). |
| 5 | **Dictation → brief pipeline** | group `dictate`+`dictation` = $209 | `prompt-refine` ($48, Opus) and `audio` ($100, Opus) turn one spoken ask into a full build; both ran solo-Opus. |
| 6 | **Drawer / mobile-nav on Sonnet but 194 log lines, 0 agents** | $55 | One session did the whole thing itself in many small turns instead of splitting into a few agent calls — more read/think/write round-trips than needed for the result. |
| 7 | **openrouter-harness** | $68 (Opus, 138 lines, 1 agent) | A single investigation task priced like a mid-size build. |
| 8 | **dev-shell** | $38 (Opus, solo) | Shell/header/footer layout — a UI composition task, Opus-priced. |
| 9 | **Re-reading big files across many small spend points** | visible as 10-40 sub-$1 charges per task in several `spend.json` files (e.g. `page-system`, `organization`) | Pattern matches "re-reading the same big files": many small charges a few seconds apart, consistent with repeated full-file reads rather than cached diffs. |
| 10 | **No model floor below Opus for "mastermind"-named tasks** | all 4 `servex-mastermind` runs this week ($58 total just for those) + `ai2-lead` ($11, Opus) | Masterminds default to the most expensive model even for routine sweeps (skill updates, triage), not just judgment calls. |

## 2. Ten cheapest wins (ranked by tokens saved per change)

| # | Change | File/skill to change | Why it's cheap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Default new tasks to Sonnet; require a stated reason to use Opus** | the `minion`/`mastermind` skill's model guidance, or wherever `spawn_agent` picks a default | Single biggest lever — 70% of spend is Opus; most of it (73 solo tasks, $322) shows no sign of needing Opus-level judgment. |
| 2 | **Masterminds spawn minions instead of building solo** | `mastermind`/`servex-mastermind` skill | The 73 "Opus, zero sub-agents" tasks are exactly the anti-pattern the `mastermind-relays-not-executes` memory note already named — enforce it as a skill rule with a cost consequence named. |
| 3 | **Cap `servex-mastermind`'s continuous Fable runs** (checkpoint + recycle before ~150k context, per brief's own suggestion) | `servex-mastermind` skill / its spawn loop | One day's run was $116; a context cap with recycle would turn long Fable sessions into several cheaper fresh ones. |
| 4 | **Route "mastermind" sweeps (skill updates, triage, routine checks) to Sonnet, reserve Fable/Opus for judgment calls only** | `servex-mastermind` skill | $58 across 4 runs this week on pure sweep work. |
| 5 | **Spawn fan-outs with `task: {dir, brief}` + a one-line prompt instead of pasting the brief into the prompt** | `spawn_agent` call sites (page-system, organization, file-system show 7-33 agents each) | Brief already recommends this; cuts duplicated brief text from every sub-agent's first turn across the highest-agent-count tasks. |
| 6 | **Put a context cap on every agent (not just masterminds)** — stop and recycle from a checkpoint file before ~150k tokens | Servex spawn/heartbeat logic | `page-system` (317 log lines) and `one-dictation` (229 lines) both look like one session running very long instead of relaying. |
| 7 | **Prompt caching on repeated readme-chain reads** | wherever agents call `load_module`/read readmes at session start | Every fresh mastermind/minion re-reads the same root-to-leaf readme chain; caching those (same content, high reuse) is pure savings with no behavior change. |
| 8 | **Smaller readme chains for narrow tasks** | module readmes under `public/framework/` | A minion fixing one page.js doesn't need the full root chain; let `load_module` take a narrower starting point when the brief names one directory. |
| 9 | **Batch heartbeats / sweep checks instead of one Servex call per tick** | Servex heartbeat config | Cheap, mechanical; reduces fixed per-tick overhead system-wide, compounds over a week. |
| 10 | **One review round for small changes, not the full review+smoke-test+merge sequence every time** | `merge.mjs` / `review.mjs` gate | Doesn't show clearly in this week's data (no dedicated review-round spend.json), but the brief names it and the build order already does a smoke-test *and* a fresh-eyes review for every merge; a size threshold (quick-fix path already exists) extends it further. |

## 3. A weekly pace rule Servex can enforce

**Daily token budget per role, spawns queued when a day is over pace**, building on the existing working cap of 5 and the dormant system:
- Give each role a daily $ budget = weekly target ÷ 7, split roughly by role (e.g. masterminds get a smaller slice than builders, since law 5 already says builders shouldn't be blocked).

## 1. Where it went (top sinks)

| Rank | Sink | $ | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Opus running tasks alone, no minions** | $322 (73 tasks) | Opus is the top-level model AND does every step itself — no delegation to Sonnet/Haiku. `2026-09-29/audio` ($100), `process-monitor` ($37), `selection` ($28) are the worst. | 2 | **Opus overall** | $1,058 of $1,521 (70%) | Opus is set as the default model for most "build a thing" tasks, even plain CRUD/UI work Sonnet handles fine. Sonnet-labeled tasks only total $317. |
| 3 | **servex-mastermind on Fable, long turns** | $116 (one 2026-09-30 run, 271 log lines) | The architect runs on Fable continuously; a single day's session racked up more than most whole tasks. Three separate `servex-mastermind` runs across the week (09-25, 09-28, 09-29) add another $58 on top. |
| 4 | **Fan-outs with many sub-agents on Opus** | `page-system` ($48, 33 agents), `organization` ($37, 17 agents), `file-system` ($44, 8 agents), `audio-consolidate` ($31, 9 agents), `figma-sept-frame` ($46, 7 agents) | Each spawns a double-digit number of agents, several on Opus, for work that reads like Sonnet-tier (settings tabs, file data model, cards). |

# Remote access: the site from outside the house: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md).

## Decision: Tailscale, not a public tunnel
**Chosen: Tailscale** (a free, private network between the owner's own devices).
- The PC and the phone join one private network. The site is reachable from anywhere, but ONLY from the owner's devices, with nothing exposed to the internet.
- `tailscale serve` gives the PC a real HTTPS name (`https://<pc>.<tailnet>.ts.net`). That's a secure context, so the **mic works on the phone with no Chrome flag**.

**Alternative: a Cloudflare Tunnel** (`cloudflared`; a quick tunnel gives a public `trycloudflare.com` URL with no account). Rejected for now: it puts the dev server and Servex on the PUBLIC internet. Servex can spawn agents and run commands, and the dev server once had a LAN-reachable exec hole (closed). A public URL would need Cloudflare Access (a Zero Trust login, which needs the lew42.com zone on Cloudflare) in front of it before it's safe. Revisit that if the owner wants to share a link with someone who isn't on their devices.

## Owner steps (one time, about 10 minutes): the only part that needs the owner
1. Install Tailscale on the PC: `winget install Tailscale.Tailscale`, then sign in (Google or GitHub login).
2. Install the Tailscale app on the phone and sign in with the SAME account.
3. Tell the vscode-mastermind "Tailscale is on". The rest is ours.

## Agent steps (after the owner's steps)
1. `tailscale serve --bg http://localhost:8137` (the site) and a second path or port for Servex if the phone needs it. Record the HTTPS URL.
2. **Let the tailnet in** where LAN-only gates exist today, but ONLY the tailnet range `100.64.0.0/10` and `*.ts.net` hosts, never the public internet:
   - `Server/plugins/MCP.js` (`PRIVATE`, `lan()`, `safe_host()`);
   - `Server/plugins/Ask.js`;
   - `public/framework/ext/drawer/tabs.js` (`LOCAL_HOST` / `DEV`).
3. Test from the phone on cellular (Wi-Fi off): the site loads, the ✦ rail works, and the mic works.
4. Add one line to the root readme ("Remote: <URL>"), and save the URL to memory.

# Page and Item, one system: the proposal

The owner's ask (2026-10-01): "show me a simple example, top down, of how the system should work… could Page extend Item… harmonize page.set and item.set". Proposed by vscode-mastermind. **Page extends Item is core surgery, so CLAUDE.md asks first: this needs the owner's go-ahead before the build.**

## The shape

```
Item                 a persistent object: id, data, events, an ordered list of child items
 └─ Page             an Item that has a URL, routes and renders
     └─ Card…        a smaller Page (an Item that grew), one class line away
item.items: Content  extends List: the ordered children plus the edit verbs. No persistence of its own.
```

- **Every Page IS an Item.** Its content is `page.items`, and a sub-page is simply an item that has grown into a page.
- **Persistence lives in Item, once:** each change is one line appended to the NEAREST page.jsonl.
- **List stays a plain array wrapper.** `Content extends List` only adds the edit verbs (add, set, move, remove) and events.

## One `set`, harmonised

Today the two `set`s differ:
- **`page.set(obj)`:** replays a log line. A method key calls the method, a settable value merges, and anything else is data.
- **`item.set(key, value)`:** stores data and emits `change`.

**One rule:** `set(obj)` takes a DELTA object, the same shape as a log line.
1. A key that names a method calls the method (e.g. `place`, `file`, `add`).
2. A value with its own `set()` receives the nested delta (recursion).
3. Anything else is data. It goes in `data`, and emits `change` with the key, the new value and the old value.
4. **Live or replay:** when the object is being REBUILT from its log, nothing is written back. A live change appends the delta as one line. A flag on the replay pass, not a second method.

`item.set("title", "Hi")` remains as sugar for `item.set({ title: "Hi" })`.

## Top down: one page, from file to screen and back

**On disk:** `notes/page.jsonl`, the page and everything on it, in one file:

```json
{"class": "/framework/core/Page/Page.js", "title": "Notes"}
{"add": {"id": "k1", "type": "p", "text": "First thought."}}
{"add": {"id": "k2", "type": "Card", "title": "An idea", "after": "k1"}}
{"at": "k2", "add": {"id": "k3", "type": "p", "text": "Detail inside the card."}}
{"at": "k1", "set": {"text": "First thought, edited."}}
{"move": {"id": "k2", "after": null}}
```

**Loading (hydrate = replay):**
1. Line 1's `class` is looked up in the shared type registry (`core/types`), and the Page is built.
2. Each later line is `page.set(line)`, in file order: `add` creates an Item of the registered `type` in `page.items`, `at` finds the item by id and passes the rest to it, `set` changes data, and `move` reorders.
3. The view draws `page.items`. Each root item is a `Sortable`.

**Editing (live):**
- The owner drags `k2` to the top. Sortable calls `item.move(...)`, Content emits `move`, and Item appends one line, `{"move": {"id": "k2", "after": null}}`.
- The owner types in `k1`. Item emits `change` and appends `{"at": "k1", "set": {"text": "…"}}`.
- Nothing is ever rewritten. The file is the history.

**Promotion:** when `k2` grows (replies, length, a task), its lines move into `notes/k2/page.jsonl` (class Card), and the parent keeps `{"file": "k2/page.jsonl"}`. It's the same object either way; only where its lines live changes.

## Alternative (recorded)
Keep Page and Item separate and share only the log writer and the type registry. That's less surgery, but you keep two `set`s, two tree models (`children` Map vs `items` List), and "is this a page or an item?" at every seam, which is the duplication CLAUDE.md law 6 forbids.

edits.old: ## The shape
edits.new:
## Naming, revised (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:40)
Free up the name `List` for the thing people SEE. **The plain data list becomes `Collection`** (today's `core/List`: only 2 callers, so the rename is cheap; keep a `List` re-export for one release). **`List` becomes the UX list** (`ux/List`): a View that draws a Collection or Content, sortable by DEFAULT through `ext/Draggable/Sortable`. "Just use a List" then gives you drag-to-sort for free, with sorting switched off by an option.

| Class | Is a | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `Collection` | — | the ordered data array: append, insert, remove, events. No UI, no saving. |
| `Content` | Collection | edit verbs by id (add, set, move, remove, `after`) |
| `Item` | — | persistent object: id, data, get/set, events, log lines; `items` is a lazy Content |
| `Page` | Item | URL, routes, rendering |
| `Card` | Page | a smaller page |
| `View` | — | the DOM |
| `List` | View | the UX list: draws a Collection or Content, sortable by default |
| `Sortable` | behaviour | drag and drop; `List` uses it |
| `Saver` | — | where the lines go |
| `types` | module | one class registry |

## The shape

edits.old: ## Naming, revised (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:40)
edits.new:
## FINAL naming (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:50): keep `List`. No `Collection`.
- **`List` is THE list**, a plain array wrapper, short and familiar. Upgrade it once and every list on the site gets the upgrade.
- **`class Content extends List`**, and Content HAS a managed view (`content.view`, an upgraded View that Content drives: it draws the items and makes them sortable).
- `Item` keeps `items` as a lazy Content. `Page extends Item`.

## Saving content (checked 2026-10-01)
- **Dev, today:** the dev socket already has an **append RPC** (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js`, since 2026-08-31). One line goes in, `fs.appendFile` writes it, and the path must resolve under `public/` and end in `.jsonl`. No whole-file write: `rpc:write` (FileSaver) stays only for non-log files. Every tab tailing the file gets the line live. Concurrent writers interleave safely.
- **To add:** validate each line in `Append.js` with the same schema check `append.mjs` and `append_log` use (wave A, `.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs`), so a browser can't write a malformed line.
- **Production (static site, no dev server):** the same `append(line)` goes to a cloud sink. `public/imagine/stream/doc/durable-objects.md` already sketches a Cloudflare Durable Object, which does exactly this. That's the `CloudSaver` later.

(The "Naming, revised" section below is superseded: no Collection, and List is not renamed.)

## Naming, revised (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:40)

edits.old: - **`class Content extends List`**, and Content HAS a managed view
edits.new:
- **A List is NOT a View, and a View is NOT a List** (the owner, 04:00): merging their method names would confuse everyone. **A List HAS a view.** There's ONE `List` class, with its view as a static part, created lazily: `class List { static View = ListView }`, and `list.view` exists only when something draws it. `ListView` makes the items sortable by default. No second class named List and no `ListUX`: a list that needs a different look swaps its part (`static View = MyView`), so subclasses don't redo any helpers.
- Content is built mostly from JSON lines by node code, not hand-written with helpers, so the helper-function question matters less here.
- **`class Content extends List`**, and Content HAS a managed view

# Remote access: the site from outside the house: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md).

## Decision (REVISED 2026-10-01 15:20, on the owner's preference): a Cloudflare Tunnel with Cloudflare Access
The owner would rather not sign up for a new service, and wants to learn Cloudflare. **lew42.com's DNS is already on Cloudflare** (nameservers jim/aitana.ns.cloudflare.com), so this needs no new account and costs nothing:
- **Cloudflare Tunnel** (`cloudflared`, free): an outbound-only connector on the PC. There's no port forwarding and no open ports. It maps, for example, `dev.lew42.com` → `http://localhost:8137`.
- **Cloudflare Access** (Zero Trust, free for up to 50 users) in FRONT of it: a login page (a one-time code to the owner's email, or Google). Only the owner gets through. **This is required.** Without it, the dev server and Servex (which can run commands) would be on the public internet.
- It's a real HTTPS name, so the mic works on the phone with no Chrome flag.
- It only runs while the PC is on and `cloudflared` is running. It's a Windows service and can be stopped any time, with no monthly bill to forget.

**Alternative (rejected):** Tailscale. It's free and very simple, but it's a new service and an app on every device. The owner prefers Cloudflare.

## Owner steps (about 10 minutes, once): only the logins
1. Run `winget install Cloudflare.cloudflared`, then `cloudflared tunnel login`. A browser opens: pick lew42.com.
2. In the Cloudflare dashboard → Zero Trust, accept the free plan if asked (no card needed for the free tier).
3. Then tell vscode-mastermind, or the watcher will notice `cloudflared`.

## Agent steps (after the owner's steps)
1. `cloudflared tunnel create monorepo`, then a config mapping `dev.lew42.com` → `http://localhost:8137` (plus a path or host for Servex if the phone needs it). DNS: `cloudflared tunnel route dns monorepo dev.lew42.com`.
2. **Before the tunnel serves anything:** a Cloudflare Access application on `dev.lew42.com`, with the policy "emails = the owner's". Verify that a logged-out browser gets the login page, not the site.
3. Run cloudflared as a service. Let the tunnel's requests through the LAN-only gates (`Server/plugins/MCP.js` `lan()`/`safe_host()`, `Server/plugins/Ask.js`, `ext/drawer/tabs.js` DEV), but ONLY when the `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` header is present and valid (Cloudflare's signed login proof), never just because of the host name.
4. Test from the phone on cellular (Wi-Fi off): the login, the site, the ✦ rail and the mic.
5. Write one line in the root readme ("Remote: https://dev.lew42.com, behind Cloudflare Access") and save it to memory.

# Voice — text to speech

`window.speechSynthesis` is the whole engine — the browser's own built-in text-to-speech, the
output half of the mic pair (`Transcriber` turns speech INTO text; `Voice` turns text BACK into
speech). Nothing to install, nothing to run.

## Use

```js
import Voice from "/framework/audio/Voice/Voice.js";

const voice = new Voice();
voice.speak("Hello there.");   // → voice.state === "speaking", then "idle" when done
voice.rate = 1.3;               // takes effect on the NEXT speak()
voice.pick(voice.voices()[2]);  // choose a voice by its SpeechSynthesisVoice object
```

## Watch out

- The browser's voice list (`voice.voices()`) can come back empty right after the page loads —
  wait for `on_voices_ready()`, don't read it once and give up.
- There's no local engine (the way `Transcriber.Whisper` wraps whisper-server) — checked, nothing
  like that is installed on this machine today. `doc/decisions.md`'s `d-voice-engine` has the
  reasoning and what a local one would need.

## More

- [Overview](/framework/audio/Voice/) — the live demo
- [`../readme.md`](../readme.md) — the audio/ library
- [`../doc/decisions.md`](../doc/decisions.md) — `d-voice-engine`: why browser, not local, for now

Headless Playwright against the real, live site (`http://monorepo.localhost`, uncommitted) —

[`proof-results.json`](proof-results.json) · shots: [`shots/`](shots/).

**36 of 38 checks pass.** The 2 that don't pass are real findings, not test bugs — see check 5.

## The 7 checks

1. **No duplicates — PASS**, on both the [demo](/framework/ux/Dictate/) and the ✦ sheet. One
   typed message draws exactly one bubble, and one assistant reply, delivered through **both**
   channels `chat.js` listens on at once (the fast SSE push and the slower file poll — the
   owner's own bug: "both messages... added twice... four messages total"), also draws exactly
   one. Shots: [`duplicates-demo.png`](shots/duplicates-demo.png),
   [`duplicates-sheet.png`](shots/duplicates-sheet.png).

   thread fills the space with no empty void under the buttons (the bug `rail-fullscreen-
   textarea` fixed). What's left under the composer is a small, deliberate ~0.9em safe-area
   padding (measured 32px at 400px wide) — not the old bug. Shot:
   [`full-screen-sheet-400.png`](shots/full-screen-sheet-400.png).
3. **Auto-scroll — PASS**, fully. 30 bubbles stay pinned to the bottom; scrolling up releases
   the lock and shows a real "jump to bottom" button (`.chatbox-jump`, the ↓ circle); a new
   bubble while scrolled up does **not** move the view; the button jumps back down and
   re-hides itself. Shot: [`autoscroll-1200.png`](shots/autoscroll-1200.png).
4. **Mic sounds — PASS**, on both surfaces. With a real (fake) microphone granted, pressing
   the mic plays exactly one start chime and stopping it plays exactly one stop chime —
   never silent, never doubled (the bug `dictate-stop-sound` fixed).
5. **The dot — PASS as a widget, but not live anywhere yet.** `new Widget({pulse: true})`
   genuinely works: locked (mic off) shows a "tap to talk" card over the feed; unlocked shows
   the small orange dot, bottom-right. Shots: [`pulse-dot-off.png`](shots/pulse-dot-off.png),

   demo and the ✦ sheet both still use the old `level` meter bar, not the dot. This is the
   two FAILs in the numbers above — a true gap, not a test mistake.

   | option | the Dictate page's demo (`page.js`) | the ✦ sheet (`rail.js`) |
   | --- | --- | --- |

   | `level` | `true` | not set → `false` |
   | `source` | `true` | not set → `false` |
   | `debug` | `true` | not set → `false` |
   | `mode` | from the page's own Dictate/Chat switch | not set → `"dictate"` |
   | `pulse` | not set → `false` | not set → `false` |
   | `card` | — | the active card's id, if any |

   So: **the two surfaces still don't match.** The demo shows a level meter, a mic picker and
   the Debug panel; the sheet shows none of those — plainer by design (a phone sheet has no
   room for a Debug panel), but there's no single place that says which of these differences
   are intentional and which are just "nobody passed it here yet." This table is the input
   the next merge (the brief's own words) needs.
7. **Menu merge — PASS.** Exactly one ⚙ button (the old second `⋯` button is gone); it opens
   one full-screen panel holding BOTH halves that used to be two small popovers — the
   engine/status info block and the full settings grid. Shot:
   [`menu-merge-open-400.png`](shots/menu-merge-open-400.png).
   **Threaded replies — PASS**, with one detail worth knowing: a reply opens its own thread
   automatically the moment it lands (not collapsed first) because it's "from the last two
   minutes" — that's the code's own deliberate rule ("so it is seen"), and the toggle still
   collapses it to "▸ 1 reply" on a click. Shot:
   [`threaded-reply-900.png`](shots/threaded-reply-900.png).

1. No duplicates — **pass** (demo + sheet), [shot](shots/duplicates-demo.png)

3. Auto-scroll + jump-to-bottom — **pass**, [shot](shots/autoscroll-1200.png)

6. Surfaces match? — **no**, see the table above

## One JSONL system: `Log` (the owner, 2026-10-01 16:05; replaces the four ad-hoc readers and writers)
```js
class Log {                        // one .jsonl file = one object's history
  url
  lines: [{}]                      // parsed, in file order
  load()                           // fetch + parse (static sites can do this)
  replay(into)                     // into.set(line) for each line: hydration
  append(line)                     // validated, then handed to the Writer
  static Writer                    // dev: socket append · cloud: a Saver · static: none (read-only)
  static Tail                      // live new lines when a server exists; otherwise nothing (one load)
  mode: "single" | "split"         // split: a child object that grew gets its own folder and log
}
```
- **It's a manager, not a stream.** Streaming (Tail) is an optional part, so a log on a static site still loads and replays.

- **Speed:** a long log gets a SNAPSHOT. Every N lines, a `{"snapshot": {...}}` line holds the whole state, and loading reads from the last snapshot on, with older lines rolled into `page.log.jsonl`. MEASURE first where the 1–3 s page delays come from (fetch, parse, replay or render) before optimising.
- **It replaces:** Servex Log (the single writer stays inside Writer), ext/JSONL (the reader), PageLog's replay, and ext/Session's own watch().
- **Page extends Item:** the owner leans yes ("seems reasonable", 16:05).

## FINAL naming (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:50): keep `List`. No `Collection`.

# Page and Item, one system: the proposal

The owner's ask (2026-10-01): "show me a simple example, top down, of how the system should work… could Page extend Item… harmonize page.set and item.set". Proposed by vscode-mastermind. **Page extends Item is core surgery, so CLAUDE.md asks first: this needs the owner's go-ahead before the build.**

## One JSONL system: `Log` (the owner, 2026-10-01 16:05; replaces the four ad-hoc readers and writers)
```js
class Log {                        // one .jsonl file = one object's history
  url
  lines: [{}]                      // parsed, in file order
  load()                           // fetch + parse (static sites can do this)
  replay(into)                     // into.set(line) for each line: hydration
  append(line)                     // validated, then handed to the Writer
  static Writer                    // dev: socket append · cloud: a Saver · static: none (read-only)
  static Tail                      // live new lines when a server exists; otherwise nothing (one load)
  mode: "single" | "split"         // split: a child object that grew gets its own folder and log
}
```
- **It's a manager, not a stream.** Streaming (Tail) is an optional part, so a log on a static site still loads and replays.
- **Deep updates by path, through ids:** `{"at": "k2/k3", "set": {...}}`. Ids are unique within their parent, so there's no global namespace to manage.
- **Speed:** a long log gets a SNAPSHOT. Every N lines, a `{"snapshot": {...}}` line holds the whole state, and loading reads from the last snapshot on, with older lines rolled into `page.log.jsonl`. MEASURE first where the 1–3 s page delays come from (fetch, parse, replay or render) before optimising.
- **It replaces:** Servex Log (the single writer stays inside Writer), ext/JSONL (the reader), PageLog's replay, and ext/Session's own watch().
- **Page extends Item:** the owner leans yes ("seems reasonable", 16:05).

## FINAL naming (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:50): keep `List`. No `Collection`.
- **`List` is THE list**, a plain array wrapper, short and familiar. Upgrade it once and every list on the site gets the upgrade.
- **A List is NOT a View, and a View is NOT a List** (the owner, 04:00): merging their method names would confuse everyone. **A List HAS a view.** There's ONE `List` class, with its view as a static part, created lazily: `class List { static View = ListView }`, and `list.view` exists only when something draws it. `ListView` makes the items sortable by default. No second class named List and no `ListUX`: a list that needs a different look swaps its part (`static View = MyView`), so subclasses don't redo any helpers.
- Content is built mostly from JSON lines by node code, not hand-written with helpers, so the helper-function question matters less here.
- **`class Content extends List`**, and Content HAS a managed view (`content.view`, an upgraded View that Content drives: it draws the items and makes them sortable).
- `Item` keeps `items` as a lazy Content. `Page extends Item`.

## Saving content (checked 2026-10-01)
- **Dev, today:** the dev socket already has an **append RPC** (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js`, since 2026-08-31). One line goes in, `fs.appendFile` writes it, and the path must resolve under `public/` and end in `.jsonl`. No whole-file write: `rpc:write` (FileSaver) stays only for non-log files. Every tab tailing the file gets the line live. Concurrent writers interleave safely.
- **To add:** validate each line in `Append.js` with the same schema check `append.mjs` and `append_log` use (wave A, `.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs`), so a browser can't write a malformed line.
- **Production (static site, no dev server):** the same `append(line)` goes to a cloud sink. `public/imagine/stream/doc/durable-objects.md` already sketches a Cloudflare Durable Object, which does exactly this. That's the `CloudSaver` later.

(The "Naming, revised" section below is superseded: no Collection, and List is not renamed.)

## Naming, revised (the owner, 2026-10-01 03:40)
Free up the name `List` for the thing people SEE. **The plain data list becomes `Collection`** (today's `core/List`: only 2 callers, so the rename is cheap; keep a `List` re-export for one release). **`List` becomes the UX list** (`ux/List`): a View that draws a Collection or Content, sortable by DEFAULT through `ext/Draggable/Sortable`. "Just use a List" then gives you drag-to-sort for free, with sorting switched off by an option.

| Class | Is a | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `Collection` | — | the ordered data array: append, insert, remove, events. No UI, no saving. |
| `Content` | Collection | edit verbs by id (add, set, move, remove, `after`) |
| `Item` | — | persistent object: id, data, get/set, events, log lines; `items` is a lazy Content |
| `Page` | Item | URL, routes, rendering |
| `Card` | Page | a smaller page |
| `View` | — | the DOM |
| `List` | View | the UX list: draws a Collection or Content, sortable by default |
| `Sortable` | behaviour | drag and drop; `List` uses it |
| `Saver` | — | where the lines go |
| `types` | module | one class registry |

## The shape

```
Item                 a persistent object: id, data, events, an ordered list of child items
 └─ Page             an Item that has a URL, routes and renders
     └─ Card…        a smaller Page (an Item that grew), one class line away
item.items: Content  extends List: the ordered children plus the edit verbs. No persistence of its own.
```

- **Every Page IS an Item.** Its content is `page.items`, and a sub-page is simply an item that has grown into a page.
- **Persistence lives in Item, once:** each change is one line appended to the NEAREST page.jsonl.
- **List stays a plain array wrapper.** `Content extends List` only adds the edit verbs (add, set, move, remove) and events.

## One `set`, harmonised

Today the two `set`s differ:
- **`page.set(obj)`:** replays a log line. A method key calls the method, a settable value merges, and anything else is data.
- **`item.set(key, value)`:** stores data and emits `change`.

**One rule:** `set(obj)` takes a DELTA object, the same shape as a log line.
1. A key that names a method calls the method (e.g. `place`, `file`, `add`).
2. A value with its own `set()` receives the nested delta (recursion).
3. Anything else is data. It goes in `data`, and emits `change` with the key, the new value and the old value.
4. **Live or replay:** when the object is being REBUILT from its log, nothing is written back. A live change appends the delta as one line. A flag on the replay pass, not a second method.

`item.set("title", "Hi")` remains as sugar for `item.set({ title: "Hi" })`.

## Top down: one page, from file to screen and back

**On disk:** `notes/page.jsonl`, the page and everything on it, in one file:

```json
{"class": "/framework/core/Page/Page.js", "title": "Notes"}
{"add": {"id": "k1", "type": "p", "text": "First thought."}}
{"add": {"id": "k2", "type": "Card", "title": "An idea", "after": "k1"}}
{"at": "k2", "add": {"id": "k3", "type": "p", "text": "Detail inside the card."}}
{"at": "k1", "set": {"text": "First thought, edited."}}
{"move": {"id": "k2", "after": null}}
```

**Loading (hydrate = replay):**
1. Line 1's `class` is looked up in the shared type registry (`core/types`), and the Page is built.
2. Each later line is `page.set(line)`, in file order: `add` creates an Item of the registered `type` in `page.items`, `at` finds the item by id and passes the rest to it, `set` changes data, and `move` reorders.
3. The view draws `page.items`. Each root item is a `Sortable`.

**Editing (live):**
- The owner drags `k2` to the top. Sortable calls `item.move(...)`, Content emits `move`, and Item appends one line, `{"move": {"id": "k2", "after": null}}`.
- The owner types in `k1`. Item emits `change` and appends `{"at": "k1", "set": {"text": "…"}}`.
- Nothing is ever rewritten. The file is the history.

**Promotion:** when `k2` grows (replies, length, a task), its lines move into `notes/k2/page.jsonl` (class Card), and the parent keeps `{"file": "k2/page.jsonl"}`. It's the same object either way; only where its lines live changes.

   - A card IS a page: a title, a preview and a detail view, backed by its own page.jsonl. It can be a conversation or an AI session, and it has its own inbox, which is its feed of updates.

edits.new:
## REVISED (the owner, 2026-10-01 16:15): not `Log`, and composition, not inheritance
- **Keep `Log` free** for the real logging API (console-like messages). A JSONL store isn't "a log of everything".
- **What the class really does:** it holds a host's DELTAS. It loads them, applies each to the host through `host.set(line)` (creating registered types as it goes: ONE type registry, the one Item already uses), appends new ones, and optionally streams. Streaming is two-way: appends go up, the tail comes down.
- **Composition:** it's a PROPERTY, `page.store`, `session.store`, `app.store`. It's not a base class, so no name clashes and clear responsibilities. Anything can have one.
- **Backends:** the dev socket (append and tail), localStorage (kept in memory, flushed on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` and rehydrated on load, for session-scoped things), memory, and later the cloud.
- **Proposed name: `Store`** (`obj.store`). Alternatives: `Journal` (append-only history), `Deltas`. The owner decides the name; the mechanism is settled.
- The `Log` sketch below stands as the mechanism, renamed.

edits.new:
## LATEST (the owner, 2026-10-01 16:25): persistence baked into Item, so Page has it
- **One `set(delta)`** for Item and Page, merged (the rule above): a method key calls the method, a settable value receives the nested delta, anything else is data and emits `change` (key, value, old). Events already exist on Item: `on`/`off`/`emit`, with `set` emitting `change` and events bubbling to the root. Page's set doesn't emit today; the merged one does.
- **Page extends Item,** so persistence is built in. **Anything that needs saving becomes a page** ("everything is a page").
- **Inside, it's still one part,** not a separate system: `Item.Store` (a static part, the house pattern) does load, replay, append and tail. Users never touch it (it's baked in), but a subclass can swap it (local storage, memory, cloud). That gives both halves: baked into the API, composed inside.
- **The saving strategy per child page:** embedded as lines in the parent's page.jsonl (the default), in its own file, or in its own folder. Chosen per child, and promoted automatically when it grows.
- The two sections below are superseded where they differ.

1. [fix] Servex/agents/Agents.js:419-421 (diff lines 419-421) — when no pool slot is ready, the minion is spawned anyway in the main tree ("writing in <cwd>"). The brief says plainly "main stays refused for minions", and that fallback lets the exact incident that started this task happen again whenever the pool is empty or still preparing. Refuse the spawn instead: throw a clear error ("no worktree ready — spawn a task-mastermind, or retry"). The test at spawn-worktree.test.mjs:511 then checks for the refusal instead of the fallback.
2. [note] Servex/Pool.js:379 `take_sync` — its comment calls the git call "BOUNDED", but `execFileSync("git", … merge --ff-only)` has no `timeout`, and it blocks the whole Servex event loop while it runs. Add `timeout: 15000`, as the other sync git calls should have.
3. [note] Server/owner-check.mjs:343-345 — if an older `owner-check.md` is already in the folder (from a second landing or a run by hand) and the new reviewer fails to write one, the script reads the old table back and logs it as fresh. Delete the file before `spawn_agent`.
4. [note] Server/owner-check.mjs:353 — the log line counts `items.length`, but done/partly/missing are counted from the reviewer's table rows. If the reviewer merges or skips rows, "N items" won't add up to D+P+M; count from `table.length`, or log the mismatch.
5. [note] Server/owner-check.mjs:244-249 — the extra "one item per `##` heading" tier is a deliberate departure from the brief's three tiers. It is explained in the doc and in the code, and it fits the real owner-words.md files, so I accept it. But a 6-heading file came back as 8 items in the proof (Server/doc/on-landing.md:88), because `###` sub-headings count as items too. Say so in the doc, or split on `##` only.
6. [note] The check that the brief asked for in "Proof" (`git diff --stat` of the task's merge) only works when the landing outcome contains the text "merge <sha>" (owner-check.mjs:272). Otherwise the reviewer gets no diff at all. That is acceptable as best-effort, but the doc should say a landing outcome without "merge <sha>" gets no diff.
7. [note] Everything else matches the brief. session-smart.md item 5 gains the sentence it asked for. on-landing.mjs wires the check in with one detached spawn plus the error line already used there. ## Lists, references, live updates, pub/sub (the owner, 2026-10-01 16:35)
- **List deltas use IDS + `after`, not indexes.** `add` / `set` / `move` / `remove` by id. Optional conflict guard: a line may carry `base` (the id of the last line its writer saw). If the file has moved on, replay still works because ids don't shift; `base` just flags a concurrent edit for review. That's the "commit hash" idea, used only as a check, never as the address.
- **Breaking a list out:** each item may live as lines in the parent (default), or `{"file": "k7/page.jsonl"}` (its own log). The list keeps only the id and order; the item's data moves. The same promotion as before.
- **The files index:** page.jsonl already gets `{"file": …}` lines from the dev server's watcher (keyed by the first path segment, Log.js). A node "create file" tool should write the line itself too, so the index never depends on a watcher being up.
- **References:** a saved reference is `{"$ref": "/framework/x/page#k7"}` (a path plus an optional id). After replay, a resolve pass swaps each `$ref` for the live object via `app.get(path)` and `find(id)`. Parent links are never saved: they're rebuilt by adoption, as Item does today.
- **Live updates today:** the dev server's `tail` RPC (Server/plugins/SocketServer/Tail.js) watches each subscribed .jsonl with chokidar, keeps a byte offset, and on a change pushes only the NEW lines to the subscribed sockets. Milliseconds, not seconds. The dictation chat doesn't use it yet (ext/Session polls), so moving it onto tail is part of "one system".
- **Pub/sub between pages:** a page PUBLISHES by appending to its own page.jsonl. To SUBSCRIBE, a page adds `{"subscribe": {"to": "/framework/x/"}}` to its own page.jsonl. At load it tails that page's log and routes the lines to a handler (an inbox, a feed). Tail already IS the per-file channel, so no new broker is needed.

# The fast path: from "fix this" to a live fix in seconds: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). **Owner: the Servex architect** (mastermind-servex-9), together with the dictation task (task-mastermind-one-dictation) for the voice end.

## Goal
The owner says, about the page or the selected item, "make this bold" or "this gap is too big". **The first fix is live in about 10–30 seconds,** for small changes of a few lines. Measure and log the time to the first fix.

## The path (node-led wherever possible, CLAUDE.md law 7)
1. **Voice → the smart assistant** knows the page and the selected element (the nav and selection events). It sends a SHORT refined request, or the verbatim one, straight to a…
2. **…warm quick-fixer:** a standing agent kept WARM (`dormant_after`: long) with the house rules loaded, plus an always-ready quick-fix worktree (the qf pool, kept synced with michael/dev). No spawn and no new worktree on the hot path.
3. **It edits, smoke-tests, and takes ONE screenshot** at the width that matters (the review skill's "pick widths by what changed"), checks the outcome, and **merges its own worktree** through `merge.mjs --quick` (a size threshold: few lines, one module, so a light review).
4. **The owner sees it live** (one reload, or the stream). The fixer posts one line in the chat with the screenshot, never chit-chat.
5. **If it's bigger than a quick fix** (more files, a layout, a new feature), the fixer says so and hands it to a task mastermind. It never stalls on the hot path.

## Related
- **Logs as rewind:** append-only logs with timestamps are a full playback of what happened; keep them. Purge only by snapshot and archive (page-item-design.md, "Speed"), never by deleting history.
- The streaming UI uses the one JSONL system (tail) for every change, so the page updates without a reload where possible.

# The fast path: from "fix this" to a live fix in seconds: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). **Driven by: the Servex architect** (mastermind-servex-9), together with the dictation task (task-mastermind-one-dictation) for the voice end.

## Goal
The owner says, about the page or the selected item, "make this bold" or "this gap is too big". **The first fix is live in about 10–30 seconds,** for small changes of a few lines. Measure and log the time to the first fix.

## The path (node-led wherever possible, CLAUDE.md law 7)
1. **Voice → the smart assistant** knows the page and the selected element (the nav and selection events). It sends a SHORT refined request, or the verbatim one, straight to a…
2. **…warm quick-fixer:** a standing agent kept WARM (`dormant_after`: long) with the house rules loaded, plus an always-ready quick-fix worktree (the qf pool, kept synced with michael/dev). No spawn and no new worktree on the hot path.
3. **It edits, smoke-tests, and takes ONE screenshot** at the width that matters (the review skill's "pick widths by what changed"), checks the outcome, and **merges its own worktree** through `merge.mjs --quick` (a size threshold: few lines, one module, so a light review).
4. **The owner sees it live** (one reload, or the stream). The fixer posts one line in the chat with the screenshot, never chit-chat.
5. **If it's bigger than a quick fix** (more files, a layout, a new feature), the fixer says so and hands it to a task mastermind. It never stalls on the hot path.

## Related
- **Logs as rewind:** append-only logs with timestamps are a full playback of what happened; keep them. Purge only by snapshot and archive (page-item-design.md, "Speed"), never by deleting history.
- The streaming UI uses the one JSONL system (tail) for every change, so the page updates without a reload where possible.

# Lists: how to store order and updates: options to compare

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). This is research plus small prototypes. Do NOT change the framework's real files.

## Read first (only these)
- `public/framework/ai/2026-09-30/proposal-flow/page-item-design.md`: the design so far (one `set(delta)`, page.jsonl lines, Item + List, the `saver`).
- `public/framework/core/List/List.js` and `core/Item/Item.js`: what exists.
- `public/framework/core/Page/Log.js`: how page.jsonl lines are replayed today.
- `public/framework/ext/Draggable/Sortable.js` and `public/framework/ux/Tree/` (the drag tree, `TreeDrag`): the drag-and-drop that will produce moves.

## The design requirements (draft; some are preferences, not rules)
1. **Append-only:** each change is ONE small line; the file is never rewritten. A move should be ONE line, not one per shifted item.
2. **Replay is fast and simple:** rebuilding the order shouldn't need walking a long chain.
3. **Few ids, little namespace overhead:** the owner dislikes "a lot of ids". If ids are needed, they should be cheap, local to the list, and automatic.
4. **Concurrent edits don't corrupt the order** (two tabs, or an agent and the owner).
5. **Works for page children too:** a page's sub-pages as a List, drag-and-drop in the tree UI, each child stored in the parent's file or broken out into its own.
6. **Live:** lines stream to other tabs (tail) and apply in place.

## Compare at least these, then recommend ONE (and give the runner-up)
- **A. Ids + `after`** (the current proposal): a linked order.
- **B. Fractional order keys:** each item has a sortable key (e.g. "a0", "a0V", "a1"); inserting between two items makes a key between theirs. One line per move, no renumbering, order = sort by key. The key can double as the item's identity in the list.
- **C. Indexes with a batched renumber:** an `order` line with the full list of ids or indexes after each change.
- **D. Anything better you know of** (CRDT-style list sequences…).

For each: the line format, the replay cost, a move, an insert, a delete, two concurrent moves, and how it meets requirements 1–6.

## Output
- `report.md`: one screen. A table of options × requirements, then the recommendation and the runner-up.
- `prototype/`: a tiny runnable node script per option (`node prototype/B.mjs`) that writes a .jsonl, replays it, and prints the order after a scripted series of insert, move, delete and two concurrent moves. Use plain node, no npm packages.
- Log one line to this task's `task.jsonl` through `node .claude/hooks/append.mjs` when done.

# Minion brief: the three core voice bugs (the owner's 20:41–20:44 test)

Load the `minion` skill first. Your parent is **task-mastermind-one-dictation**. Work only in your served worktree, `C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/dictate-core`, which has its own server (the port is in `.worktrees.json` in the main repo, under `dictate-core`). These three bugs come first; nothing else goes in this merge.

**The evidence** is the owner's own session, read it first: `public/framework/ai/2026/10/01/remote-access-install-tailscale-on-pc-an/ai/v-pl3m2ih.jsonl` (68 lines). The owner was on a phone (host `10.0.0.135:8137`), mostly on `/framework/ux/Dictate/` with the ✦ sheet open.

## 1. No assistant replies (the smart assistant went silent for 8 minutes)
**What happened:** the smart assistant answered at 20:40:16 and 20:40:42. From 20:41:13 it spent ONE turn of 8 minutes (its transcript is `C:/Users/mike/.claude/projects/C--Code-lew42-monorepo/b58e7543-c665-44a6-8932-1b6bce68947f.jsonl`). It called `list_agents` (1.8 million characters, over the limit), grepped, then fought `dir_log`'s format twice. Its reply landed at 20:49:28. Everything the owner said in between waited behind it.
**The cause** is `Servex/agents/session-smart.md` rule 1: "Before you start any work, look at what is already running: the Servex tool `list_agents`…".
**Do:**
- Rewrite rule 1 so the smart assistant **answers first**: its reply to the owner is the first thing in every turn. It looks up in-flight work only when the owner's words are about work, and then from a small source (`public/framework/ai/asks.jsonl`'s last lines, or the newest `task.jsonl` line 1s), **never `list_agents`**.
- Give `dir_log` the right shape in the prompt (its error said "a log.jsonl line is ONE of session, task, decision"; the call that worked used `line: {decision: {...}}`), so it never takes three tries.
- Keep it short; the file is a prompt, so every line costs time.
**Prove:** quote the changed lines in your report. Prompt changes reach only NEW sessions; say so. Don't restart Servex.

## 2. "PAR" shown as a bubble
**What happened:** the fast assistant's new-paragraph marker is written as an invisible `{"para": {at, re}}` line (`Servex/agents/Sessions.js` around line 815). `ext/Session/Session.js`'s `entry()` passes it through as `{type: "para"}`, and `ux/Dictate/Widget.js`'s `Thread.draw()` splits a bubble on it. The owner still saw a bubble reading just "PAR".
**Do:** find the surface that draws it. Candidates: the ✦ sheet, the ☰ drawer's AI tab, a card's own chat on its `/framework/ai2/…` page, `ext/Chat/Chat.js`'s `draw()`, and `split_paragraph()` leaving an empty or label-only bubble behind. Fix it in the one shared place, so `para` never draws on any surface.
**Prove:** replay this exact session file, headless, through a stubbed Servex stream (see the scratchpad pattern below). Shoot the ✦ sheet at 400×800. No "PAR" or "para" text appears anywhere in the DOM.

## 3. The owner's lines DUPLICATED ("All right, I'm just gonna keep talking…" ×3)

# Line art: an image filter that scores how "line-like" every pixel is: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md), and the idea is in the blog post [/blog/ai/lines-to-3d/](/blog/ai/lines-to-3d/). Build a working filter page; no 3D yet.

## What it does
Input: any image (drop a file, or pick a sample). Output: a mostly WHITE grayscale image where each pixel is DARKER the more confident it is part of a LINE. That's line art.

## The score (the owner's three ingredients)
1. **Change, in every channel:** for each pixel, the derivative to its neighbours in hue (circular), saturation and brightness. Combine them, so a whisper-faint wall seam still registers.
2. **Direction:** use the gradient's ORIENTATION, not just its size. The standard tool is the **structure tensor**: average the gradient outer products over a small window. Its eigenvalues give a **coherence** of (λ1−λ2)/(λ1+λ2): near 1 where neighbours agree on one direction (a line or edge), near 0 for noise or texture.
3. **Consistency along the line (length and signal strength):** reward a response that keeps going in its own direction. Integrate the coherent response along the edge direction for some distance, which also suppresses short flickers. Normalise by the local noise level, so a faint but STEADY seam beats a loud random speckle.

Line confidence = coherence × consistency-along-the-line × (gradient size relative to local noise). Map it to darkness, with a gamma slider.

## The page: /imagine/lines/
- The original and the line art side by side (stacked on mobile).
- A few sliders: window size, line length, noise floor, gamma. Live updates on a canvas.
- 3 or 4 samples: a synthetic box or room drawn on a canvas (known answer: 8 corners, 12 edges), plus 1 or 2 real photos (find any photo already in the repo, or the owner drops one).
- **Plain JS on canvas** (ImageData), no npm packages. Keep the core a pure function, `lines(imageData, opts) → Float32Array`, in its own file, so it can run in node later for batch work.

# inspect(): every object and class as a card, and Dictate as a live system diagram: requirements

The owner's words are verbatim in [owner-words.md](owner-words.md). A big task, in two parts. Part 1 first.

## Part 1: `inspect()`, the house pattern for seeing any object
- **Build on what exists, don't duplicate (law 6):** `ux/Content/Object`:
  - `object()` gives one card: the class name, `name = value` per property, and the method names;
  - `view()` / `DefaultView.js` gives a lazy tree of ui/item rows;
  - a class can override it with `Thing.View`.
- **`static icon = "…"`** on a class: the name of its icon (the icon system). An instance shows its class's icon.
- **`instance.inspect()` and `Class.inspect()`:** a render method kept SEPARATE from `render()`. `render()` stays free for the object's real template; `inspect()` is the debug and inspector view, available on every object even without a render method. It captures markup like any factory.
  - **An instance card:** icon, instance name, class name, the key properties (configurable), and arrays as nested cards. It works recursively: a property's value inspects itself.
  - **A class card:** the SAME icon in a more substantial frame (bigger, "a class definition"), listing properties and methods with the core API first, each as a nested card. It's the visual form of the readme's `## Architecture` block.
  - Variants: `minimal` (icon + names, like an Inbox context card), `card` (the default), `full`. Name them well; the owner expects some sculpting.
- **One view or many:** keep one default (`Thing.View`). Multiple live views are possible, but note the update cost (you have to loop the views). Recommend, and record the alternative.
- **Document it in the code system** (/framework/code/patterns: "render vs inspect"; parts as statics; `static icon`). A class's doc page opens with its class card.

## Part 2: the Dictate PLAYGROUND as a full-bleed, live system diagram (3440-friendly)
- The playground tab goes **full bleed**, using a 2D layout (columns and rows) that fills a widescreen.
- **Every object a dictation session creates is a real object with an icon,** shown with `inspect()` and updating live as you talk:
  1. the audio source (mic, levels);
  2. the segments;
  3. the RAW transcriptions;
  4. the CLEAN ones;
  5. the prompt analysis (investigation and planning, a coming phase);
  6. the chat messages, replies and reactions;
  7. the session and its files (what's written where: the JSONL lines as they land).

  If something is a plain string or blob today and should be an object, make it one.
- **Like a log: immutable.** Nothing is overwritten. A raw transcription stays visible after its clean version arrives. No jumping: new things append, and the view never reorders under you.
- **Layout:** source → raw → clean → analysis → chat as columns (or a table) on desktop, with the session's objects as a structure panel. On mobile, a stack with tabs is fine (the existing tabs).

## Rules
- Coordinate with task-mastermind-one-dictation, which owns the dictation widget and is fixing its core bugs. Part 2 builds the DIAGRAM around their widget, not a second widget.
- A Sonnet task mastermind with at most 2 Sonnet minions, in a pool worktree, through merge.mjs. Screenshots at 1920 and 3440 (it's a layout), plus 400 for the inspect cards.
- Land Part 1 first, then Part 2.
